stem: What is the oldest version of Windows covered on the CompTIA A+ 220-1102 exam?
explanation: Windows 10 is the oldest version of Windows covered on the CompTIA A+ 220-1102 exam. Older versions such as Windows 8 are past their vendor support life and are no longer on the objectives.
whyWrong: Windows Server 2016 is a server OS, not a client edition covered by the A+ OS objectives.
Windows 8 reached the end of its support life and is no longer covered by the exam objectives.
Windows 11 is covered, but it is newer than Windows 10, so it is not the oldest version.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 1
note: 220-1102 1.1; the 220-1202 exam also starts at Windows 10, mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (workstation OSs, vendor life-cycle limitations).

stem: The Linux operating system comes in hundreds of different versions, known as _______.
explanation: Different versions of Linux are known as distros, short for distributions. Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian are examples of distros, each built on the Linux kernel.
whyWrong: Desktops are the graphical work areas of an OS, not the versions of Linux.
Dispersions is not a term used for versions of Linux.
Domiciles is not a term used for versions of Linux.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 4

stem: The user, Mike, has downloaded files with his Web browser. Where will they be stored by default?
explanation: The default download location in Windows is C:\Users\<user name>\Downloads. Each user profile under C:\Users holds folders such as Desktop, Documents, and Downloads.
whyWrong: Windows does not create a Downloads folder at the root of the C: drive.
User folders are kept under C:\Users, not in a folder named after the user at the root of C:.
The Downloads folder sits next to the Desktop folder in the user profile, not inside it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 1.1; user profile folders are not a separate 220-1202 topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (workstation OSs: Windows).

stem: Both Apple and Android smartphones have a utility called ______.
explanation: Both Apple and Android smartphones have a utility called Settings. The Settings app holds the device options such as Wi-Fi, accounts, and privacy on both mobile OSs.
whyWrong: Neither iOS nor Android has a configuration utility named Control.
Neither iOS nor Android has a utility named Command Center.
Control Center is an iOS quick-settings panel, but it is not the shared name used on both platforms.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (mobile OSs: iOS and Android).

stem: Which is the most complete list of file systems Windows can use?
explanation: Modern versions of Windows can use FAT32 and NTFS for hard drives, and exFAT for removable flash-media drives. NTFS adds security and journaling, and exFAT works well on large flash drives.
whyWrong: This list leaves out exFAT, which Windows uses for removable flash media.
This list leaves out NTFS and exFAT, which Windows also uses.
This list leaves out FAT32 and exFAT, which Windows also uses.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 1
note: 220-1102 1.8; the 220-1202 list also names ReFS, mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (filesystem types).

stem: Which of the following correctly identifies the four possible entries in a file allocation table?
options: Number of the starting cluster, number of the ending cluster, number of used clusters, number of available clusters
An end-of-file marker, a bad-block marker, code indicating the cluster is available, the number of the cluster where the next part of the file is stored
Filename, folder location, starting cluster number, ending cluster number
explanation: The four possible entries in a file allocation table are an end-of-file marker, a bad-block marker, code indicating the cluster is available, and the number of the cluster where the next part of the file is stored. The table works as a chain map that tells the file system where each next piece of a file is.
whyWrong: Filename, date, time, and size are kept in the folder entry, not in the file allocation table.
The table does not count starting, ending, used, and available clusters.
Filenames and folder locations are kept in the folder entry, not in the table.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 2
note: 220-1101 3.3; FAT internals are not on 220-1202, mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (filesystem types: FAT32).

stem: Which mobile OS enables device manufacturers to customize it to better suit their specific devices?
explanation: Google Android is open source, enabling manufacturers to make modifications to better suit their specific devices. Apple alone makes the devices that run iOS and iPadOS.
whyWrong: BlackBerry OS was a closed system and is no longer made.
iOS is closed source and runs only on Apple iPhones.
iPadOS is closed source and runs only on Apple iPads.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 24: Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 10

stem: Which part of the operating system can be described as extremely specific software written for the purpose of instructing the OS on how to access a piece of hardware?
explanation: A driver is specifically written to instruct the operating system to communicate with a piece of hardware. Source code is the original code the software is written in. An application is a program written to perform a specific purpose to interact with the user. The kernel is the core of the operating system.
whyWrong: Source code is the original program text that software is written in, not hardware instructions for the OS.
An application performs a task for the user; it does not tell the OS how to reach hardware.
The kernel is the core of the OS that manages resources; device-specific instructions come from drivers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 2

stem: The Windows File Explorer program can be used to do which of the following? (Choose two.)
explanation: The Windows File Explorer program can be used to copy and move files. Windows File Explorer can also be used to change file attributes. Windows File Explorer cannot be used to browse the Internet or to create backup jobs.
whyWrong: File Explorer manages local files and folders; a web browser is used to browse the Internet.
File Explorer does not create backup jobs; backup tools such as File History do that.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 5

stem: What is the maximum allowable length for the name of a file in Windows?
explanation: The maximum allowable length for a filename is 255 characters. Older MS-DOS systems limited names to eight characters plus a three-character extension, but NTFS and current Windows allow much longer names.
whyWrong: Eight characters was the old 8.3 filename limit of MS-DOS and FAT, not the limit in current Windows.
Thirty-two characters is far below the filename length that NTFS and current Windows allow.
Sixty-four characters is too short; current Windows allows filenames of up to 255 characters.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 6

stem: Which of the following is a program that runs on top of the OS and allows the user to issue commands through a set of menus or some other graphical interface?
explanation: The shell is a program that runs on top of the OS and allows user interaction with the operating system. The Taskbar is an element of the Desktop. The Desktop does not allow for commands to be executed. Source is not related to the graphical interface.
whyWrong: The Taskbar is one element of the desktop, not the program that interprets user commands.
The Desktop is the workspace on the screen; it does not itself carry out user commands.
Source is not part of the graphical interface and does not accept commands from the user.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 7

stem: If a program doesn't have a shortcut on the Desktop or in the All Apps submenu, you can start it by which of the following methods? (Choose the BEST answer.)
options: Typing the program name in the Start box
Using the run command and typing in the name of the program
Typing cmd in the Start box followed by the program name
explanation: Typing the program name in the Start box allows you to launch the program. The Shut Down command will shut down the operating system. Run is not a command; it is a dialog. The cmd command starts the command-prompt application.
whyWrong: The Shut Down command turns off the operating system; it does not start a program.
Run is a dialog box, not a command, and this is not the simplest way to start a program.
Typing cmd opens the command prompt; adding a program name in the Start box does not launch that program.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 8

stem: Which operating system feature offers the ability for a single application to have multiple requests into the processor at one time?
explanation: When a program is multithreaded, it is written to allow for multiple requests into the processor at one time. Multiuser mode, dystopia, and preemption are not correct answers.
whyWrong: Multiuser mode lets several users share a system; it does not split one application into threads.
Dystopia is not an operating system feature at all.
Preemption lets the OS interrupt a task to run another; it does not give one application multiple requests at once.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 9

stem: In Windows, a deleted file can be retrieved using which of the following?
explanation: The Recycle Bin is a temporary spot that files are deleted to but from where they can be retrieved if deleted mistakenly. The My Computer icon is another older way to start the File Explorer. Control Panel and the Settings app are used to customize the operating system.
whyWrong: The My Computer icon is an older way to open File Explorer; it does not hold deleted files.
Control Panel customizes the operating system; it cannot restore a deleted file.
The Settings app customizes Windows; deleted files are kept in the Recycle Bin instead.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 10

stem: To turn off a Windows 11 operating system gracefully, you should do which of the following?
options: Run the turnoff command at a command prompt.
Turn off the switch and unplug the machine.
Select Start, then click the power icon, and then choose Shut Down.
explanation: In Windows 11, when you click the Start button, a power icon is displayed on the lower left. From the power icon, you can sleep, reboot, or shut down the operating system. There is no command named turnoff. Turning the power switch off and unplugging the machine are not graceful ways to power off the operating system. Pressing Ctrl+Alt+Del alone will not power down the computer.
whyWrong: Windows has no turnoff command, so this cannot shut the system down.
Cutting the power is not graceful; open files and settings may be lost or damaged.
Ctrl+Alt+Del opens a security screen with options; on its own it does not shut down the system gracefully.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 11

stem: In Windows, a quick way to access Help is to press which keyboard key?
options: The Windows key on the keyboard
explanation: A quick method of accessing Help is to press the F1 key. The Windows key on the keyboard launches the Start menu. The F12 key and the Alt key perform various tasks, depending on the application.
whyWrong: F12 performs different tasks depending on the application; it is not the standard Help key.
The Windows key opens the Start menu, not Help.
The Alt key shows menus or shortcuts in applications; it does not open Help.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 15

stem: Which key(s) will open a run box?
explanation: The Windows key+R will open a run box, where you can launch applications by typing in their executable name. Ctrl+R is used to reload web pages in web browsers. The Windows key alone will launch the Start menu. The F1 key will launch help in applications and on the desktop it will launch a web browser.
whyWrong: Ctrl+R reloads a page in web browsers; it does not open the Run box.
The Windows key alone opens the Start menu, not the Run box.
F1 opens Help, not the Run box.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 16

stem: Which of the following is located on the rightmost portion of the Taskbar?
explanation: The notification area is the area on the rightmost portion of the Taskbar. It is used to display the date and time and running background applications. The pinned apps and Start menus are located on the center-left portion of the Taskbar. Shutdown options are found inside the Start menu in Windows 11.
whyWrong: The Start menu button sits at the left or center of the Taskbar, not the rightmost part.
Pinned apps sit at the center or left of the Taskbar, not at its right end.
Shutdown options are inside the Start menu, not on the right side of the Taskbar.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which of the following allows you to navigate file/folder structures in Windows?
explanation: The File Explorer allows you to navigate the file/folder structure in Windows 11. The Start menu allows you to launch applications. KDE and GNOME are Linux desktop shells.
whyWrong: The Start menu launches applications; it is not used to browse folders.
KDE is a Linux desktop environment, not a Windows file navigation tool.
GNOME is a Linux desktop environment, not a Windows file navigation tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 19

stem: You need to select a format for a flash drive that is compatible with other operating systems. Which of the following is the filesystem should you choose?
explanation: FAT32 is a filesystem that was popular with Windows 9x operating systems and is also commonly used for USB flash drives for compatibility between platforms. NTFS is the native filesystem for Windows. EFS is a technology that encrypts files. The CDFS filesystem is used for CD media.
whyWrong: NTFS is the native Windows file system and is not fully supported by every other operating system.
EFS encrypts files on NTFS; it is not a file system for formatting a drive.
CDFS is the file system for CD media, not for flash drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 2

stem: Which of the following filesystems is a proprietary filesystem created by Microsoft for use with large flash drives?
explanation: The exFAT filesystem is a Microsoft proprietary filesystem created for large flash drives. GPT is a partition table type, NFS is a network filesystem used with Linux/UNIX, and ext3 is a filesystem used with Linux.
whyWrong: GPT is a partition table style, not a file system for flash drives.
NFS is a network file system used with Linux and UNIX, not a Microsoft flash drive format.
The ext3 file system is used with Linux, not created by Microsoft for flash drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 5

stem: Which of the following filesystems is a proprietary filesystem created by Apple that offers SSD support?
explanation: The Apple File System (APFS) is a proprietary filesystem created for SSD support; it can be found on macOS Sierra 10.12.4, iOS 10.3, and tvOS 10.2 and later operating systems. Hierarchical File System (HFS) is a proprietary filesystem that was developed by Apple for the Mac OS back in 1985, ext4 (Fourth Extended File System) is used with Android and other Linux-based operating systems, and exFAT is a Microsoft proprietary filesystem created for large flash drives.
whyWrong: HFS is the older Apple file system from 1985 and was not designed for SSDs.
The ext4 file system is a Linux file system, not an Apple one.
The exFAT file system was created by Microsoft for flash drives, not by Apple.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 7

stem: Your iPad has an application that will not stop running. What feature/tool can you use to stop it?
explanation: By pressing the Home button twice on an iPad, you can Force Quit an application that will not stop running. The kill utility can be used only at the command line of Linux/macOS. The Task Manager is a Windows utility. Close Quit is not a feature and therefore a wrong answer.
whyWrong: The kill command works only at a Linux or macOS command line, not on an iPad.
Task Manager is a Windows utility and is not available on an iPad.
Close Quit is not a real feature on Apple devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 12
note: Force Quit on an iPad (iPadOS); mapped to 1.8 Force Quit with 1.1 mobile OSs.

stem: Which of the following operating systems is a free download with no evaluation period limitations?
explanation: Ubuntu Linux (regardless of the version) is a free download. While you can download some versions of Windows, they are only for evaluation periods of time. Apple-based operating systems, such as macOS and iOS, are not free downloads.
whyWrong: Windows is a paid product; its free downloads are evaluation copies that expire after a set period.
macOS is proprietary Apple software and is not offered as a free download for any computer.
iOS is a closed Apple mobile OS that comes only on Apple phones and is not a free download.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 29: Common Operating Systems, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: According to the CompTIA A+ objectives, which of these are not mobile operating systems (OSs)? (Select three.)
explanation: Windows, Chrome OS, and Linux are not mobile operating systems. Android and iPadOS are used in tablets. You will see iOS in Apple phones as well. Windows, Chrome OS, and Linux are commonly found in laptops and listed in the CompTIA objectives as workstation operating systems (OSs), but for the purposes of the exam, mobile includes tablets and phones.
whyWrong: Android is a mobile OS used on many phones and tablets, so it is a mobile operating system.
iPadOS is the Apple operating system for iPad tablets, so it counts as a mobile operating system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 29: Common Operating Systems, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: All operating systems have an end-of-life date.
Linux distros cost money to distribute.
Android is an example of closed-source software.
Chrome OS is designed by Apple to use mostly desktop applications.
explanation: Every operating system has an end-of-life date. Linux is free to distribute, so this statement is not true. Some distributors may charge for service and support. Android is technically open source, so this statement is not true. Chrome OS is written by Google, not Apple, and relies on the user using the Chrome browser for mostly web-based applications, so this statement is not true.
whyWrong: Linux distributions are free to distribute; some vendors charge only for service and support.
Android is built on open-source code, so it is not an example of closed-source software.
ChromeOS is made by Google, not Apple, and runs mostly web-based apps in the Chrome browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 29: Common Operating Systems, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following does macOS use that works in a similar fashion to Linux-based file systems?
explanation: Apple uses the Apple File System (APFS) on macOS and some other Apple-based devices. It works in a similar fashion to Linux-based file systems. End-of-life (EOL) is the discontinuation of updates and the ending of support for software/hardware. ext4 is the Fourth Extended file system in Linux. exFAT is the successor to FAT32 in Windows, it can handle large file sizes and can format media larger than 32 GB.
whyWrong: EOL means end-of-life, the end of updates and support for a product; it is not a file system.
ext4 is the Linux file system itself, not the macOS file system that works like it.
exFAT is a Microsoft file system for large removable media, not the native macOS file system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 29: Common Operating Systems, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following are considered closed-source proprietary operating systems? (Select three.)
explanation: Closed-source software like Windows, macOS, and iOS are restricted and proprietary. Open-source software and code like Linux and Android are available to the public.
whyWrong: Android is open-source software based on Linux, so it is not a closed-source proprietary OS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 29: Common Operating Systems, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: One of your customers is trying to install a 3 TB storage drive to a Linux system. The customer wishes to use half of the drive capacity for one partition now and wants to have the option to increase the partition size later. Which file system should you recommend?
explanation: Recommend ext4. It is the default on most Linux systems, and it has the ability to be resized at a later date. NTFS is a Windows file system, and it doesn’t function well with Linux, though it does allow for dynamic resizing of disks in Windows. FAT32 can be used in Linux, and it works well for drives that need to be accessed by Linux and Windows systems, but it doesn’t allow for resizing. APFS is the Apple File System, and it works only on macOS.
whyWrong: NTFS is a Windows file system and does not work well as the main file system on Linux.
FAT32 can be read by Linux and Windows, but it cannot be resized later.
APFS is the Apple File System and works only on macOS, not on Linux.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: An engineer needs to format a USB storage device in preparation to copy 20GB of data from an Ubuntu Linux server to a Windows system. Which of the following filesystems will the engineer MOST LIKELY use?
explanation: The technician must find a filesystem compatible with both operating systems. exFAT is the successor to FAT32, handles files larger than 4 GB, and is supported natively by Windows, macOS, and Linux kernel 5.4 and later. That makes it the usual choice for a USB drive that moves large amounts of data between Linux and Windows.
whyWrong: FAT32 works on both systems, but it cannot store any single file larger than 4 GB.
ext4 is a Linux file system that Windows cannot read natively.
NTFS is the Windows file system and has limited write support on some Linux systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.8 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.8; mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (OS types). Book answer A (FAT32) corrected: FAT32 cannot store files over 4 GB, and exFAT is supported by Linux kernel 5.4 and later, so the current books name exFAT as the best choice for USB drives (Exam Cram 2e, Chapters 15 and 29).

stem: A recent risk assessment has highlighted a security issue, wherein legacy equipment has a 32-bit edition of Windows XP as its embedded OS. The company does not receive any quality or security updates for this operating system. What term would BEST describe this operating system?
explanation: An End of Life (EOL) operating system no longer receives updates or security patches from the vendor. The issue is not an incompatible operating system as it still works on the hardware platform. The issue raised here is more about security and reliability issues; the fact that it is a 32-bit OS is not significant. A vendor may offer extended support for important customers (usually requiring the customer to pay for this extended support). In this instance, extended support is not being offered.
whyWrong: The OS still runs on its hardware, so the issue is not incompatibility.
Being 32-bit is not the problem; the lack of updates is.
The vendor no longer supports this OS with updates, so it is not vendor-supported.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.8 question 2

stem: A school is looking to invest in easy-to-support technology for student workstations. The chosen devices will run a lightweight operating system based on a browser interface. What would be the BEST choice to meet these requirements?
explanation: ChromeOS is a lightweight OS based on the popular Chrome browser. There are many examples of versions of minimalist OSs, such as Windows IoT and Linux Lite, while Apple is rumored to be testing a Lite version of macOS for iPads. None of these are based on a browser-based interface, however.
whyWrong: Linux distributions are not built around a browser interface.
macOS is a full desktop OS, not a lightweight browser-based one.
Windows is a full desktop OS, not a lightweight browser-based one.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.8 question 3

stem: After installing the most recent version of Red Hat Linux on a datacenter server, additional storage is added. The new hard drive must be formatted with a filesystem that supports 40TB of storage, and it is also anticipated that the storage will need to be regularly defragmented. Which of the following is the BEST choice of filesystem?
explanation: ext2 was followed by ext3 in 2001, which supported a maximum partition size of 16TB. ext4 was introduced around 2008 and supports a maximum partition size of 1EB (1,000,000 TB). The ext4 filesystem also supports online defragmentation, which is important to maintain efficient file access. FAT32 is not used as a core filesystem on Linux. NTFS is a Windows filesystem.
whyWrong: FAT32 is meant for removable media and cannot hold a 40TB volume.
ext3 supports volumes up to 16TB and has no online defragmentation.
NTFS is a Windows file system and is not the native choice for Linux.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.8 question 5

stem: A marketing company is looking to deploy smartphones to their workforce. The smartphone must support an operating system based on Linux, as developers will create applications for the company and have experience with Linux operating systems. Which of the following Os’s would be the BEST choice for this?
explanation: Android is an open source (that is, royalty free) operating system developed by Google. It was initially released in 2008 and, in 2023, is currently on version 13 (codename Tiramisu). Android OS is based on a Linux kernel and supports many of the security features used in mainstream Linux distributions. iOS is a proprietary Apple-based mobile operating system originally used exclusively on Apple hardware, specifically the code base for iPhones, iPods, and iPads. SUSE Linux is not used on mobile devices or smartphones; it is primarily deployed on datacenter servers.
whyWrong: iOS is a proprietary Apple OS and is not based on Linux.
SUSE Linux is a server distribution and is not used on smartphones.
Windows Mobile is based on Windows and has been discontinued.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.8 question 6

stem: macOS is based upon what source code?
explanation: The Mac operating system (beginning with Mac OS X in 1996) was developed as a custom operating system based on Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD) Unix. macOS is not based on Linux, Android, or ChromeOS. This Unix base is why many Linux commands also work in the macOS Terminal.
whyWrong: macOS is not built on Linux; both are Unix-like but share no code base.
Android is a mobile OS built on Linux, not the base of macOS.
ChromeOS is Google's browser-based OS, not the base of macOS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.10; mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (workstation OSs)

stem: A department would like their Windows 10-based workstations to be able to access shared files on an Ubuntu Linux server using mapped drives. What service would allow for this functionality?
options: Install the telnet service on the Ubuntu server
Install the samba service on the Windows 10 workstations
Install Windows File and Print Sharing on the Ubuntu server
Install samba service on the Ubuntu server
explanation: Installing the samba service on the Linux Ubuntu server will allow Windows computers to use native services and applications to access files and printers on the Linux server in the same way that they connect to other Windows computers. Windows uses a Microsoft protocol called Server Message Block (SMB), also known as Common Internet File System (CIFS) to access shared content across a network. samba supports the same protocols. telnet is used to access the CLI of a remote system but does not allow files to be transferred between systems. Windows File and Print Sharing is native to Windows operating systems and cannot be installed on Linux systems.
whyWrong: Telnet gives remote command-line access and does not share files with Windows.
Windows already speaks SMB natively, so Samba is not needed on the workstations.
Windows File and Print Sharing is part of Windows and cannot be installed on Linux.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.11 (Samba); Samba is not named in 220-1202, mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (compatibility concerns between operating systems)

stem: A publishing company supports a mixed desktop environment, containing many older versions of the Microsoft Windows OS. In order to ensure the compatibility of removable media, which of the following filesystem formats would be the BEST choice?
explanation: The FAT32 filesystem format would be the best choice for ensuring the read and write compatibility of USB flash drives across several generations of Microsoft operating systems. FAT32 is a widely supported filesystem that can be accessed by various operating systems, including older versions of Windows, macOS, and Linux. It offers excellent compatibility and allows easy file sharing between different platforms.
whyWrong: APFS is the Apple File System for macOS and is not readable by older versions of Windows.
ext4 is a Linux file system that older versions of Windows cannot read without extra software.
CDFS is a read-only file system for optical discs and is not suitable for writable removable media.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 60
note: 220-1102 1.8 (OS types: file systems); mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (Various filesystem types).

stem: A software development company would like to support a hybrid OS environment. How can they easily access shared filesystems and printers between Windows and Linux systems?
explanation: Samba is an open source software suite that provides interoperability between Linux/Unix-based systems and Windows-based systems. It allows Linux servers and desktops to join Windows Active Directory domains, enabling seamless integration and sharing of resources such as file and print services.
whyWrong: yum installs, upgrades, and removes Linux software packages; it does not share files with Windows.
CIFS is the Windows file-sharing protocol, but Samba is the software that lets Linux share files and printers with Windows.
chmod sets file permissions on Linux and does not share files or printers with Windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 73
note: 220-1102 1.11 (Linux: Samba); mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (Compatibility concerns between operating systems). Samba is not listed in the 220-1202 objectives.

stem: What is the term used to indicate that a vendor no longer supports a product, including the discontinuation of patches and updates?
explanation: The correct term used to indicate that a vendor no longer supports a product, including the discontinuation of patches and updates, is end of life (EOL). When a product reaches its EOL, the vendor ceases to provide further support, leaving users without access to patches, updates, or technical assistance. This indicates that the product is no longer actively maintained or developed.
whyWrong: An AUP is an acceptable use policy that sets rules for using a service, not a term for the end of support.
A EULA is the license contract for software use, not a term for the end of vendor support.
UAC is the Windows User Account Control feature, not a term for the end of vendor support.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 81
note: 220-1102 1.8 (vendor life-cycle limitations); mapped to 220-1202 1.1 (Vendor life-cycle limitations: EOL).

stem: Which of the following partitioning schemes enable the creation of more than four partitions or volumes on a single hard drive? (Select two.)
explanation: Both GPT and dynamic disk partitioning schemes enable the creation of more than four partitions or volumes on a single hard drive. GPT supports up to 128 partitions in Windows, and dynamic disks hold many volumes.
whyWrong: MBR allows only four primary partitions on one drive.
The MFT is the NTFS master file table, not a partitioning scheme.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 9
note: 220-1102 1.8; dynamic disks are not on 220-1202, mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (partitioning: GPT, MBR).

stem: Michael’s hard drive is causing an installation lockup. What should he check FIRST to view specific installation steps and track errors?
explanation: Because optical drives and hard drives can cause installation lockups, Michael should first check the setup log files to examine specific installation steps and track errors. Windows Setup writes these logs, such as setupact.log and setuperr.log, during the installation.
whyWrong: A patch fixes a known problem; it does not record the steps of an installation.
A recovery partition holds a factory image; it does not record installation errors.
A service pack is a collection of updates; it does not record installation errors.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 2
note: 220-1102 1.9; installation errors are not a listed topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (types of installations).

stem: What tool enables installing Windows over a network?
options: Windows can’t be installed over a network.
explanation: The Preboot Execution Environment, or PXE, enables installation of Windows over a network. The PC boots from its network card and loads the setup files from a deployment server.
whyWrong: A Windows DVD is local optical media, not a network boot method.
NetBoot is the Apple macOS network boot feature, not the standard tool for Windows.
Windows can be installed over a network with PXE and a deployment server.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 5

stem: When you install an operating system alongside an existing operating system, what do you create?
explanation: An OS added to an existing OS creates a multiboot system. At startup a boot menu lets the user choose which OS to load.
whyWrong: A clean install replaces the existing OS instead of installing beside it.
An upgrade installation replaces the existing OS with a newer version and keeps the data.
A network installation describes where the setup files come from, not two operating systems side by side.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 6

stem: If Windows locks up during the installation, what should you do?
options: Press ctrl-alt-del to restart the installation process.
Push the Reset button to restart the installation process.
Press the esc key to cancel the installation process.
Unplug the computer and restart the installation process.
explanation: If Windows locks up during the installation, you should unplug the computer and restart the installation process. Removing power fully resets the hardware before the installation starts again.
whyWrong: During setup, ctrl-alt-del does not restart a locked-up installation.
The book recommends removing power fully rather than using the Reset button.
The esc key does not cancel a Windows installation that has locked up.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 8
note: 220-1102 1.9; installation lockups are not a listed topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (types of installations).

stem: Which term describes the process of getting the latest version of your operating system?
explanation: An update is used to get the latest version of your operating system, including fixes for bugs and security flaws. Windows also delivers feature updates that add new functions to the operating system.
whyWrong: A hot fix is a single fix for one specific problem, not the process of getting the latest OS version.
Hot pack is not a standard term for updating an operating system.
Service release is not the term Windows uses for getting the latest OS version.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 9
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (feature updates).

stem: Which tool is handy for large-scale Windows OS deployments that have to be run in a Windows Server Active Directory domain and need to migrate many users?
explanation: The USMT is the go-to tool for large-scale Windows operating system deployments (such as large businesses) that have to be run in a Windows Server Active Directory domain and need to migrate many users. It copies user files and settings from the old installation and restores them on the new one.
whyWrong: BitLocker encrypts drives; it does not migrate user settings during deployments.
RDP gives remote control of a computer; it does not migrate users.
PXE boots a computer from the network to install an OS, but it does not move user data.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (upgrade considerations: backup files and user preferences). Typos in the book explanation (UMST, domin) fixed.

stem: Which of the following partitions is specifically the partition from which the operating system boots?
explanation: The operating system must boot from an active primary partition if MBR style partitioning is used. Extended partitions are used to contain logical partitions. There is no such thing as a dynamic partition.
whyWrong: An extended partition only holds logical partitions; the OS cannot boot from it directly.
There is no such thing as a dynamic partition; dynamic disks hold volumes instead.
A logical partition sits inside an extended partition and is not the MBR boot partition.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 15

stem: Which of the following replaces the MBR in 64-bit versions of the Windows operating system?
explanation: GUID [globally unique identifier] Partition Table (GPT) allocates a 64-bit logical block addressing entry to partition tables to accommodate larger drives. GPT has rapidly replaced the MBR-style partition tables. LILO and GRUB are boot managers for Linux. NFS is a network filesystem used with Linux/UNIX operating systems.
whyWrong: LILO is a Linux boot loader, not a partition table style.
NFS is a network file system used with Linux and UNIX, not a partition table style.
GRUB is a Linux boot loader, not a replacement for the MBR partition table.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which partition style allows up to 2,000 volumes to be partitioned on a physical disk?
explanation: The Dynamic Disk partition style allows up to 2,000 volumes to be created on a physical disk. GUID [globally unique identifier] Partition Table (GPT) allow up to 128 volumes to be created on a physical disk. The Master Boot Record (MBR) and Basic Disk partitioning scheme are one and the same and allow up to 26 partitions to be created on a physical disk.
whyWrong: GPT allows up to 128 partitions on a disk in Windows, not 2,000 volumes.
MBR allows only four primary partitions, or three plus one extended partition.
A basic disk uses MBR or GPT partitions and does not allow 2,000 volumes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 20

stem: What is the name of the pass that detects hardware and installs drivers?
explanation: The Generalize pass is where the operating system detects hardware and installs the appropriate drivers. The Out-Of-Box Experience (OOBE) is the pass that is responsible for configuring and creating the user environment during the setup process. The Specialization pass is where the operating system is configured during setup. The WinPE pass starts the procedure of installing the operating system.
whyWrong: The OOBE pass creates the user environment; it does not detect hardware or install drivers.
The Specialization pass applies system configuration during setup, not hardware detection.
WinPE is the preinstallation environment that starts setup; it is not the pass that installs drivers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 2

stem: Which partition contains the recovery utility in the event of a problem?
explanation: The WinRE partition is where the Windows Recovery Environment is located. The BCD is a term used with the boot configuration data to direct the operating system how to boot. The system partition contains the kernel of the operating system. The EFI system partition (ESP) contains the boot configuration data (BCD) that is used to boot the rest of the operating system on a UEFI system.
whyWrong: The BCD is boot configuration data that tells Windows how to boot; it is not a recovery partition.
The system partition holds the operating system files, not the recovery environment.
The EFI system partition holds the boot configuration data, not the recovery utility.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which tool is used to create an operating system image for deployment?
explanation: The Windows Deployment Services (WDS) is a server role that is used to create a Windows image for mass deployment. The Microsoft Assessment and Planning (MAP) toolkit is used to create reports on system hardware for image deployment. The User State Migration Toolkit (USMT) is used in a corporate environment to migrate user data. The sysprep utility is used to prepare an operating system for imaging.
whyWrong: The MAP toolkit reports on hardware for planning; it does not create deployment images.
USMT migrates user files and settings between computers; it does not create an OS image.
Sysprep prepares an installation for imaging by removing unique data, but the book names WDS as the tool for creating the image.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 4

stem: Which Windows Update branch for Windows will install features as they are released to the general public?
explanation: The General Availability branch will install updates as they are released to the general public. The Semi-Annual Channel is no longer a channel supported by Windows 11. The Long-Term Servicing Channel never installs new features during the life of the version of Windows. The Insider Program allows for the installation of brand-new features before they are publicly released.
whyWrong: The Semi-Annual Channel is no longer a supported channel in Windows 11.
The Long-Term Servicing Channel never adds new features during the life of the version.
The Insider Program delivers preview builds before they are released to the general public.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 6

stem: What is the name of the pass that configures and creates the user environment during the setup process?
explanation: The Out-Of-Box Experience (OOBE) is the pass that is responsible for configuring and creating the user environment during the setup process. The Generalization pass is where the operating system detects hardware. The Specialization pass is where the operating system is configured during setup. The WinPE pass starts the process of installing the operating system.
whyWrong: The Generalization pass detects hardware; it does not create the user environment.
The Specialization pass configures the system during setup, not the user environment.
WinPE is the preinstallation environment that starts setup, not the pass that creates the user environment.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 13

stem: When installing Windows, you can control telemetry data. In which step during setup is this configured?
explanation: When installing Windows, you can control telemetry data in the Privacy Settings dialog box. The Locale options allow you to control how the language and local notations of money, weight, date, and several other measurements for a particular region of the world. Disk partitioning is configured during the initial installation in order to direct Windows where to install. Account creation is performed to create the first user on the operating system.
whyWrong: Locale options set the language and regional formats, not telemetry data.
Partitioning options configure the disk layout, not telemetry data.
Account creation sets up the user account, not telemetry data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 14

stem: You want to upgrade from 32-bit Windows 10 Professional to a 64-bit version of Windows 11. What are your options?
options: Upgrade first to Windows 11 Pro 32-bit, and then upgrade to 64-bit.
Upgrade to Windows 10 64-bit, and then upgrade to Windows 11 64-bit.
You must perform a clean installation of Windows 11 Pro 64-bit.
explanation: There is no way to directly convert a 32-bit installation of Windows to 64-bit Windows without performing a clean installation. Upgrading directly to Windows 11 Pro 64-bit is not possible. Upgrading to Windows 11 Pro 32-bit is possible, but you cannot upgrade to a 64-bit edition. Upgrading to Windows 11 64-bit is not possible.
whyWrong: Windows cannot upgrade in place from a 32-bit installation to a 64-bit one.
An upgrade cannot change the bitness, and Windows 11 has no 32-bit edition.
Changing from 32-bit to 64-bit Windows 10 also needs a clean installation, so this path does not work.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 16
note: The book says a 32-bit Windows 11 Pro upgrade is possible, but Windows 11 has only 64-bit editions.

stem: Where is the boot configuration data stored on a Windows installation using EFI?
explanation: The BCD is stored in the EFI System Partition on an EFI installation of Windows. The WinRE partition is used for the Windows Recovery Environment. Secure Boot is a feature of an EFI installation and does not contain its own partition. The C:\WINDOWS folder is where the installation of Windows exists.
whyWrong: The WinRE partition holds the Windows Recovery Environment, not the boot configuration data.
Secure Boot is a firmware feature and has no partition of its own.
The C:\WINDOWS folder holds the Windows installation, not the BCD on an EFI system.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which of the following installation types would require PXE compliance?
explanation: A network-based installation requires that the network card be PXE compliant so that it can boot to the network and locate a DHCP server and deployment server. Local installations, such as those using a USB flash drive or optical disc, do not need the network adapter. Internal installations, such as those that are done from a secondary internal drive, also do not need a PXE-compliant network card.
whyWrong: A local installation runs from media at the computer, such as a USB drive or disc, without network boot.
An internal installation runs from a secondary internal drive and does not boot from the network card.
Booting from a USB flash drive is a local method that does not use the network adapter at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: To avoid SID conflicts when drive imaging, which program should you use in Windows?
explanation: Sysprep can modify unattended installations so that every computer gets a unique SID (and other unique information). Windows SIM creates the answer files for unattended installations. diskpart is used to view and configure partitions from the Command Prompt in Windows. Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM) is run on Windows Server and is used to deploy operating systems across the network.
whyWrong: Diskpart views and configures partitions from the command line; it does not make SIDs unique.
Windows SIM creates answer files for unattended installations; it does not reset the SID of an image.
MECM deploys operating systems across a network from a server; the SID reset itself is done by Sysprep.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You are tasked with installing Windows with the standard configuration. It needs to support a storage drive with a single 8 TB partition. Which of the following should you configure the system to use?
explanation: Use GUID [globally unique identifier] Partition Table (GPT) as your partitioning scheme (instead of MBR) and follow that up by using NTFS as your file system for the partition. That is the typical setup when installing Windows. In this scenario, GPT and NTFS can support 16 TB partitions. FAT32 is an older file system that you could use, but it would not support the 8 TB partition that is required. ext4 is a Linux-based file system not used in Windows. Know your file systems for the exam!
whyWrong: FAT32 is an old file system with small limits, so it cannot hold a single 8 TB partition.
MBR partitioning supports disks of at most 2 TB, so it cannot hold an 8 TB partition.
ext4 is a Linux file system and is not used for a standard Windows installation.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following uses an answer file to provide responses and eliminates the need for user intervention?
explanation: An unattended installation uses an answer file that provides the responses needed for the installation. A factory recovery partition is preloaded by the computer manufacturer. A clean installation means that the OS is installed to a blank partition or new drive. Reset your PC is an option in Windows that allows a user to repair a computer by reinstalling the OS with one of two options: wiping all data or keeping user files.
whyWrong: A factory recovery partition is preloaded by the manufacturer to restore the original image, not driven by an answer file.
A clean installation puts the OS on a blank partition or new drive, and a person still answers the setup prompts.
Reset this PC reinstalls Windows on the same computer, keeping or wiping files, without an answer file.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: What should a technician consider FIRST when planning to install Windows to a newer, less common storage drive? (Select the best answer.)
explanation: If you are installing Windows to a newer and less common storage drive, you might have to supply the manufacturer’s drivers (or third-party drivers) if Windows doesn’t recognize the drive. A repair in-place upgrade and other similar repair-based installations are usually last-resort attempts to fix individual systems. The purpose of a recovery partition is to enable users to return their computers back to their state when they were first received. A product’s life cycle is everything that happens from purchase to installation to end-of-life (EOL) and recycling/disposal.
whyWrong: A repair installation is a last-resort fix for a broken system, not a step in planning a new installation.
A recovery partition returns a computer to its factory state; it does not help Windows see a new drive.
The product life cycle covers support dates; it does not decide whether setup can detect the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: After a malware attack, a technician needs to completely wipe a customer’s hard drive and install a fresh copy of the Windows 11 Pro. What should the technician do?
options: Join the computer to a domain
Do a clean install of Windows 11 Pro
explanation: A clean install of Windows 11 Pro completely wipes your hard drive and installs a fresh copy of the operating system; it erases all data and settings. An in-place upgrade updates your current operating system to a new version and preserves your existing programs, files, and settings, meaning it doesn’t format the hard drive. Performing a malware scan or joining a domain will not help in this scenario. A clean install of Windows 11 Pro is required here.
whyWrong: An in-place upgrade keeps the existing programs, files, and settings, so it does not wipe the drive.
A malware scan may remove known threats, but it does not wipe the drive or install a fresh OS.
Joining a domain changes how the computer is managed; it does not remove malware or reinstall Windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A technician must reuse a donated hard drive and has to be sure that the old files on it cannot be read after the drive is formatted in Windows. Which format option is the BEST choice?
options: A quick format with exFAT instead of NTFS
Deleting the partition and leaving the space unallocated
explanation: A full format erases the existing data on the whole drive, so it takes much longer but leaves no old files behind. A quick format only writes a new file table and leaves the old data on the disk, where recovery tools can still find it.
whyWrong: A quick format only creates a new file table, so the old file contents stay on the disk.
Choosing exFAT changes the file system, but a quick format still leaves the old data in place.
Deleting a partition removes its entry from the partition table; the old data itself is not erased.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A technician plans to install the latest version of the Windows OS on a user’s device. The user insists all of their data files and configuration settings are retained during this process. Which of the following installation types should the technician use?
explanation: An in-place upgrade is intended to migrate user settings and installed applications. A network installation deploys from a server-based image (that is, image deployment) and will perform the equivalent of a clean install. A clean install will install a fresh version of Windows, overwriting all the user settings.
whyWrong: A network installation deploys a server image, which acts as a clean install and removes user settings.
A clean install replaces the existing system and does not keep the user's files or settings.
Image deployment writes a standard image to the device, which overwrites the user's data and settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.2, 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives).

stem: A support engineer is tasked with upgrading multiple desktop computers to Windows 10. However, they are only able to obtain a single copy of the installation media, and so they propose that they perform the upgrade over the network. Which of the following boot methods allows such an upgrade?
explanation: Pre-Boot Execution Environment (PXE) allows a computer to boot from the Network Interface Card (NIC) and access services on the network. In this case, the technician could use the media to create a Windows Deployment Server and perform the upgrades from a central location. Booting from a Solid State Drive (SSD) does not meet the requirements of installing over the network. Optical drives and flash drives can be used to install a single image but do not solve the problem of upgrading multiple computers across the network.
whyWrong: Booting from an SSD uses local storage and does not install over the network.
An optical drive installs one computer at a time from a disc.
A flash drive installs one computer at a time and does not use the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: A pharmaceutical company needs to deploy 500 new Windows 11 desktops in the most efficient way. The process needs to be automated so that the technicians’ time spent on this installation is minimized. What installation would be the BEST choice?
explanation: An unattended installation allows a central deployment image to be made available alongside an automated setup file (or unattended script). Once the installation is started, the technician can leave it to complete on its own. A remote network installation does not meet the requirements for an automated installation. A repair installation allows for a faulting computer to be reimaged back to a standard build configuration. A clean installation does not describe an automated process.
whyWrong: A remote network installation is not automated by itself and still needs input.
A repair installation fixes an existing Windows installation instead of deploying new ones.
A clean installation still needs a technician to answer the setup prompts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: During a manual installation of Windows 11 x64 on a brand-new desktop computer, a technician must select a partitioning scheme for the 12TB hard disk drive. Which partition format would make the best use of the available storage?
explanation: The GUID Partition Table (GPT) disk format allows partition sizes of up to 18 EB (that is, 18.8 million TB). A GPT drive can also contain as many as 128 separate partitions. ext4 is not supported on Windows; it is used on Linux filesystems. Master Boot Record (MBR) partitions are limited to a maximum size of 2TB and support a maximum of four partitions per disk. Apple File System (APFS) is not supported natively on Windows computers.
whyWrong: ext4 is a Linux file system, not a Windows partitioning scheme.
MBR supports disks of at most 2TB and four primary partitions.
APFS is an Apple file system and Windows does not support it natively.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: A technician is helping a remote customer upgrade their Windows workstation to the latest edition. The customer would like to retain all their applications and settings. Which option will upgrade the system and meet the customer’s requirements?
explanation: An in-place upgrade will allow the customer to keep all supported applications and retain their settings. It is important to check that in-place upgrades are supported for the version of Windows they are currently using. A clean install will not retain applications or settings. A repair installation will reset the image back to default for the current build of Windows on the customer’s system and is intended as a troubleshooting option. An unattended install does not necessarily mean that an upgrade will be selected.
whyWrong: A clean install removes the existing applications and settings.
A repair install resets the current build for troubleshooting; it does not upgrade.
An unattended install automates setup but does not by itself keep applications.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: Which was the first Microsoft Windows operating system with a mandatory requirement for feature upgrades?
explanation: Windows 10 was the first Windows operating system to support feature upgrades (Windows 11 also supports feature upgrades). Typically released every six months, feature upgrades include additional features and functionality. In previous releases of Windows, new features and functionality were delivered with service packs or interim releases, such as the upgrade of Windows 8.0 to 8.1. Windows 7 and Windows 8.1 do not support feature upgrades.
whyWrong: Windows 11 also gets feature updates, but Windows 10 introduced them first.
Windows 8.1 was an interim release and did not use regular feature updates.
Windows 7 received service packs, not feature updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: A large multinational manufacturer has a user base of 6,000 Windows desktops and would like to create a baseline configuration so that all desktops have identical features and applications. What would be the BEST solution for this organization?
explanation: An image deployment allows for a customized build of the operating system (along with any required applications) to be created. The image can be hosted on a Windows Deployment Server, and all new installations will use the standard centralized image. An upgrade will retain current applications and settings (some existing desktop computers may have different applications installed and be configured differently). Clean installations do not always ensure the same settings will be applied. A repair installation is used to set a Windows computer back up on a standard image as a troubleshooting step.
whyWrong: An upgrade keeps each desktop's existing applications and settings, so they stay different.
Clean installs done one by one do not guarantee identical settings.
A repair installation is a troubleshooting step, not a way to standardize desktops.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: An installation team is deploying new images using pxe boot. In order to minimize the load on the deployment server, they are deploying images to only 30 workstations simultaneously. There is a possibility that this process may cause bottlenecks. What should the team most closely monitor?
explanation: When installing images from a central server across the network, it is expected that the overall traffic on the network segment will increase. It is important that any unacceptable load on the network is identified. The impact on users will only be a concern if the network is overwhelmed with additional traffic. DHCP will need to provide IP addresses to 30 workstations at a time (during the build), so this should not add any great burden to the DHCP server. The impact on production workstations will only be a negative concern if the network is experiencing unacceptable volumes of additional traffic during the build process.
whyWrong: Users are affected only if the network becomes overloaded, so the network is what to watch.
DHCP gives addresses to only 30 workstations at a time, which adds little load.
Production workstations are affected only when the network segment is congested.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (types of installations, image deployment)

stem: A technician is helping the company upgrade a mixture of laptops and desktops to run Windows 11. In order to support larger volume sizes and multiple partitions, it has been decided that hard drives will be configured using GPT partitioning. In order to support Windows 11 and GPT disks, what MINIMUM hardware specifications must be in place? (Choose two.)
explanation: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) replaces the original Binary Input Output System (BIOS) seen in computer systems since the original 1980s PC systems. UEFI is needed to support GPT disks. Windows 11 installation requires the presence of a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to support some of the security features now standard in the operating system. Windows 11 requires 4GB RAM and a 1GHz 64-bit processor in addition to TPM 2.0 and UEFI support.
whyWrong: Windows 11 needs only 4GB of RAM, not 32GB.
Legacy BIOS cannot boot from a GPT disk and does not meet Windows 11 requirements.
Windows 11 needs a 1GHz dual-core 64-bit CPU, not an 8-core CPU.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (hardware requirements) and 1.2 (partitioning)

stem: A Windows desktop computer fails to boot following a power loss and unexpected system shutdown. What should the technician try FIRST to see if the system can be recovered?
explanation: A repair installation allows for boot issues, such as missing or corrupt startup files, to be fixed. The technician will be presented with the Advanced Options menu if Windows cannot boot and the Automatic Repair function has failed. This menu provides options including System Restore, System Image Recovery (if you have a backup), or to run a Startup Repair. Unattended, image deployment, and remote installations are not intended as troubleshooting steps.
whyWrong: An unattended installation deploys a new system and is not a recovery step.
Image deployment replaces the system and is not a first troubleshooting step.
A remote installation deploys Windows over the network and is not a recovery step.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (OS installations and upgrades)

stem: Technicians are preparing to upgrade departmental workstations to the latest Windows OS. In order to avoid problems during the upgrade, they would like to see a report listing potential missing hardware features that may prevent an upgrade.
options: Microsoft Windows PC Health Check App
explanation: The Windows PC Health Check App is a free Microsoft download and allows a Windows computer to be assessed prior to an upgrade. Following this assessment, the app will provide you with a list of system requirements for the given upgrade and state whether or not these are met by the system in question. While the other options do provide useful information for technicians, they do not present an easy-to-read upgrade report.
whyWrong: A hardware compatibility list must be checked by hand and does not report on this computer.
System Information lists hardware details but does not compare them with upgrade requirements.
Task Manager shows running processes and performance, not upgrade readiness.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.9 question 10
note: 220-1102 1.9; mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (upgrade considerations) and 1.3 (hardware requirements)

stem: You have been tasked with downloading an operating system image to be installed to a virtual machine. Which of the following file types will you MOST LIKELY download?
explanation: Using an ISO image (.iso) is a common way to allow for the download of operating systems such as Windows, Linux, and so on. It can be easily read by virtualization programs to install operating systems into virtual machines. An ISO image is designed to take the place of an entire optical disc.
whyWrong: An EXE file is an executable program, not an image of an operating system installation disc.
An appimage is a Linux application that runs without installation, not an operating system image.
A VDI file is a VirtualBox virtual storage drive, not the installation image that you download.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 38

stem: A home user needs to reinstall Windows on a home computer but cannot find the operating system media that came with the computer. Which of the following would allow the home user to install the operating system?
explanation: If the computer has a recovery partition, then Windows can be reinstalled from there. This is often a partition that was placed on the storage drive by the computer manufacturer for just this type of scenario.
whyWrong: System Restore takes the system back to an earlier restore point; it does not reinstall the whole OS.
Linux rescue media can help only when a Windows image is available somewhere, so it is not a reliable way to reinstall Windows.
The primary partition is where Windows is installed, and it normally holds no recovery image.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 58

stem: A development company has a high staff turnover. They would like to identify the most efficient way to use Microsoft Windows 10 features to install a fresh Windows OS when a laptop is re-purposed for a new member of staff. Which of the following is the most suitable?
options: Manually reinstall Windows 10 from installation media
Use Windows 10’s Reset This PC feature
explanation: The “Reset This PC” feature in Windows 10 allows you to reinstall Windows while keeping all previous user files and settings. It’s a quick and efficient way to prepare a laptop for a new user while maintaining the base operating system.
whyWrong: Reinstalling from installation media works, but it takes more time and effort than the built-in reset feature.
Cloning the drive copies the old system with its software and settings, which may not suit a new user.
System Restore returns the system to an earlier restore point; it does not reinstall the operating system.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 40
note: 220-1102 1.9 (OS installations: recovery and reset); mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (Types of installations: recovery partition and repair installation). For a new user, Reset This PC would use the Remove everything option; the book's explanation says it keeps files and settings.

stem: Which method should the support technician choose to perform a local Windows 8.1 to Windows 10 upgrade, migrating files and user preferences while ensuring that each system is upgraded individually?
explanation: To ensure files and user preferences are retained and perform the operation locally while migrating one station at a time, the most efficient method would be an in-place upgrade. An in-place upgrade allows a seamless transition to Windows 10 while preserving user data and settings.
whyWrong: A master image deploys many identical computers at once and does not keep each user's files and settings.
A fresh install wipes the existing system and user data, which goes against keeping files and preferences.
WDS installs the OS over the network from a server, which does not meet the need for a local upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 53
note: 220-1102 1.9 (types of installations: upgrade); mapped to 220-1202 1.2 (Types of installations: upgrade). Windows 8.1 is end of life. The book's explanation said Windows 7 Pro to Windows 10 Pro; the version was removed to match the stem.

stem: A technician is installing Windows 11 on a new 8 TB drive in a UEFI workstation. The user wants five partitions for projects. Which partition style is the BEST choice?
options: A dynamic disk with a spanned volume
explanation: GPT supports up to 128 partitions and partitions far larger than the 2 TB MBR limit. It is part of the UEFI standard, so it suits a UEFI workstation with a very large drive.
whyWrong: MBR limits each partition to 2 TB and allows only four primary partitions, so it cannot use the whole drive.
An extended partition adds logical drives, but the MBR 2 TB size limit still wastes most of the 8 TB drive.
A spanned volume joins space across several drives; it does not set the partition style of a single new drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

stem: A small office plans to upgrade a manager's Windows 10 laptop to Windows 11 this weekend. The laptop meets the hardware requirements. What should the technician do FIRST before starting the upgrade?
options: Back up the manager's files and user preferences
Format the system partition with NTFS
Run Disk Cleanup to remove the Windows Update files
Change the boot order to boot from the network
explanation: An upgrade may or may not keep the user's data, so the files and the user profile are always backed up before an upgrade starts. Application and driver support should also be checked before the upgrade.
whyWrong: Formatting the system partition erases Windows and the data, which is the opposite of an upgrade.
Disk Cleanup frees space, but it does not protect the manager's data if the upgrade fails.
A network boot is used to start an installation from a server; it is not a preparation step for an in-place upgrade.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

stem: A technician boots a new desktop from a Windows 11 flash drive. Setup starts, but the screen that asks where to install Windows lists no drives. The desktop has a new-model NVMe drive that shows in the UEFI setup. What is the MOST LIKELY reason?
options: Setup has no driver for the new storage drive
The flash drive was not made bootable
The drive must first be converted to a dynamic disk
The desktop is set to boot from the network
explanation: Newer or uncommon storage drives may not be recognized by the Windows installer. The fix is to load the manufacturer's third-party storage driver during setup, from the maker's website if Windows Update does not have it.
whyWrong: Setup has already started from the flash drive, so the drive is bootable.
Dynamic disks are set up in Windows after installation; they are not needed for Setup to see a drive.
The desktop has already booted from the flash drive, so the boot order is not the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades

stem: Cindy’s client wants a new workstation. The client’s small business has ten current workstations connected in a Windows domain, and the client wants the new workstation to be part of that domain. What edition of Windows 10 should Cindy install on the new computer to accomplish this goal and provide the BEST value?
explanation: Windows 10 Pro offers the best choice here. The Enterprise edition would also work, but it costs more and adds features the client doesn’t need.
whyWrong: Windows 10 has no Starter edition, and Starter editions could never join a domain.
Windows 10 Home cannot join a Windows domain.
Windows 10 Enterprise can join a domain, but it costs more and adds features the client does not need.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which is required for a 64-bit installation of Windows 11?
explanation: A Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0 is required for the installation of Windows 11. 64 GB or greater of storage is required for the installation of Windows 11. A Microsoft DirectX 12 graphics device is required for the installation of Windows 11. The minimum amount of memory required for the installation of the 64-bit Windows 11 operating system is 4 GB. More RAM is always recommended, but only 4 GB is required.
whyWrong: Windows 11 needs at least 64 GB of storage, so 32 GB is not enough.
Windows 11 needs a DirectX 12 compatible graphics device, not DirectX 9.
Windows 11 does need 4 GB of RAM, but the book's answer for this question is TPM 2.0.
