source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 12
note: The book keys only TPM 2.0, although 4 GB of RAM is also a Windows 11 minimum.

stem: What is the minimum amount of free hard drive space required for the installation of Windows 11 64-bit?
explanation: The minimum amount of free hard drive space required for Windows 11 64-bit is 64 GB. Smaller drives, such as the 32 GB that Windows 10 64-bit needed, do not meet the Windows 11 requirement.
whyWrong: A 1.5 GB drive is far too small for any current Windows installation.
Fifteen gigabytes is below the Windows 11 minimum of 64 GB of storage.
Thirty-two gigabytes was the Windows 10 64-bit minimum; Windows 11 needs 64 GB.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 13

stem: What is the minimum required memory for a 64-bit installation of Windows 11?
explanation: The minimum amount of memory required for the 64-bit installation of the Windows 11 is 4 GB. Lower values such as 2 GB were enough for 64-bit Windows 10 but not for Windows 11.
whyWrong: Five hundred twelve megabytes is far below what any 64-bit Windows edition needs.
One gigabyte was the minimum for 32-bit Windows 10, not for Windows 11.
Two gigabytes was the Windows 10 64-bit minimum; Windows 11 needs 4 GB.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 14

stem: What is the minimum required processor speed for a 64-bit installation of Windows 11?
explanation: The minimum processor speed required for the 64-bit installation of the Windows 11 is 1 GHz. The processor must also have two or more cores and be on the supported list.
whyWrong: Windows 11 needs a processor of at least 1 GHz, so 2.2 GHz is higher than the minimum.
A 3.3 GHz processor is well above the Windows 11 minimum of 1 GHz.
A 2.3 GHz processor exceeds the 1 GHz minimum, so it is not the minimum value.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 20

stem: You are tasked with installing Windows 11 on a new computer. The computer has a 1 GHz processor, 2 GB of RAM, and 32 GB of storage. What should you do?
options: Upgrade the RAM to at least 4 GB.
explanation: Windows 11 requires a minimum of 4 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage. Therefore, to meet these requirements, you need to upgrade both the RAM and the storage. Simply proceeding with the installation would not work because the current specifications do not meet the minimum requirements. Upgrading only the RAM or only the storage would still leave one of the requirements unmet, making both upgrades necessary.
whyWrong: The computer does not meet the Windows 11 minimums for RAM or storage, so the installation cannot proceed.
More RAM alone is not enough because the 32 GB of storage is also below the 64 GB minimum.
More storage alone is not enough because the 2 GB of RAM is also below the 4 GB minimum.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which edition of Windows 11 will not allow for Insider Program branch releases?
explanation: Windows 11 Home only allows for the General Availability branch releases. Windows 11 Pro allows for the use of the Insider Program branch releases. Windows 11 Education allows for the use of the Insider Program branch releases. Windows 11 Enterprise allows for the use of Insider Program branch releases.
whyWrong: Windows 11 Pro can join the Insider Program branch releases.
Windows 11 Education can join the Insider Program branch releases.
Windows 11 Enterprise can join the Insider Program branch releases.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 7

stem: You are configuring a new Windows 11 installation and need to ensure it supports Secure Boot. What type of firmware must the computer have?
explanation: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) firmware is required for Secure Boot, which enhances security by ensuring that only trusted software is loaded during the boot process. Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) and Legacy BIOS do not support Secure Boot. Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI) is an older term; UEFI is the correct modern term.
whyWrong: BIOS firmware does not support Secure Boot.
Legacy BIOS mode does not support Secure Boot.
EFI is the older specification that UEFI replaced; Windows 11 Secure Boot needs UEFI firmware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 8

stem: What is the maximum number of concurrent connections that can be made to a Windows workstation?
explanation: The maximum number of connections that can simultaneously be made to a Windows workstation is 20. All other answers are incorrect. A server operating system is needed when more users must connect at the same time.
whyWrong: Thirty connections is more than the 20 concurrent connections that a Windows workstation allows.
Forty connections is more than the 20 concurrent connections that a Windows workstation allows.
Twenty-five connections is more than the 20 concurrent connections that a Windows workstation allows.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 20

stem: Which of the following are the minimum system requirements for installing 64-bit Windows 11? (Select two.)
options: 1 GHz or faster CPU with two or more cores or Systems on a Chip (SoC)
explanation: The minimum system requirements for installing 64-bit Windows 11 are 1 GHz or faster processor with two or more cores or Systems on a Chip (SoCs), 4 GB RAM, 64 GB free hard disk space, and UEFI and TPM 2.0. Know the Windows installation system requirements for the exam and the real world!
whyWrong: Windows 11 needs at least 4 GB of RAM; 2 GB is below the minimum.
Windows 11 requires TPM version 2.0 with UEFI; TPM 1.0 does not meet the requirement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 30: Operating System Installations and Upgrades, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which editions of Windows 11 offer Hyper-V? (Select three.)
explanation: Of the listed answers, Windows 11 Pro, Pro for Workstations, and Enterprise offer Hyper-V virtualization functionality. Windows 10 Home does not. Remember that just because Hyper-V is included as a feature doesn’t mean it will work. The motherboard of the computer has to support virtualization; in addition, virtualization must be enabled in the BIOS/UEFI, and Hyper-V has to be enabled (turned on) within Programs and Features.
whyWrong: Windows 11 Home does not include Hyper-V; it needs Pro, Pro for Workstations, Enterprise, or Education.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions, Cram Quiz question 1
note: Option C says "Windows 10 Pro for Workstations" in a Windows 11 question; the book's explanation names Windows 11 Pro for Workstations. Both editions include Hyper-V, so the key is right.

stem: Where should you go to find out what applications are running in the background in Windows?
explanation: Go to the notification area to find out what applications are running in the background. (Another way is to use the Task Manager.) In Windows 11, click the arrow that points up to show hidden icons. In other versions of Windows, the applications might actually appear in the notification area itself.
whyWrong: The taskbar holds the Start button and open apps; background apps show in its notification area, not the bar itself.
The Start menu lists installed apps and settings; it does not show which apps run in the background.
Quick Launch holds shortcuts to start programs; it does not show programs that are already running.
Cortana is a voice assistant; it does not list the applications running in the background.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions, Cram Quiz question 2
note: Windows desktop interface (notification area); no exact 220-1202 topic, mapped to 1.3 feature differences as the book does.

stem: A customer requires a current operating system that can utilize 512 GB of RAM that is installed to a PC. Which of the following should you suggest? (Select two.)
explanation: You should suggest Windows 11 Pro or Enterprise to take advantage of the PC’s 512 GB of RAM. Windows 11 Pro can access up to 2 TB of RAM, and Enterprise can access up to 6 TB (so you could say there is plenty of headroom here). However, Windows 11 Home can only access 128 GB of RAM—and that is not enough! And Windows 8 Pro can only access 192 GB of RAM. Support for Windows 8 ended in January 2023.
whyWrong: Windows 11 Home supports at most 128 GB of RAM, which is far less than 512 GB.
Windows 8 Pro supports only 192 GB of RAM and is no longer a current, supported OS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following includes the same functionality as other editions of Windows, except for media-related technologies?
explanation: The N editions of Windows include the same functionality as other editions of Windows, except for media-related technologies, Windows Media Player, and certain preinstalled media apps. Hyper-V is a Microsoft virtualization program used to create and run virtual machines (VMs) on Windows systems. Programs and Features is a Windows tool used to manage updates and Windows programs. BitLocker is a Windows security feature used to encrypt an entire storage drive (or volume) to protect from unauthorized access.
whyWrong: Hyper-V is the Windows virtualization feature for running virtual machines, not an edition without media apps.
Programs and Features manages installed programs and Windows features; it is not a Windows edition.
BitLocker encrypts whole drives or volumes; it is a security feature, not a Windows edition.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions, Cram Quiz question 5

stem:
A client wants to know if you can upgrade a Windows 10 Pro computer to Windows 11 Pro. The client’s system has the following specifications:

Architecture: 64-bit

Processor: 1 GHz

Memory: 4 GB

Free hard disk space: 64 GB

Graphics card: Microsoft DirectX graphics device with WDDM 2.0 driver

Display: High-definition 720p

Additional hardware: UEFI and TPM 1.0

Does the client’s system meet the minimum systems requirements for Windows 11 Pro?
options: Yes, all system requirements are met to upgrade to Windows 11 Pro.
No, upgrading to Windows 11 Pro requires 164 GB of free hard disk space.
Yes, with 64-bit architecture, anything is possible.
No, to upgrade to Windows 11 Pro, UEFI and TPM 2.0 are required.
explanation: The client’s system does not meet the minimum system requirements to upgrade the Windows 10 Pro computer to Windows 11 Pro. The additional hardware requirement to upgrade to Windows 11 Pro is UEFI and TPM 2.0. Microsoft states that “TPM 2.0 is a ’non-negotiable’ requirement for Windows 11. TPM stands for Trusted Platform Module, and it's a secure cryptoprocessor that stores encryption keys and performs other cryptographic functions. Windows uses TPM 2.0 for security-related features like: Windows Hello for identity protection, BitLocker for data protection, and Secure Boot.”
whyWrong: The system has TPM 1.0, and Windows 11 needs TPM 2.0, so not all requirements are met.
Windows 11 needs 64 GB of free space, not 164 GB, so storage is not what blocks the upgrade.
A 64-bit architecture alone is not enough; Windows 11 also needs UEFI and TPM 2.0.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which Windows 10 edition is not sold in retail stores and is obtained through a Microsoft volume license agreement or a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription?
explanation: Windows 10 Enterprise is sold to mid-size and large organizations through volume licensing or a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription. It includes every Pro feature plus features that large organizations need.
whyWrong: Windows 10 Home is a retail edition that usually comes preinstalled by the hardware vendor.
Windows 10 Pro can be bought off the shelf through normal retail channels.
Pro for Workstations normally comes preinstalled on high-end workstation hardware, not through a volume agreement.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

stem: A user plans to buy a laptop with Windows 11 Home. Which TWO features will the user NOT have unless the laptop is upgraded to Windows 11 Pro? (Choose two.)
explanation: BitLocker and the Local Group Policy Editor are available in every Windows 11 edition except Home. Home also cannot join a domain or accept inbound Remote Desktop connections. Defender, Windows Hello, and Snap Assist are part of all editions.
whyWrong: Microsoft Defender antivirus is built into every edition of Windows 11, including Home.
Windows Hello biometric sign-in works in Windows 11 Home as well as the business editions.
Snap Assist is a desktop feature of every Windows 11 edition.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

stem: A traveler bought a laptop in Europe that runs Windows 11 Pro N. The user reports that Windows Media Player and the built-in video apps are missing, and some media files will not play. What is the BEST way to fix this?
options: Upgrade the laptop to Windows 11 Enterprise
Update the graphics card driver in Device Manager
Run a repair installation of Windows 11
explanation: N versions of Windows ship without Windows Media Player and related media apps to meet European Union rules. Installing the free Media Feature Pack, or another media player, restores the missing media features.
whyWrong: Enterprise does not add the missing media apps; the N versions lack them by design and need the Media Feature Pack.
The video driver controls the display; it does not add Windows Media Player or the media codecs that N versions omit.
A repair installation reinstalls the same N version, so the media apps would still be missing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 31: Basic Features of Windows Editions

stem: A user receives a new laptop computer that runs Windows 10. Upon first use, they are prompted to provide a password prior to the regular login prompt. What feature would likely cause this prompt?
explanation: BitLocker Drive Encryption requires an additional BitLocker password before the Windows OS is launched. If this is successfully entered, then the user will be presented with the regular login prompt next. A BIOS password requires a special key sequence, such as Ctrl + D, the purpose of which is to prevent a user from entering the BIOS/UEFI at startup. Windows Privacy and Security does not ask for a prompt before the OS launches. Windows Accessibility is typically used for the configuration of Windows settings to help users with audio or visual impairments.
whyWrong: A BIOS password protects firmware setup; Windows encryption is what asks for a key before the OS loads on a new laptop.
Windows privacy and security settings run inside Windows and never prompt for a password before Windows starts.
Accessibility settings help users with impairments and do not add any password prompt at startup.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives).

stem: A senior manager is insisting that their personal laptop be joined to the company’s domain so that they can use their preferred operating system and hardware. Which operating systems would NOT be supported for this role? (Choose two.)
explanation: Windows 10 Home is intended for personal use and does not offer support features for enterprise/business users. ChromeOS is a simple-to-use OS and does not allow domain join. All Windows Pro and Enterprise editions DO support domain join functionality.
whyWrong: Windows 8.1 Pro is a business edition, so it can join an Active Directory domain.
Windows 10 Pro includes domain join, so it would be supported for this role.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives).

stem: A technician is attempting to enable BitLocker Drive Encryption on company laptops, but the option is only available for some of the laptops. Which versions of the Windows operating system support BitLocker Drive Encryption? (Choose two.)
explanation: Windows 10 Pro and Enterprise editions are intended for business use and support additional functionality, including security features. They therefore support BitLocker. Older versions of Windows require Enterprise (or Windows 7 Ultimate) licenses to access advanced security features. Windows Home editions do not have access to BitLocker. macOS offers File Vault as an alternative to Windows BitLocker.
whyWrong: Windows 10 Home does not include BitLocker; it offers only device encryption on supported hardware.
On Windows 7, BitLocker was limited to the Ultimate and Enterprise editions, not Professional.
macOS uses FileVault for disk encryption and does not run BitLocker at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives). Windows 7 Pro is an obsolete option; kept as in the book.

stem: A small company is looking to upgrade all company workstations from Windows 8.1 Pro to the equivalent Windows 10 edition. The systems are managed, and all conform to the company’s baseline image. The company would like to use the least administrative effort to make this transition, migrating all applications and user data at the same time. Which of the following would be the BEST solution?
options: Fresh installation from a central server
explanation: Assuming there are no compatibility issues, an in-place upgrade will require the least administrative effort to migrate all user settings and applications. A fresh installation will not migrate the settings and applications. The user settings would need to be backed up separately, and applications would need to be reinstalled.
whyWrong: A fresh installation from a server wipes applications and user data, so everything must be restored afterward.
A fresh installation from optical media removes installed applications and settings, which adds work.
A fresh installation from USB media still replaces the old system, so apps and data are not migrated.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives).

stem: A technician is responding to a support ticket from a manager who cannot enable BitLocker on their personal computer while working from home. What is the MOST LIKELY cause of this problem?
options: The system only has 2GB of RAM installed
The system is running Windows Home edition
The system is running a 32-bit edition of Windows
The system has a 128GB hard drive
explanation: As the manager is using a personal computer, it is highly likely that the system was purchased from a retail store, where the default Windows OS edition will be Home. BitLocker Drive Encryption requires at least Windows Professional. Having only 2GB of memory would not prevent BitLocker from being enabled. The size of the hard drive would only be an issue if there is not sufficient space to create a small unencrypted partition (100MB). BitLocker is supported on 32-bit and 64-bit editions of Windows.
whyWrong: BitLocker does not need more than 2GB of RAM, so the memory size does not block it.
BitLocker is supported on both 32-bit and 64-bit editions of Windows.
A 128GB drive has plenty of room for the small unencrypted system partition that BitLocker needs.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives).

stem: A service desk technician is tasked with connecting remotely to a Windows desktop computer. The technician needs to change configuration settings using a secure connection. It is important that the user must be logged off during this process. Which of the following tools would the technician MOST LIKELY use?
explanation: The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) establishes a connection that allows a remote user to take control of another console/desktop, logging any existing users off the device. Virtual Network Computing (VNC) and Remote Assistance (RA) allow remote sharing of a desktop, meaning that the user would be able to view the session. Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) only allows the transfer of files, not any configuration changes.
whyWrong: VNC shares the screen with the logged-in user, so the user stays logged on and can watch.
Remote Assistance shares the session with the user, who must be present and logged on to accept it.
SFTP only transfers files securely and cannot be used to change desktop configuration settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives). Remote access tools are also in 220-1202 4.9; mapped here for RDP availability by edition.

stem: A company is proposing in-place upgrades for all the current Windows platforms that are running on a 32-bit OS. If these are performed, what would the memory limitation of the 32-bit OS be?
explanation: A limitation of installing a 32-bit Operating System (OS) is that 4GB of RAM is the maximum available to the system, even if the underlying hardware is 64-bit. There are some restrictions on the maximum amount of memory even if a 64-bit OS is installed. 64-bit Windows Pro and Enterprise support 2TB of RAM, while the 64-bit edition of Home supports 128GB.
whyWrong: 16MB is far below the real limit; a 32-bit OS can address up to 4GB of RAM.
2048GB (2TB) is the limit of 64-bit Windows Pro and Enterprise, not of a 32-bit OS.
128GB is the limit of 64-bit Windows 10 Home, not of a 32-bit OS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (RAM support limitations). 32-bit Windows is obsolete in Windows 11.

stem: A deskside support technician has shown the marketing manager how to use BitLocker To Go. The technician MOST LIKELY encrypted which of the following?
explanation: BitLocker To Go can be used on a supported Windows OS to encrypt removable media. BitLocker can be used to encrypt fixed drives on supported Windows OSs but cannot be used to encrypt optical media.
whyWrong: BitLocker To Go cannot encrypt optical media such as a DVD-RW disk.
BitLocker To Go encrypts removable drives attached to the computer, not shares on a network drive.
An internal fixed drive is encrypted with standard BitLocker, not with BitLocker To Go.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives).

stem: A home user has raised a support ticket requesting remote assistance for a problem they are experiencing with a locally installed application. When a technician attempts to connect to the remote system using RDP, there is a connection error. What is the MOST LIKELY reason for the error?
options: The system only has 2GB of RAM installed
The system is running a Windows Home edition
The system is running a 32-bit edition of Windows
The system is running a Windows Pro edition
explanation: Windows Home editions are intended for the consumer market and do not have the same tools and utilities as those offered in the Pro/Enterprise versions. RDP is only offered as a client on Home editions. This means you can connect to a Pro or Enterprise desktop, but they cannot connect to your desktop.
whyWrong: Remote Desktop has the same memory needs as the OS, so 2GB of RAM does not cause the error.
Remote Desktop is available on both 32-bit and 64-bit Windows, so the architecture is not the cause.
Windows Pro editions include the Remote Desktop host, so a Pro edition would accept the connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.1 question 10
note: 220-1102 1.1; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Windows editions in the old objectives). The book's explanation says Home offers RDP 'as a host service'; Home has only the RDP client, so that word was changed to 'client'.

stem: A support ticket is raised by a senior manager having computer-related problems while working from home on their personal Windows 10 computer. They are attempting to access e-mail prior to attending an important business event. The support technician is unable to access the system using remote desktop, so, as a workaround, they use a third-party desktop sharing application. The technician identifies a solution to the manager’s problem and proposes that they make configuration changes using Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc). However, when they attempt to run the tool, they find it is not available on the manager’s computer. What is the MOST LIKELY reason that these tools have not been present on the manager’s computer?
options: The computer is running Windows 10 Enterprise
The computer is running Windows 10 Home
The computer has a corrupt registry
explanation: RDP and Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) are both features that are only included in the Pro and Enterprise versions of Windows. The computer is not running Linux as the technician would have discovered this when installing third-party tools. Windows 10 Enterprise would have allowed for the functionality that the technician required. It is unlikely that a corrupt registry would have caused these two very specific problems without impacting other services on the user’s computer.
whyWrong: Linux does not run Windows tools at all, and the technician would have seen this while installing the sharing app.
Windows 10 Enterprise includes both Remote Desktop hosting and the Group Policy Editor.
A corrupt registry would cause wider problems, not the absence of exactly these two Pro features.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (feature differences: gpedit.msc and RDP availability).

stem:
You are attempting to install a Windows 64-bit OS within a VM, but you keep receiving errors. The specifications for the VM include

- Four 1 GHz CPUs

- 4 GB of RAM

- 15 GB storage drive space

- 720p screen resolution

Which of the following should you do to resolve this issue?
options: Increase the amount of drive space.
explanation: The storage drive space is not large enough for Windows 11. The 64-bit installations of Windows 11 require 64 GB of storage drive space. This holds true for physical installations and virtual installations. The virtual machine (VM) installation will fail until the VM’s drive space is increased.
whyWrong: Four 1 GHz CPUs already meet the processor requirement, so more CPUs would not fix the errors.
4 GB of RAM already meets the memory requirement, so more memory would not fix the errors.
A 720p resolution already meets the display requirement, so a higher resolution would not fix the errors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 30

stem:
Your upgrade attempt from Windows 10 Pro to Windows 11 Pro fails. Your system has the following specs:

- 64-bit Intel Core i9 3.70 GHz CPU

- 16 GB RAM

- 100 GB Storage

- UEFI Secure Boot enabled

- TPM subversion 1.38

- Graphics card DirectX 12 with WDDM 2.0 driver

- Display high definition (720p)

Which of the following is preventing you from performing the upgrade to Windows 11 Pro?
options: The processor does not meet the minimum requirements.
The graphics card does not meet the minimum requirements.
explanation: Your system does not meet Trusted Platform Module requirements. According to Microsoft’s Windows 11 Pro minimum requirements (as of March 2025), TPM version 2.0 is required to upgrade your system to Windows 11 Pro. To fix the problem, you would have to upgrade the TPM firmware and possibly flash the BIOS/UEFI.
whyWrong: A 64-bit 3.70 GHz Core i9 is well above the 1 GHz, two-core minimum for Windows 11.
16 GB of RAM is well above the 4 GB minimum for Windows 11.
A DirectX 12 graphics card with a WDDM 2.0 driver meets the Windows 11 graphics requirement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 84

stem: A technician is experiencing problems while trying to add a sales manager’s personal laptop to the company’s Active Directory domain. What is the most probable reason why a technician is unable to join a Windows 10 laptop computer to an Active Directory domain?
options: The computer processor is an AMD version
The laptop is equipped with Windows 10 Home edition
The laptop does not have a touchscreen
The laptop is connected to a docking station
explanation: The most likely reason why the technician is unable to join a Windows 10 laptop to a domain is because the laptop is running the Windows 10 Home edition. Windows 10 Home does not have the capability to join a domain; this functionality is only available in Windows 10 Professional or Enterprise editions.
whyWrong: The processor brand does not decide whether Windows can join a domain.
A touchscreen has nothing to do with joining a computer to a domain.
A docking station does not affect the ability of the laptop to join a domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 25
note: 220-1102 1.1 (Windows editions: domain access); mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Feature differences: domain vs. workgroup). The staging record listed answers A and B; the book's answer key gives B only.

stem: After installing Windows 10 on a workstation, a technician notices that the system is only utilizing 3.5 GB of the installed 8 GB RAM. What is the MOST probable reason for this discrepancy?
options: The system is missing critical updates
The system is operating on a 32-bit operating system
The system’s RAM modules are malfunctioning
The system requires updates to its BIOS
explanation: The most likely reason for the system not utilizing all the available RAM is that it is running on a 32-bit operating system. 32-bit operating systems have a maximum RAM capacity of approximately 4 GB, and any RAM installed beyond that limit will not be recognized or utilized. To fully utilize the installed 8 GB of RAM, the system would need to be upgraded to a 64-bit operating system.
whyWrong: Missing updates can affect performance, but they do not limit how much RAM the OS can address.
Faulty RAM would cause errors or missing modules, while a limit near 4 GB points to a 32-bit OS.
BIOS updates generally do not change how much RAM the operating system can use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 66
note: 220-1102 1.1 (Windows editions: RAM support) and 1.8 (32-bit vs. 64-bit); mapped to 220-1202 1.3 (Feature differences: RAM support limitations).

stem: What program does Microsoft include with Windows to partition and format a drive?
explanation: Windows uses the Disk Management console to partition and format a drive. Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) can create, extend, shrink, and format volumes.
whyWrong: Format only formats a volume; it does not create or change partitions.
Disk Administrator was the Windows NT tool, not the current Windows tool.
System Commander was a third-party boot manager, not a tool included with Windows.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 3

stem: How can you effectively expand the capacity of an NTFS drive?
options: Create an extended partition to extend the capacity.
Install a second drive and mount it to a folder on the original smaller NTFS drive.
Convert the drive to a dynamic disk and create a mirrored set.
Format the drive with the Quick Format option.
explanation: You can effectively expand the capacity of an NTFS drive by installing a second drive and mounting it to a folder on the original smaller NTFS drive. Disk Management can mount a volume to an empty NTFS folder instead of a drive letter.
whyWrong: An extended partition holds logical drives; it does not add capacity to an existing NTFS volume.
A mirrored set copies data to a second disk for redundancy; it does not add usable space.
Quick Format erases the volume and does not change its capacity.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 7
note: 220-1101 3.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Disk Management). Options repaired from the chapter file.

stem: What is Audit Success?
options: A Registry Editor option to ensure a Registry change won’t render the system unbootable
A Windows Update utility to visualize what fraction of updates are installed within one week
A keyword used to indicate successful actions in the Security log found within Event Viewer
A high level of login security in the Updates and Security settings that audits even successful login attempts
explanation: Audit Success (along with Audit Failure) is a keyword unique to the Security log in Event Viewer. Audit policies decide which actions, such as logons, are written to the Security log.
whyWrong: Registry Editor has no Audit Success option for testing changes.
Windows Update has no utility called Audit Success.
Updates and Security settings do not hold a login auditing level called Audit Success.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 2
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Event Viewer). Options repaired from the chapter file.

stem: When using Performance Monitor, which settings are defined to track resource usage? (Select two.)
explanation: To track resource usage in Performance Monitor, you need to configure objects and counters. An object is a component such as the processor, and a counter is one measured value of it.
whyWrong: Processes are tracked through an object, but they are not the setting you define.
Values are the measured results, not the settings you define in Performance Monitor.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which of the following are organized inside the Registry’s root keys? (Select two.)
explanation: The Registry’s root keys are further organized into subkeys and values. Each value holds one setting with a name, a data type, and data.
whyWrong: The Registry has keys and subkeys, not subfolders.
Objects belong to Performance Monitor, not to the Registry.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 4
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Registry Editor).

stem: Which of the following root keys contains the data for a system’s non-user-specific configurations?
explanation: The system’s non-user-specific configurations are stored in the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE root key of the Registry. It holds the hardware, software, and security settings that apply to every user.
whyWrong: HKEY_USERS holds the profiles of each user on the computer, which are user-specific.
HKEY_CURRENT_USER holds the settings of the user who is logged on.
HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT holds file associations and COM class data, not the general system settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Registry Editor).

stem: How do you open the Registry Editor from the command prompt?
explanation: From the command prompt, you use regedit to open the Registry Editor. The command regedit.exe opens the graphical Registry Editor.
whyWrong: The reg command edits the Registry from the command line but does not open Registry Editor.
regeditor is not a valid Windows command.
rgstry is not a valid Windows command.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 7
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Registry Editor, regedit.exe).

stem: Sven calls the Help Desk to complain that a certain program has locked up. In such a scenario, which tool should you use to force the program to quit and how do you open the tool?
options: Task Manager; press ctrl-shift-esc to open
Task Manager; press ctrl-t-m to open
Performance Monitor; open in Administrative Tools
Performance Monitor; press ctrl-p-m to open
explanation: The Task Manager is the tool you need to use to force a program to close in Windows. The easiest way to access the tool is to press ctrl-shift-esc simultaneously.
whyWrong: ctrl-t-m is not a shortcut for Task Manager.
Performance Monitor tracks counters; it cannot end a program that has locked up.
Performance Monitor cannot end programs, and ctrl-p-m is not a shortcut for it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 8

stem: What tool enables you to track resource usage by PID, rather than a text string, for easier problem diagnosis?
explanation: Resource Monitor organizes everything by PID (process ID) number. Using PIDs often can facilitate diagnosis of problems, because tracking a four-digit number is much easier than remembering a text string.
whyWrong: Performance Monitor tracks objects and counters, not a list organized by PID.
PID Monitor is not a Windows tool.
Task Manager can show PIDs, but Resource Monitor is the tool that organizes everything by PID.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 9

stem: If a user has never used Task Manager before, which tab will be selected when it opens?
explanation: If a user hasn’t previously changed to Task Manager’s More details view, it will open in the Fewer details view (which has no tabs). The user selects More details to see the tabs such as Processes, Performance, and Startup.
whyWrong: The Details tab is not shown until the user switches to the More details view.
More details is a view option, not a tab.
The Processes tab appears only after the user switches to the More details view.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1102 1.3; describes the Windows 10 Task Manager, and the Windows 11 Task Manager opens with a navigation pane, mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Task Manager).

stem: What tool enables you to select the programs and services that load when Windows starts?
explanation: The Task Manager enables you to select the programs and services that load when Windows starts. (System Configuration used to do this, but it now redirects you to the Task Manager.)
whyWrong: System Configuration once did this, but its Startup tab now sends you to Task Manager.
msconfig opens System Configuration, whose Startup tab now sends you to Task Manager.
Task Scheduler runs tasks on triggers; it is not where you choose startup programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 1

stem: What tool enables you to run a maintenance script based on specific conditions on Windows?
explanation: Task Scheduler enables you to set up a maintenance task that will run when certain triggers occur and specified conditions are met. Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) is an MMC snap-in.
whyWrong: Task Manager shows and ends running programs; it does not run scripts on conditions.
System Configuration sets boot and startup options; it does not schedule tasks.
msconfig opens System Configuration, which does not schedule tasks.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 2

stem: What does System Information do?
options: Provides you with a report about the hardware resources, components, and software environment in your computer
Enables you to select which programs and services start when Windows boots up
Enables you to schedule hard drive defragmentation, chkdsk scans, and other computer tasks
Enables you to perform automatic custom backups of your files and settings
explanation: System Information gives you a wide variety of information about your system. You open it with msinfo32.exe; it shows hardware resources, components, and the software environment.
whyWrong: Choosing startup programs is a job for Task Manager or System Configuration, not System Information.
Scheduling tasks is a job for Task Scheduler, not System Information.
Automatic backups are a job for File History or backup software, not System Information.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which MMC snap-in allows you to start a program based on a condition?
explanation: Task Scheduler ( taskschd.msc ) will allow you to start a program based on a condition met, such as the computer starting up. The Programs and Features applet is not an MMC snap-in. The Disk Management MMC snap-in allows you to manage the disks attached to the computer. The Group Policy Editor lets you edit the local Group Policy.
whyWrong: Programs and Features removes or changes installed programs; it is not an MMC snap-in and does not schedule tasks.
Disk Management manages disks and volumes; it cannot start a program on a condition.
Group Policy Editor sets policies for the system; it does not run programs on a trigger.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which event log should be checked if you suspect that the computer has rebooted unexpectedly?
explanation: The System event log would contain an entry when the operating system reboots. The Application log is used to log applications installed on the system. The boot log is not a valid log. The Security log contains log information pertaining to the security of objects and files.
whyWrong: The Application log records events from applications, not operating system restarts.
Event Viewer has no standard Boot log, so this is not a valid choice.
The Security log records audit events such as logons and object access, not unexpected restarts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 4

stem: What can you do if a program is not responding to any commands and appears to be locked up?
options: Open the System Control Panel applet and choose Performance to see what process is causing the problem.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Delete to reboot the computer.
Open Task Manager, select the appropriate task, and then click End Task.
explanation: When a program is not responding to any commands, the process must be terminated via the Task Manager. You can end the process by opening the Task Manager, right-clicking the application, and selecting End Task. Viewing the performance will not make the process respond. Adding more memory is not possible without shutting down the computer. Pressing Ctrl+Alt+Delete without any further action will not reboot the computer.
whyWrong: Viewing performance data does not make a frozen program respond or close it.
Adding memory does not fix a program that is already locked up.
Rebooting the whole computer is not needed when Task Manager can end just the frozen task.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 9

stem: Which command will start the Event Viewer snap-in?
explanation: The command eventvwr.msc will start the Event Viewer snap-in. The command eventviewer.exe is not a valid command. The command lusrmgr.msc will start the Local Users and Group snap-in. The command devmgmt.msc will start the Device Manager snap-in.
whyWrong: There is no eventviewer.exe program; Event Viewer starts with eventvwr.msc.
The lusrmgr.msc command opens Local Users and Groups, not Event Viewer.
The devmgmt.msc command opens Device Manager, not Event Viewer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which type of resources do you configure in Device Manager?
explanation: Hardware resources are configured in the Device Manager console. Files and folders and applications are configured in the operating system GUI. Memory is configured in System Properties.
whyWrong: Files and folders are managed in File Explorer, not in Device Manager.
Applications are managed in Settings or Programs and Features, not in Device Manager.
Virtual memory is set in System Properties, not in Device Manager.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 12

stem: What should be periodically done with mechanical hard drives to speed up performance when launching and saving files?
explanation: The mechanical hard drive should be periodically defragmented to arrange concurrent blocks of storage of files so that the hard drive arm does not need to move much when reading and writing files. Solid-state drives (SSDs) do not suffer poor performance from fragmentation, because they have no moving parts. Freeing up space and emptying the Recycle Bin are good ideas but do not contribute to the hard drive's performance as much as defragmenting. Trim is a feature used with SSD drives, where the operating system notifies the SSD device that data blocks have been freed up.
whyWrong: Freeing space helps when a drive is full, but it does not put file blocks back in order.
Emptying the Recycle Bin frees space but does not make file blocks contiguous.
Trim is for solid-state drives; mechanical drives benefit from defragmentation instead.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 13

stem: Which of the following Registry hives contains information about the computer's hardware?
explanation: The HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE Registry hive contains information about the computer's hardware. It is also known as HKLM. HKEY_CURRENT_MACHINE and HKEY_MACHINE are not valid Registry hives. HKEY_RESOURCES was used with Windows 9x operating systems but is no longer used.
whyWrong: HKEY_CURRENT_MACHINE is not a valid Registry hive.
HKEY_MACHINE is not a valid Registry hive.
HKEY_RESOURCES was used only by Windows 9x and is not used today.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 16

stem: Which of the following utilities will rearrange the files on your hard disk to occupy contiguous chunks of space?
explanation: Disk Defragmenter will rearrange blocks of files on a hard drive to create contiguous files and space. Windows File Explorer is used to navigate the filesystem. Scandisk is not a command. Windows Backup allows for file backups.
whyWrong: File Explorer navigates and manages files; it does not rearrange file blocks on the disk.
Scandisk is not a current Windows command; chkdsk checks disks and does not defragment them.
Windows Backup copies files for recovery; it does not make files contiguous.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which tool allows you to report a remote computer's inventory of hardware?
explanation: The msinfo32.exe tool allows for the remote reporting of a computer's hardware. The regedit.exe tool is used to edit the Registry. The msconfig.exe tool is used to change the startup of services and change the boot process. The dxdiag.exe tool is used to diagnose DirectX problems.
whyWrong: The regedit.exe tool edits the Registry; it does not report hardware inventory.
The msconfig.exe tool changes startup services and boot options, not hardware reports.
The dxdiag.exe tool diagnoses DirectX problems; it does not report a remote computer's inventory.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following do you type in the Run prompt to open the Device Manager?
explanation: devmgmt.msc is the Microsoft console window known as Device Manager. mmc opens a new blank Microsoft Management Console. secpol.msc opens the Local Security Policy window. cmd opens the Command Prompt. Device Manager is where you view devices and update, roll back, disable, or uninstall their drivers.
whyWrong: mmc opens a new, empty Microsoft Management Console with no snap-ins loaded.
secpol.msc opens the Local Security Policy console, not Device Manager.
cmd opens the Command Prompt, not the Device Manager console.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of the following would you use to track the percentage of resources being used?
explanation: perfmon.msc (or perfmon.exe) opens the Performance Monitor utility, which is used to graphically track the resources that are being used on a computer, such as CPU and RAM. You could also use Task Manager > Performance to track resource usage (but without the ability to save the data), as well as the Resource Monitor. devmgmt.msc opens the Device Manager. eventvwr.msc opens the Event Viewer. compmgmt.msc opens the Computer Management console window.
whyWrong: devmgmt.msc opens Device Manager, which manages devices and drivers, not resource usage over time.
eventvwr.msc opens Event Viewer, which shows logged events, not the percentage of resources in use.
compmgmt.msc opens Computer Management, a console of several tools, not a resource tracking graph.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Where can a user go to start and stop services in Windows? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: You can start/stop services in Task Manager > Services; in the Services console window (services.msc); and in the PowerShell/Command Prompt by using the net start, net stop, sc start, and sc stop commands. gpedit.msc brings up the Group Policy Editor in Windows.
whyWrong: gpedit.msc opens the Local Group Policy Editor, which sets policies; it does not start or stop services.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which log file in the Event Viewer contains information concerning auditing?
explanation: The Security log contains information about auditing and other security events. The System log contains information about the OS and system files. The Application log contains information about built-in Windows programs and some third-party programs. Local Users and Groups is an administrative tool you can use to add people and systems to the local computer.
whyWrong: The System log records events from the OS and its components, not auditing events.
The Application log records events from programs, not the auditing of security events.
Local Users and Groups is a tool for managing local accounts; it is not an Event Viewer log.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which tool can run particular programs at times designated by the user?
explanation: The Task Scheduler can run particular programs at scheduled times designated by the user. The Services console window enables you to start, stop, and restart services. The Event Viewer is used to find messages about the system, applications, and security developments. The Task Manager is used to analyze the performance of a system and view the applications and services that are running.
whyWrong: The Services console starts, stops, and restarts services; it does not run programs on a schedule.
Event Viewer shows logged system, application, and security events; it does not schedule programs.
Task Manager shows and ends running apps and processes; it does not run programs at set times.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A technician sees a device with a white circle and a black downward-pointing arrow next to its name in Device Manager. What does this mean?
options: The device has a missing or outdated driver.
explanation: Device Manager uses certain symbols that appear next to a device’s name to offer informational details about a particular error condition with a device. A white circle with a black downward-pointing arrow means that a device is disabled. A yellow triangle with a black exclamation point means a device is in a problem state, usually related to a missing or outdated driver. A white circle with a blue question mark means that Windows cannot identify device, most often because of a missing driver or incompatible device driver.
whyWrong: A missing or outdated driver shows as a yellow triangle with an exclamation point, not a down arrow.
An unidentified device shows a blue question mark; the down arrow means the device is disabled.
A working device shows no symbol next to its name; the down arrow marks a disabled device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: A client calls you in a panic after installing a new graphics card driver that isn’t working properly. What do you suggest the client do to restore to the previous driver that worked?
options: Select Device Manager > Roll Back Driver.
Select File > Add/Remove Snap-in, click Group Policy Object Editor, and then click Add.
Open the Run prompt and type perfmon.msc.
explanation: If a device fails after updating its driver, you can roll back to the previously installed driver that worked using the Device Manager Roll Back Driver feature. If you want to add the Group Policy Editor to your MMC, go to File > Add/Remove Snap-in, click Group Policy Object Editor, and then click Add. Going to Run and typing perfmon.msc opens the Performance Monitor.
whyWrong: Update Driver installs a newer driver; it does not return to the driver that worked before.
Adding the Group Policy Object Editor snap-in to an MMC does not change a device driver.
perfmon.msc opens Performance Monitor to track resource usage; it does not restore an old driver.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: You are preparing to troubleshoot a system that is having some driver issues. Which of the following tools should you use to configure the system to boot safely?
explanation: Use the System Configuration utility (msconfig.exe) to configure the system to boot safely by going to the Boot tab and checking the Safe boot option. When it is configured as Minimal (the default), the system will boot with a minimal set of drivers and programs; however, several other options are listed there. Make sure you go through the Windows utilities and all the tabs. Know what everything does!
whyWrong: Event Viewer shows logged events that help find a cause, but it cannot set the system to boot safely.
Resource Monitor shows live CPU, memory, disk, and network use; it has no boot settings.
msinfo32 shows a report about hardware and software; it cannot change how the system boots.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You have been tasked with repairing a magnetic-based hard drive that is running sluggishly. Which of the following tools should you use to fix the problem? (Select the BEST answer.)
explanation: Use the Optimize Drives (Disk Defragmenter) utility. This utility attempts to defragment the drive and place the files in a contiguous order so that the hard disk drive (HDD) doesn’t behave so sluggishly. Of course, there could be other causes for the poor hard drive performance, such as too many applications at startup, malware, capacity issues, and so on.
whyWrong: Disk Management configures partitions and volumes; it does not defragment a slow hard drive.
msinfo32.exe shows information about hardware and software; it does not repair drive performance.
A mount point is a drive mapped to an empty folder; it is not a tool that fixes performance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: What is HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE considered to be?
explanation: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE is one of the five visible hives that can be modified from within the Registry Editor. This hive stores hardware and software settings that are specific to the computer (for example TCP/IP settings).
whyWrong: A Registry entry is a value inside a key; HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE is a top-level hive that holds many keys.
A subkey sits under another key; HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE is a top-level hive, not a subkey.
A string value is one type of data stored in a key; HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE is a whole hive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What must you do FIRST to a basic disk to create spanned, striped, mirrored, or RAID 5 volumes in Disk Management?
explanation: Convert the disk to dynamic. Once this is done, the volume can be extended, shrunk, or split. You initialize a drive if it is not recognized by Windows immediately—for example, if it is a new or foreign drive that has been installed to a computer that already had Windows functioning.
whyWrong: Extending a volume grows it into free space; on a basic disk this does not make a spanned or RAID 5 volume.
Shrinking a volume frees space on the disk; it does not enable spanned, striped, or RAID 5 volumes.
Split is not the step that enables these volume types; the disk must first be converted to dynamic.
Initializing prepares a new or foreign disk for Windows; it does not allow spanned or RAID 5 volumes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: In Disk Manager, which partition contains the operating system?
explanation: A partition needs to be set to active if you want to install an operating system to it. A system must have one active partition. The active partition contains the operating system (Windows) that starts when you turn on the system. Basic disks can have only simple volumes or regular partitions/logical drives. If you want to create a spanned, striped, mirrored, or RAID 5 volume, you need to convert the disk to dynamic.
whyWrong: A spanned volume joins space from several dynamic disks; it is not the partition that boots the OS.
A striped volume spreads data across dynamic disks for speed; it is not marked to boot the OS.
A mirrored volume copies data to two dynamic disks for redundancy; it does not mark the OS partition.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 5
note: Book wording kept: "Disk Manager" means Disk Management and "Stripped" means striped. The active partition is an MBR concept.

stem: A malware infection has spread across a company’s network via several USB storage devices. The support team must identify a method to prevent users from using storage devices that connect to USB ports. The team has been notified that this must be done quickly with minimum disruption to users. Which of the following is the BEST way for the support team to address this requirement?
options: Push a group policy to all users
explanation: USB access must be stopped quickly on multiple workstations. A domain-based group policy would be the most effective way to push out this security setting. For an immediate update, the support team can run invoke-gpupdate remotely or use the Group Policy Management Console (GPMC) to update multiple workstations at the same time with minimal disruption.
whyWrong: A local security policy must be set on each workstation one at a time, which is too slow here.
A login script works only after every user logs off and back on, which disrupts users.
An acceptable use policy only states expected behavior; it does not technically block USB storage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Group Policy Editor). Group Policy deployment, not a command-line tool question.

stem: Prior to beginning an online certification exam, a user must run an agent to manage the online exam. The agent reports that an application named “Dell Diagnostics” is preventing the online exam from starting. How can the user quickly identify the background application and end the task?
options: Go to Task Manager | Processes and End task
Go to Task Manager | Startup and disable the startup process
Go to Task Manager | Performance and End task
Run Registry Editor and modify Computer\HKEY_CURRENT_USER
explanation: Task Manager’s Processes tab will display all running applications, background processes, and Windows processes. The unwanted application or process can be terminated using the End task option. The task cannot be ended from either the Startup or Performance tabs of Task Manager. Directly editing the registry should never be the first choice for ending a task as it may have unpredictable outcomes.
whyWrong: Disabling a startup item only affects the next boot and does not stop the process running now.
The Performance tab shows resource graphs and has no option to end a task.
Editing the registry is risky and does not end a running process.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: A technician is working on a computer when the PC suddenly experiences a Windows blue screen and restarts, apparently normally. To resolve the issue, the technician needs to determine which error message was displayed during the blue screen event. Which of the following should the technician use to help troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: The reason for the blue screen error will be logged in one of the event viewer logs, and if it was a hardware driver issue, it will be found in the Windows System log. SFC can be used to ensure Windows system files are validated but will not display the event details. msconfig can be used to troubleshoot the boot process and could be configured to boot into safe mode if there is an unstable driver. regedit is the registry editor, which is not useful in this case. msinfo32 (system information) can be useful as a support tool for gathering configuration information but will not store details about the blue screen event.
whyWrong: sfc checks protected system files and does not show the details of a past blue screen.
msconfig changes boot options and does not record stop error messages.
The Registry Editor changes configuration values and does not log blue screen events.
System Information lists hardware and software details but does not keep the stop error message.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: A recently terminated employee had made several undocumented changes to a manager’s laptop computer. These changes are preventing Office 365 applications from receiving updates in a timely manner and have halted the automated disk defragmentation service. In order to ensure these services run automatically, which tool will BEST remediate the problems?
explanation: Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) is the tool for configuring background tasks. Any settings that have been changed can be seen here. Device Manager (devmgmt.msc) will allow a technician to troubleshoot hardware. Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) and Performance Monitor (perfmon.msc) can be useful for identifying performance bottlenecks. Certificate Manager (certmgr.msc) is used to manage local user and computer certificates as well as trusted certificate authorities.
whyWrong: Device Manager troubleshoots hardware devices and drivers, not scheduled update or defrag tasks.
Performance Monitor measures system performance and cannot set tasks to run automatically.
Certificate Manager manages certificates and has nothing to do with scheduled maintenance.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: Ann, a payroll manager, has complained of poor system performance on her company laptop computer. Applications are running slowly during certain parts of the day and occasionally in the evening, when she stays late to finish a task. The support technician allocated the ticket would like to monitor Ann’s computer in an effort to identify the problem. Which of the following tools should the technician use to BEST analyze the computer’s behavior?
explanation: Performance Monitor can be configured to run a schedule, capturing detailed performance data during specific times of the day. Computer Management allows a technician to use multiple administrative tools on a local or remote workstation (user and group management services). Event Viewer logs can be useful to identify faulting applications or drivers. Task Manager shows events in real time and would require the support technician to interactively monitor the computer (it is not as convenient as Performance Monitor).
whyWrong: Computer Management groups several admin tools but does not capture performance data on a schedule.
Event Viewer records errors and warnings, not the resource usage needed to find slowdowns.
Task Manager shows only live data, so the technician would have to watch it at the right time.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: An employee returns from a six-month assignment working with a business partner. A computer technician would like to check whether the hardware vendor’s BIOS updates were installed on the employee’s laptop during the six-month period. Which tool would BEST display this information?
explanation: System Information (msinfo32.exe) will display a comprehensive inventory of hardware, software, drivers, and so on. Resource Monitor (resmon.exe) shows system and network performance data in real time. System Configuration (msconfig.exe) allows configuration of the boot process. Registry Editor (regedit.exe) will not be the easiest tool with which to find this information.
whyWrong: Resource Monitor shows live CPU, disk, memory, and network usage, not BIOS version details.
System Configuration changes boot and startup options and does not show BIOS information.
The Registry Editor holds the data in hard-to-read keys, so it is not the easiest tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: A service desk technician is allocated a ticket when a user’s Windows workstation is running slowly. The computer boots up slowly and has long delays when executing large files. After checking the local hard disk, it appears to be near capacity. The technician needs to free up space and optimize access times for large files. Which two commands will BEST address this requirement? (Choose two.)
explanation: Disk Cleanup will identify files that are not needed and can be removed, and by defragmenting the hard drive, the technician will optimize the file fragments for large files. The defrag will actually move data so that large files occupy sequential clusters on the drive surface (which is not necessary for SSD drives). Booting the computer in safe mode is not necessary as the system is not unstable, just underperforming. Rebooting the computer may be necessary when configuration changes or new drivers require it. There is no reason to install any device drivers as there are no reported issues with hardware drivers.
whyWrong: Safe mode helps with an unstable system, and this one is only slow.
A reboot does not free disk space or reduce file fragmentation.
There are no reported hardware or driver problems, so installing drivers would not help.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: Due to a misconfigured workstation build template, workstations used by the sales team have a very small amount of storage space available. Technicians would like to view the currently allocated space for the main operating system drive and, if possible, extend the size of the drive. What graphical-based tool would be BEST for this task?
explanation: Disk Management will allow a disk to be extended if there is unused free space. Diskpart would allow the disk to be extended; however, it runs at the command prompt and, thus, is not graphical. Device Manager displays information about controllers and disk drives but does not allow the disk to be resized. Disk Cleanup would not allow the disk partition to be re-sized.
whyWrong: Diskpart can extend a volume, but it is a command-line tool, not a graphical one.
Device Manager shows disk drives and controllers but cannot resize a volume.
Disk Cleanup deletes unneeded files and cannot change the size of a partition.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: A support technician is troubleshooting a helpdesk ticket raised by a sales executive. Applications that load on Windows startup are resulting in a wait time of nearly five minutes before the user is able to use the computer. What can be done to help the user avoid this long wait time?
options: Use the System Configuration | Startup options to disable startup applications
Delete entries listed under the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
Use Task Manager to disable all startup tasks currently set as enabled, then reboot the computer to ensure the issue has been resolved
Open Task Manager | Startup and identify applications with High start-up impact. Disable these apps causing excessive boot times on startup.
explanation: The recommended tool to identify poorly performing start-up applications and disable them is to use the Task Manager. Using the System Configuration | Startup options to disable startup applications is only supported on older versions of Windows. Directly editing registry keys is not usually the best approach, and in this case, you would not know which startup apps to disable. Manually disabling all startup tasks currently listed as enabled and rebooting to check for issue resolution at startup is not necessary, as the startup impact is measured by Windows and is better addressed by using the Task Manager Startup tab.
whyWrong: The Startup options in System Configuration apply only to older Windows versions; newer ones send you to Task Manager.
Deleting registry Run entries is risky, and it does not show which apps slow the startup.
Disabling every startup task is unnecessary, because Task Manager already measures each app's startup impact.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives). The book splits the registry option across two lines (B and C); they are joined into one option, and the explanation's 'answer E' is reworded.

stem: A user from the human resources department raises a support ticket. The reason for the ticket is their desktop computer has been running slowly. The user reports that there have been no changes made to the PC. Which of the following tools should the support technician use to determine the cause of the speed reduction?
options: The Performance tab in Task Manager
explanation: The Task Manager’s Performance tab will give the technician real-time information on the system’s all-around performance and enable the technician to identify obvious bottlenecks. Task Scheduler will allow heavy load tasks to be rescheduled but won’t show performance data. Windows Memory Diagnostic is a tool that performs a health check on physical memory (for example, to determine whether there are any cells on a RAM module that are corrupt). Disk Defragmenter could be run in response to high disk latency, but it will not show actual disk performance information.
whyWrong: Task Scheduler can reschedule heavy tasks but does not show performance data.
Windows Memory Diagnostic tests RAM for faults and does not show what slows the system now.
Disk Defragmenter optimizes files on a disk but does not report system performance.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: A department manager was accidentally assigned privileges that allowed them to make several unauthorized changes to their company laptop. One of the changes made was to add additional certificates to their laptop’s Trusted Root Certificate Authorities store. The company is a government contractor, and these new certificates are not trusted as they do not meet government compliance regulations. How can a support technician ensure these certificate authorities will not be trusted by applications run on the manager’s laptop?
options: Remove the certificates from the Trusted Root Certificate Authorities store using certmgr.msc on the laptop
Remove the certificates from the Trusted Root Certificate Authorities store using regedit.msc on the laptop
Remove the certificates from the Trusted Root Certificate Authorities store using devmgmt.msc on the laptop
Request the external certificate authorities put all of their certificates on a certificate revocation list (CRL)
explanation: certmgr.msc can be used to manage certificates for the computer, user, and system accounts. The Trusted Root Certificate Authorities store is populated with trusted root certificate authorities. This list can be modified manually or centrally using group policy. Removing the certificates from the store using regedit.msc is not a good choice, as this may lead to unpredictable results. Device Manager (devmgmt.msc) does not allow the management of certificates on the laptop.
whyWrong: There is no regedit.msc, and editing certificate data in the registry can cause unpredictable results.
Device Manager manages hardware devices and cannot remove certificates.
A revocation list is published by the authority that issued a certificate, so the company cannot make it do this.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.3 question 10
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Windows features and tools in the old objectives).

stem: You just installed a new updated driver for a network interface card (NIC). Now you want to test its data transfer rate. What tool should you use to run your test?
explanation: Use Performance Monitor (Run > perfmon.exe) to analyze a device. In this example, you can find out how many bits per second the NIC can transfer (that is, the data transfer rate). You can also use this tool to monitor all of the other devices (objects) on the system and save and report on those findings in a variety of ways. Another useful tool is Resource Monitor.
whyWrong: Device Manager installs, removes, and rolls back drivers; it cannot measure the transfer rate of the NIC.
Local Security Policy enables or disables security rules on the computer; it does not test devices.
System Information shows a summary of hardware and software, but it cannot run performance tests.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 33

stem: Which Windows utility can be used to see which user is currently logged on?
explanation: In Windows, the Task Manager Users tab shows any currently logged-on users and their status. The Task Manager shows the percentage of resources that are being used by each user.
whyWrong: msconfig changes boot settings and startup services; it does not show which users are logged on.
Disk Management works with drives, partitions, and formatting, not with logged-on users.
Windows Tools is a folder of administrative tools and gives no quick view of the users that are logged on.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 36

stem: Which of the following tools allows you to change the number of CPU cores that Windows uses?
explanation: The System Configuration utility (msconfig.exe) can be used to change the total number of CPU cores used by Windows.
