You can find this by going to the Boot tab and clicking the Advanced options button. From there, check the Number of processors checkbox and select the number of CPU cores (or the actual number of CPUs if you have more than one). This is usually done to troubleshoot the CPU or Windows; in most cases, Windows will use all CPU cores available to it by default.
whyWrong: Performance Monitor can show each core in real time, but it cannot change how many cores Windows uses.
dxdiag analyzes the DirectX audio and video components; it has no setting for CPU cores.
Task Manager shows the load on each core, but it cannot set the number of cores Windows boots with.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 54

stem: A user notifies a technician about a sluggish computer performance. Which of the following tools can assist the technician in identifying the underlying cause of the issue?
explanation: When troubleshooting a slow computer, the Performance Monitor tool is a valuable asset for a technician. Performance Monitor allows the technician to monitor various system resources, such as CPU usage, memory utilization, disk activity, and network performance. By analyzing the data collected by Performance Monitor, the technician can identify resource bottlenecks or abnormal behavior that may be causing the slow performance.
whyWrong: A third-party system optimizer changes settings but does not give detailed data on the cause of the slowdown.
Registry Editor edits the registry and does not measure system performance.
Task Scheduler runs tasks at set times or events and does not monitor resource use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 22
note: 220-1102 1.3 (MMC snap-ins: Performance Monitor); mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (MMC snap-in: perfmon.msc).

stem: Which of the following options would a technician utilize to enable automatic application boot-up upon logging into a conference room computer? (Choose two.)
explanation: To achieve automatic application boot-up upon logging in to a conference room computer, a technician would employ two specific options. First, utilizing the Task Scheduler feature allows them to schedule the application to launch automatically upon user login. Second, the Startup Folder option enables the technician to add a shortcut of the application to the system’s designated startup folder, ensuring it initiates during the login process.
whyWrong: Windows Explorer manages files and folders; it has no setting that launches an application at logon.
System Information shows a summary of the system and cannot start applications at logon.
Programs and Features installs, repairs, and removes programs; it does not start them at logon.
Device Manager manages hardware devices and drivers, not the applications that start at logon.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 46
note: 220-1102 1.3 (Task Manager: Startup; Task Scheduler); mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (Task Manager: Startup; MMC snap-in: taskschd.msc).

stem: A support technician installed an antivirus application on a user’s home computer. The user later reports that the computer has been running slowly, with the hard drive activity light constantly solid. What should be the FIRST step to address this issue?
options: Check Services in Control Panel to identify any overutilization of system resources
Monitor performance using Performance Monitor to analyze resource utilization
Run System File Checker to verify the integrity of Windows files for any modifications
Review Event Viewer logs to identify any errors or issues
explanation: To address the reported slow performance and constant solid activity light on the hard drive, the FIRST step should be to use Performance Monitor to analyze resource utilization. This tool provides real-time monitoring and insights into the computer’s performance, allowing you to identify any specific processes or applications that might be causing the slowdown.
whyWrong: The Services console manages and configures services; it does not measure resource use.
System File Checker repairs Windows system files, which is not related to the high disk activity.
Event Viewer shows logged errors but does not show the live resource use that causes the slowdown.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 56
note: 220-1102 1.3 (MMC snap-ins: Performance Monitor); mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (MMC snap-in: perfmon.msc).

stem: A user encounters connection issues when attempting to use a third-party USB adapter. Which of the following tools should a technician employ to address this problem?
explanation: To troubleshoot connection issues with a third-party USB adapter, a technician should utilize the devmgmt.msc tool. devmgmt.msc, also known as Device Manager, allows technicians to view and manage hardware devices connected to a computer. By opening Device Manager, the technician can verify if the USB adapter is recognized by the system and check for any associated driver issues. They can then proceed to update or reinstall the appropriate drivers, ensuring compatibility and resolving any connection problems.
whyWrong: taskschd.msc opens Task Scheduler, which runs scheduled tasks and does not manage device drivers.
eventvwr.msc opens Event Viewer, which shows logs but cannot update or reinstall the adapter driver.
diskmgmt.msc opens Disk Management, which manages drives and partitions, not USB adapters.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 70
note: 220-1102 1.3 (MMC snap-ins: Device Manager); mapped to 220-1202 1.4 (MMC snap-in: devmgmt.msc).

stem: A user says her computer has started in Safe Mode every day since a technician worked on it last week. Which tool should the technician use to BEST fix this?
explanation: Safe boot set on the Boot tab of System Configuration stays on for every restart. Setting the General tab back to Normal startup (and clearing Safe boot) returns the computer to a normal start.
whyWrong: Disk Cleanup removes temporary files; it does not change how Windows boots.
System Information only shows hardware and software details and cannot change any setting.
Resource Monitor shows live resource use; it has no boot settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

stem: A technician installs a second drive in a Windows 11 PC. The drive shows in the UEFI setup, but File Explorer does not show it. Which tool BEST lets the technician make the drive usable?
explanation: A new secondary drive must be initialized, given a volume, and formatted before File Explorer shows it. Disk Management does all three in one graphical tool.
whyWrong: Device Manager manages device drivers, but it cannot initialize, partition, or format a drive.
Optimize Drives defragments existing volumes; it cannot create a volume on a new drive.
Performance Monitor tracks counters such as disk activity, but it does not set up drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 33: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part II

stem: A user's computer takes a long time to become usable after sign-in, and many tray icons load at startup. The user wants some of the programs to stop starting automatically. Which action is BEST?
options: Disable the unneeded programs on the Startup apps tab of Task Manager
End the programs on the Processes tab of Task Manager
Sign off the other users on the Users tab of Task Manager
Delete the programs' entries from the Event Viewer logs
explanation: The Startup apps tab of Task Manager shows each startup app's status and its startup impact. Disabling an app there keeps it from starting each time the computer starts.
whyWrong: Ending a process stops it only until the next restart, when it starts again.
Signing off other users frees their resources but does not change which programs start at sign-in.
Event Viewer logs record events; clearing them has no effect on which programs start.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 32: Microsoft Operating System Features and Tools, Part I

stem: Jaime wishes to check her hard drive for errors. What tool should she use in Windows 11?
explanation: Error checking is used to check a drive for errors. Error checking is on the Tools tab of the drive properties and runs the same checks as chkdsk.
whyWrong: FDISK was an old MS-DOS partitioning tool and is not in Windows 11.
Format erases a volume to prepare it for use; it does not check it for errors.
Disk Management manages partitions and volumes but does not check a drive for errors.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 1.2; error checking is not a listed 220-1202 topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (chkdsk).

stem: Which commands pause after displaying a screen’s worth of directory contents? (Choose two.)
explanation: The ls | more and dir /p commands in UNIX and Windows, respectively, pause a long listing at the end of the page. The more command can also take the output of any other command through a pipe.
whyWrong: dir p lists items named p; the switch needs a slash to pause the listing.
Windows has no less command, so dir | less does not work at the Windows prompt.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which Windows command is functionally equivalent to the Linux ls command?
explanation: The Windows dir command accomplishes a similar function to the Linux ls command. Both commands list the files and folders in the current directory.
whyWrong: command is not a Windows command that lists directory contents.
copy copies files; it does not list the contents of a directory.
dd is a UNIX tool that copies raw data; it is not a Windows command.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Of the following, which BEST describes the function of the Windows gpresult command?
options: Lists all recently updated group policies
Lists the group policies applied to a user
Lists all changes to a user’s group policies since the last refresh
Lists any and all conflicting group policies
explanation: The gpresult command in Windows lists group policies applied to a user. It shows the Resultant Set of Policy for a user or computer.
whyWrong: gpresult shows the policies that apply now, not a list of recently updated policies.
gpresult does not list the changes since the last policy refresh.
gpresult does not list conflicting group policies.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 9

stem: How do you run a command at the Windows command prompt with administrative privileges?
options: Enter an elevated username and password at the command prompt.
Right-click a command-prompt shortcut and then select Run as PowerUser.
Right-click a command-prompt shortcut and then select Run as administrator.
The cmd command only runs with administrator privileges.
explanation: To run a command at the Windows command prompt with administrative privileges, right-click a command-prompt shortcut and then select Run as administrator. Some commands, such as sfc, need an elevated prompt to run.
whyWrong: The command prompt does not accept an elevated username and password typed at the prompt.
Windows has no Run as PowerUser option.
cmd runs with standard user rights unless it is started as administrator.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1102 1.2; running elevated is not a separate topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (OS management).

stem: Steven’s Windows system can’t connect to the Internet, and he comes to you, his PC tech, for help. You figure out that it’s a DHCP problem. What program should you run to troubleshoot his DHCP problem from the client side?
explanation: You should run ipconfig, or more specifically ipconfig /release and then ipconfig /renew to get a new IP address if a DHCP server is available for Steven’s Windows system. This typically resolves most DHCP client-side problems. ifconfig is the program used by macOS and Linux systems for this task. Neither config nor dhcp is valid.
whyWrong: ifconfig is the macOS and Linux tool, not the Windows tool.
config is not a valid command.
dhcp /review is not a valid command.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 1

stem: What command would you use to view the path taken by an Ethernet packet?
explanation: The tracert command in Windows traces the path a data packet takes to get to its destination. macOS and Linux use the traceroute utility for similar purposes. Each line of the output is one router hop on the way to the destination.
whyWrong: ping tests whether a host replies; it does not show the path the packet takes.
ipconfig shows the local IP configuration, not the path to a destination.
nslookup queries DNS servers; it does not show the path a packet takes.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which of the following is the correct net syntax for discovering which network shares on a particular server are mapped on your computer?
explanation: To see the network shares mapped on your computer, use net view \\fileserver. The net use command maps a drive letter to a share once you know its name.
whyWrong: net needs a subcommand; net \\fileserver is not valid syntax.
net has no map subcommand; net use maps drives.
net share manages the shares on the local computer, not those of a server.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 3
note: 220-1102 1.2; net view is not on 220-1202 (net use is), mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (network commands).

stem: Which command can be used to display the cached NetBIOS names for a Windows system?
explanation: nslookup and dig only work with DNS, not NetBIOS. nbtstat -A is for querying a remote system’s name, but nbtstat -c displays the cached names. NetBIOS names are the older Windows computer names used on local networks.
whyWrong: nslookup queries DNS and does not show NetBIOS names.
dig is a DNS tool and does not show NetBIOS names.
nbtstat -A queries the name table of a remote system by IP address, not the local cache.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 1.2; nbtstat is not on 220-1202, mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (network commands).

stem: What command-line utility would you run to show a list of network computers?
explanation: Use the net view command to show a list of computers on the network. With a computer name added, net view lists the shares on that computer.
whyWrong: net send sent messages to other users and has been removed from Windows.
show net_servers is not a valid Windows command.
net use maps or lists connections to shared resources, not the computers on the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 8
note: 220-1102 1.2; net view is not on 220-1202 (net use is), mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (network commands).

stem: What option often enables you to diagnose TCP/IP errors such as connection problems?
explanation: You can often use the ping command to diagnose TCP/IP problems. The ping command sends ICMP echo requests and reports whether replies come back and how long they take.
whyWrong: FTP transfers files; it is not a tool for diagnosing connections.
QoS gives some traffic priority; it is not a diagnostic tool.
APIPA gives an address when DHCP fails; it is a sign of a problem, not a test.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 8

stem: While troubleshooting a client computer, you decide to obtain a new IP address from the DHCP server. After releasing the existing address, which command do you use to get new IP information from the DHCP server?
explanation: The ipconfig command is perhaps the most-used utility in troubleshooting and network configuration. The ipconfig /renew command will send a query to the DHCP server asking it to resend and renew all DHCP information. For a more detailed look at the ipconfig command, type ipconfig /? at the command prompt. The ip command is used with Linux and macOS clients. There is no /refresh or /start switch for these commands.
whyWrong: The ipconfig command has no /refresh switch.
The ip command is used on Linux and macOS, and it has no /release switch.
The ip command is used on Linux and macOS, and it has no /start switch.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 14
note: From a Core 1 chapter; ipconfig is a 220-1202 1.5 command-line tool.

stem: Which of the following can you type in the Start menu in Windows to open a command prompt? (Choose two.)
explanation: You can open a command prompt by typing cmd or command in the Start menu. The command prompt utility will pop up in the search results. Run is not a command; it is a dialog box. Open is not a command; it is an operating system action.
whyWrong: Run is a dialog box opened with Windows key+R; typing it does not open a command prompt.
Open is an operating system action, not a program name that starts the command prompt.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which utility can be used to schedule a remote shutdown?
explanation: The shutdown utility can be used to schedule a remote shutdown—for example, shutdown /t 60 /m \\computer. The taskmgr utility is used to view tasks, kill is used to kill processes, and netstat is used to view network statistics and activity.
whyWrong: Task Manager shows and ends tasks on the local computer; it cannot schedule a remote shutdown.
The kill command ends processes; it does not shut down a remote computer.
The netstat command shows network connections and statistics; it cannot shut down a computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which command will allow copying of all data to include NTFS permissions?
explanation: The robocopy command will copy all data and will include NTFS permission to remain intact. The xcopy and copy commands will copy files from a source folder to a destination folder but will not copy NTFS permissions. The chkdsk command is used to check the integrity of the NTFS filesystem.
whyWrong: The xcopy command copies files and folders but does not keep NTFS permissions.
The copy command copies files but does not keep NTFS permissions.
The chkdsk command checks a file system for errors; it does not copy data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 5

stem: Which command is used to measure packet loss as a packet travels to a destination address?
explanation: The pathping command will measure the packet loss at each router as the packet travels to the destination address; it combines the ping and tracert commands. The ping command will return a single destination's response time. The nslookup command is used to resolve DNS addresses. The tracert command allows you to see how a packet travels to its destination.
whyWrong: The ping command reports response time to a single destination, not loss at each router.
The nslookup command queries DNS; it does not measure packet loss.
The tracert command lists the routers on the path but does not measure packet loss at each hop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 9

stem: Which command will allow you to check a volume for corruption?
explanation: The chkdsk command is used to check a volume for corruption, as well as attempt to repair the corruption. The diskpart command allows you to create, modify, and view volumes on a disk. The format command allows you to format a filesystem on a volume. The sfc command is used to fix corrupted files but not volume corruption.
whyWrong: The diskpart command creates, changes, and views partitions and volumes; it does not check for corruption.
The format command creates a new file system on a volume and erases its data.
The sfc command repairs corrupted Windows system files, not volume file system errors.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 11

stem: You are troubleshooting a network issue and need to verify the path packets take to a destination. Which command should you use?
explanation: The tracert command shows the path packets take to a destination, helping to identify where delays or failures occur. The ping command checks connectivity but not the path. nslookup resolves DNS names but does not trace the path. netstat shows network connections and ports but not the path.
whyWrong: The ping command checks whether a host responds but does not show the path.
The nslookup command resolves DNS names; it does not trace the path.
The netstat command lists connections and ports; it does not show the route to a host.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 15

stem: Which command is used to identify ports in use by applications and the operating system?
explanation: The netstat command can be used to view ports in use by the operating system and network applications communicating with the network. The ipconfig command allows you to see the current IP address and DNS information for the operating system. pathping allows you to view packet loss along the path to a destination IP address. The nslookup command is used to resolve DNS records.
whyWrong: The ipconfig command shows the IP address and DNS settings, not the ports in use.
The pathping command measures packet loss along a path, not local ports.
The nslookup command queries DNS records, not ports in use.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which command can copy multiple files and entire directory trees?
explanation: robocopy can copy an entire drive of information with just one command (including switches). xcopy could also do the job, but robocopy takes its place.
whyWrong: copy copies one or more files but cannot copy whole directory trees with their subfolders.
cut is not a Windows command-line command; it is a clipboard action in graphical apps.
paste is a clipboard action in graphical apps, not a command that copies directory trees.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which command determines whether protected system files have been overwritten and replaces those files with the original version?
explanation: sfc determines whether system files have been overwritten and replaces those files with the original versions. chkdsk can check for errors and fix some errors, but it cannot work with system files. md is the command used to make a directory. xcopy is used to copy large amounts of data to a new location.
whyWrong: chkdsk checks a volume for file system errors and bad sectors; it does not restore protected system files.
md makes a new directory; it does not check or replace system files.
xcopy copies files and folders to a new location; it does not verify protected system files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You need to assign drive letters and make a partition active from the Command Prompt. Which of the following will allow you to perform these activities?
explanation: diskpart is the command-line counterpart of Disk Management. From the DISKPART> prompt, you can create, delete, and extend volumes; assign drive letters; make a partition active; and so on. The format command is used to format storage media to a particular file system, such as NTFS, FAT, or FAT32. defrag is the command-line version of the Disk Defragmenter; these tools help make the files on a drive contiguous instead of fragmented.
whyWrong: Disk Management can do these tasks, but it is a graphical console, not a Command Prompt tool.
format writes a file system such as NTFS to a volume; it does not assign letters or set a partition active.
defrag makes the files on a drive contiguous; it does not assign drive letters or set partitions active.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You have been tasked with bringing the policies of a Windows 11 computer up to date. You won’t be able to log off and back on, and you must use the Command Prompt. Which of the following tools should you use?
explanation: You should use gpupdate to bring the Windows policies up to date without requiring the admin to log off and on again. The shutdown command is used to turn off or restart a computer. rd is used to remove directories. The Local Security Policy is the place where you can go to modify many policy settings (such as the password policy), but it is a graphical tool. To enforce the changes made in the Local Security Policy, use the gpupdate command. winver is used to find out what operating system version you are running.
whyWrong: shutdown turns off or restarts a computer, which the task does not allow; it does not refresh policies.
rd removes directories; it has nothing to do with applying policies.
Local Security Policy is a graphical tool for editing policy settings; it does not refresh them from the command line.
winver shows the Windows version that is running; it does not update policies.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which command is the BEST option for a technician to learn more about the ping command from a Command Prompt?
explanation: For more information about the ping command, you can enter ping /? at a Command Prompt. If you are ever stumped about a particular command, read the help file associated with it. The naming convention for this is [command name] /?. ping help is not a valid command. [command name] /? won’t work unless you enter a valid command followed by a /?. Although Siri will tell you that ping is a computer administration software utility used to test network connectivity, Siri won’t work from a Command Prompt!
whyWrong: ping help is not a valid command; ping treats help as a host name and does not show its help text.
[command name] /? is only the general pattern; it must be typed with a real command name to work.
A voice assistant does not run at a Command Prompt and is not a command-line help method.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which command shows the path of routers between your computer and a web server?
explanation: tracert is used to run a trace between the local system and a remote destination. It shows all routers along the way. ping is used to test connectivity to another system directly. ipconfig displays the Internet Protocol configuration of the local computer. nbtstat shows the name table cache and services running on the system.
whyWrong: ping tests whether a remote host replies; it does not list the routers along the path.
ipconfig shows the local computer's IP configuration; it does not trace a route to a server.
nbtstat shows NetBIOS name tables and sessions; it does not show the routers to a server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You need to map a network drive to a share named data1 on a computer named Jupiter-Server. You want to use the J: drive letter. Which syntax should you use to do this in the Command Prompt?
explanation: You should use the command net use J: \\Jupiter-Server\data1. All the other answers are incorrect. The Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is \\computername\sharename.
whyWrong: This path names the share first and the computer second; a UNC path is \\computername\sharename.
The drive letter needs a colon, and the UNC path must start with two backslashes before the computer name.
The drive letter goes before the UNC path in net use, not after it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 2
note: Options B and D were changed: in the book they differ from A only in backslashes and the colon, which the app's option check treats as the same text. The answer (A) and the explanation are the book's.

stem: A user’s computer is powered on and appears to work properly. However, the user cannot access any wired network resources, printers, or shared drives. In addition, the user cannot access the Internet. Which of the following commands should you use to troubleshoot the problem?
explanation: Of the listed answers, the best one is the ping command. It will help you to decipher what the problem is. However, consider using ipconfig /all before running ping.
whyWrong: netstat lists current connections and ports; with no network access, it shows little that finds the fault.
net use connects to shared folders; it cannot help when the computer reaches no network at all.
nslookup tests DNS name resolution; it does not first show whether the computer reaches the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A customer is unable to access a network share. However, the customer can access email. You analyze the system and confirm that the customer has the correct permissions to access the share. Which command should you use FIRST to troubleshoot the problem?
explanation: Implement the net use command so that you can make the connection to the network share. (Of course, you could also do this in File Explorer, but this chapter is about the command line!) Use nslookup to resolve domain names to IP addresses or to modify DNS servers. Use ipconfig to analyze the system. Use ping to test whether another system is “alive” on the network.
whyWrong: nslookup tests DNS name resolution; the customer reaches email, so name resolution is working.
ipconfig shows the IP configuration, but the network works, since email arrives, so the share needs a connection.
ping tests whether another host replies; it does not connect the customer to the network share.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A customer’s computer running Windows cannot connect to any Internet resources. Which command should you use to ensure that the gateway address of the customer’s computer is on the same network number as the IP address of the client computer? (Select the BEST answer.)
explanation: The ipconfig command displays current TCP/IP network configuration values such as IP address, subnet mask and default gateway. The ipconfig /all command can offer a lot of information that can help you troubleshoot problems. If a user cannot connect to any Internet resources, the reason could be that the gateway address is improperly configured. Remember that the gateway address must be on the same network number as the IP address of the client computer.
whyWrong: ip is the Linux command for network interfaces; it is not the Windows tool for this check.
whoami shows the logged-on user, groups, and privileges, not the gateway or IP address.
pathping traces routes and measures packet loss; it does not show the local gateway and subnet settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A network engineer must troubleshoot a section of a business network in which marketing users cannot access printers, e-mail, or websites. The network infrastructure equipment appears to be working correctly, so the engineer is looking to eliminate misconfigured user workstations as a possible cause of the problem. Which command-line tool would provide the BEST information regarding workstation configuration?
explanation: ipconfig /all will give comprehensive configuration details for the workstation network interface/s, showing the IP address, subnet mask, DHCP server, DNS settings, and more. ping is a useful utility but, in this case, will only ping the loopback address (127.0.0.1), giving no configuration information. netstat will show network connections and listening ports. It can also be used to display Ethernet statistics but will not show network card configuration settings. hostname is a command that will show only the workstation name.
whyWrong: ping localhost only tests the local TCP/IP stack and shows no configuration details.
netstat -a lists connections and listening ports, not the adapter's IP, DNS, or DHCP settings.
hostname shows only the computer name and gives no network configuration details.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: An administrator is responsible for the operating system migration of 300 Windows users. As part of the migration, the administrator must save the end-users’ data to a temporary shared drive. The data must retain all security permissions and support hidden files. Which of the following commands will achieve this result by default?
explanation: robocopy (robust copy) is designed to mirror large amounts of data. It supports the copying of additional attributes, including hidden files, and maintains folder permissions. It has been included in the Windows OS since Vista. The copy command is not designed as a bulk copying tool; it does not retain permissions. xcopy does not support hidden files or maintain folder permissions.
whyWrong: The copy command copies files one by one and does not keep security permissions or hidden files.
xcopy skips hidden files and drops permissions unless extra switches are added.
cp is a Linux and macOS command and is not available at the Windows command prompt.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives). robocopy copies hidden files by default but copies NTFS permissions only with /SEC or /COPYALL; the book's 'by default' is not exact, though robocopy is still the best answer.

stem:
A technician is troubleshooting network connectivity and receives the following output:
Server: UnKnown
Address:  10.10.0.1
Non-authoritative answer:
Name:    www.google.com
Addresses:  2a00:1450:4009:81e::2004
          142.250.187.196
  1    <1 ms     *       <1 ms  WIN2022-DC [10.10.0.1]
  2     *        *        *     Request timed out.
  3     3 ms     1 ms     1 ms  172.17.48.1
  4     3 ms     3 ms     3 ms  192.168.0.1
  5     6 ms     6 ms     6 ms  151.231.252.44
  6    16 ms    72 ms    16 ms  2.120.11.144
  7    15 ms    14 ms   109 ms  72.14.219.96
  8    17 ms     *        *     216.239.40.71
  9    16 ms    16 ms    16 ms  142.251.54.35
 10    17 ms    18 ms    17 ms  lhr25s33-in-f4.1e100.net [142.250.187.196]
Which of the following tools is the technician MOST LIKELY using? (Choose two.)
explanation: nslookup (Name Server Lookup) is used to send a query to a DNS server (that is, Name Server). The output in the question is from nslookup www.google.com. tracert is the Windows trace route command. It displays the hops as packets are forwarded to the destination system. It is useful to identify bottlenecks where traffic is slowed down.
whyWrong: ping reports replies from one host and does not list DNS server answers or the hops on the path.
ipconfig shows the local adapter configuration, not name lookups or route hops.
netstat lists local connections and listening ports, not DNS answers or route hops.
NetBIOS statistics (nbtstat) show NetBIOS names and sessions, not DNS answers or route hops.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: A customer powers on their laptop and discovers that, though their device displays the normal Windows desktop, they are unable to access any network-based resources. Which of the following tools should be used at the command line to troubleshoot this scenario?
explanation: ping will allow a support technician to establish where the connectivity fails. The ping command can be used to test gateway access and remote (internet) connectivity. msconfig will display the configuration used during the boot process. nbtstat will not allow a technician to test connectivity on the network. nslookup will be useful if the technician is troubleshooting name resolution but would typically be used after ping.
whyWrong: msconfig changes boot and startup settings and cannot test network connectivity.
nbtstat shows NetBIOS name information and does not test whether hosts can be reached.
nslookup tests name resolution only, so it is used after basic connectivity is confirmed with ping.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: A network technician investigates an ongoing incident in which a desktop computer makes a connection to an IP address across the network. The technician needs to resolve the computer’s name associated with the IP address. Which of the following commands should the network technician use?
explanation: nslookup can resolve names to IP addresses (that is, forward lookups) and IP addresses to names (reverse lookups). DNS servers need to be configured with Pointer Records (PTR) and reverse lookup zones to support reverse lookups. gpresult allows a technician to troubleshoot Group Policy settings on the local machine. ipconfig is used to display local network configuration settings (it does not display remote workstation configuration settings). net user is a Windows command that’s used to manage local user accounts.
whyWrong: gpresult reports applied Group Policy settings and cannot resolve an IP address to a name.
ipconfig shows the local adapter settings and does not look up names for remote IP addresses.
net user manages local user accounts and has nothing to do with name resolution.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: A support technician has added a Windows 10 workstation to the domain companydomain.com. The technician needs to verify that the workstation has received security policies from the domain. Which command will confirm whether the policies have been effective?
explanation: gpresult will process and output the current group policy settings, and the level of detail can be determined by a command switch. /Z is super-verbose output (that is, the most detailed). ipconfig /all will not display group policy settings. netstat /e will display only Ethernet statistics for a local network interface. nslookup will use DNS to resolve registered names to Internet Protocol (IP) addresses.
whyWrong: ipconfig /all shows network adapter settings, not the Group Policy settings that were applied.
netstat -e shows only Ethernet statistics for the local interface.
nslookup resolves DNS names to addresses and cannot report applied security policies.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: A technician is using a command-line interface to perform tasks on a Windows 10 computer. The technician needs to determine which ports have active TCP connections to local or remote hosts. Which of the following commands should the technician use?
explanation: netstat -p TCP (-p for protocol) allows the display of current TCP or UDP connections. In this case, the desired output is TCP connections. Note that switches can be combined. If the required output was connections and listening ports, netstat -a -p tcp could be used. netstat -p UDP would only display UDP ports (NOT TCP ports).
whyWrong: net use maps and manages shared network drives and does not list TCP connections.
nslookup queries DNS servers and does not show connections or ports.
netstat -p UDP shows UDP activity only, not the TCP connections the technician needs.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives). The book's explanation says net use manages local user accounts; that is net user (net use maps shared drives), so that sentence was left out.

stem: An administrator has tested a new Group Policy Object (GPO) and now wants to deploy it into the production environment. After deployment, the finance users do not appear to be receiving the new GPO. The administrator thinks the problem may be related to other GPOs that have been deployed at the same time. Which of the following command-line tools would be MOST USEFUL for the administrator to verify which GPOs are being deployed to the accounting department?
explanation: gpresult will display the current group policy that has been deployed to the workstation. nbtstat displays NetBIOS statistics (not group policy). nslookup is used to query a DNS server. gpupdate will process any new and existing group policy but will not display the resultant settings. tasklist is a Windows command roughly equivalent to the GUI Task Manager process tab.
whyWrong: nbtstat shows NetBIOS statistics and has no information about Group Policy Objects.
nslookup queries a DNS server and cannot show which GPOs apply.
gpupdate applies new and changed policy but does not display the resulting settings.
tasklist lists running processes, like the Task Manager Processes tab, not policy settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 10
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: A technician is creating a logon script that needs to automatically assign a drive mapping to a public folder shared on server1. The new drive letter on the user’s workstation will be allocated the P drive letter. Which of the following commands will achieve the desired result?
explanation: net use allows temporary access to a shared folder (or, in this case, a persistent drive mapping to a shared folder). It is important to choose the correct syntax. The allocated drive letter p: must be defined before the \\server1\public location. tracert is not used to map drives. net use \\P will not work as the syntax is wrong.
whyWrong: tracert traces the route to a host and cannot map a drive letter to a share.
This net use syntax is wrong because the drive letter must come first, followed by the UNC path.
tracert shows network hops and cannot map a drive, whatever the arguments are.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 11
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5, 1.7 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: After a malware incident, a Windows system displays evidence of operating system files that have been modified. Anti-malware definitions were updated, and a full scan was performed. What needs to be performed NEXT to verify the integrity of the Windows operating system files?
explanation: SFC is the built-in Windows system file checker. /SCANNOW scans for the integrity of all protected system files and repairs files with errors when possible. As the malware in this instance has targeted Windows operating system files, this is the best tool. chkdsk is a tool that's used to repair disk errors, such as corrupt areas on the disk.
whyWrong: chkdsk checks and repairs file system and disk errors, not modified Windows system files.
diskpart RESCAN looks for new disks and does not verify system file integrity.
netstat -s shows per-protocol network statistics and has nothing to do with system files.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 12
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: An administrator has created a new group policy and deployed it into the production environment. The administrator would now like to verify that the new group policy settings have been downloaded and are now enforced on user workstations. Which of the following commands will allow the administrator to verify that the group policy is working?
explanation: There are three group policy tools in this question, so it is important to read this question carefully, as the goal is for a technician to verify the group policy locally. gpresult is run at the command prompt of a workstation to display applied group policy settings. The Group Policy Management Console (gpmc.msc) is typically run remotely by administrators to manage and report group policy objects. gpupdate could be used to apply new settings but does not report. shutdown -r (restart) will not report on group policy settings, although it could be used as a troubleshooting step, as some settings may require a reboot.
whyWrong: shutdown -r restarts the computer and does not report which policy settings are applied.
dcdiag tests domain controller health, not the policy settings on a workstation.
The Group Policy Management Console manages and reports GPOs centrally rather than verifying them at the workstation.
gpupdate applies new policy settings but does not report which settings are in effect.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.2 question 13
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (command-line tools in the old objectives).

stem: A technician is troubleshooting a user’s workstation that has no network connectivity. After confirming that the current IP address is set to 169.254.44.89, what is the NEXT action that the technician should take?
options: Attempt to obtain an IP address using ipconfig /flushdns
Attempt to obtain an IP address using ipconfig /all
Attempt to obtain an IP address using ipconfig /renew
Attempt to obtain an IP address using ipconfig /flushdhcp
explanation: The current IP address of 169.154.44.89 is an Automatic Private IP Address (APIPA), which is self-assigned by the client computer. This happens if the DHCP service is unable to respond to a client request. It is likely that there was a temporary service disruption. ipconfig /renew will indicate whether the DHCP service is available or if the issue needs to be escalated. ipconfig /all shows the current network configuration.
whyWrong: The /flushdns switch clears the DNS resolver cache; it does not request a new IP address.
The /all switch only shows the current configuration, which the technician has already checked.
There is no /flushdhcp switch in ipconfig, so this command does nothing useful.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: You plug a 32 GB flash drive into a Windows laptop. The flash drive has multiple smaller partitions that are not writable. Which of the following diskpart commands can be used to remove the partitions so that you can later format the drive to full capacity?
explanation: The clean option in diskpart removes all partitions. This way, you can later format the drive to full capacity. As per the docs.microsoft.com diskpart page: “clean removes any and all partition or volume formatting from the disk with focus.”
whyWrong: The repair option repairs a software RAID 5 volume; it does not remove the partitions on a disk.
The merge option works with virtual hard disks; it does not remove the partitions on a flash drive.
The extend option grows a volume into free space; it does not remove the existing partitions.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 2

stem: Which command is used to list the contents of a directory in the Command Prompt?
explanation: dir is used to list the contents of a directory in the Command Prompt or PowerShell. You might also use the tree command to show the tree of directories.
whyWrong: cd changes the current directory; it does not list the contents of a directory.
ping tests whether another computer answers on the network; it does not list files.
ver shows the Windows version number; it does not list the contents of a directory.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 3

stem: You have been tasked with printing a Group Policy configuration report to an HTML file for offline review. Which of the following commands will enable you to do this?
explanation: Use the gpresult command, which allows you to view the results of the Microsoft Group Policy configuration and print it to various file formats if you wish. With the /h option, gpresult saves the report as an HTML file.
whyWrong: gpupdate applies the latest Group Policy settings to the computer; it does not create a report.
gpedit.msc opens the Local Group Policy Editor to change policies; it does not print a report to a file.
secpol.msc opens the Local Security Policy window; it does not export a Group Policy results report.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 9

stem: Which of the following commands should you use to find out what edition of Windows is running?
explanation: Use the winver command to find out the version and edition of Windows that is running. This command opens a window that displays the information graphically. You could also use the ver command in the Command Prompt or $PSVersionTable in PowerShell.
whyWrong: pathping shows the route and packet loss to a remote host; it does not show the Windows edition.
ls is a Linux command that lists the contents of a directory, not a way to find the Windows edition.
hostname shows the name of the computer, not the edition of Windows that it runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 10

stem: You are troubleshooting a Windows system that is suffering from poor performance. The Event Viewer states that the file system is corrupt. What should you do NEXT?
options: Reload the OS using FAT32 instead of NTFS.
Run chkdsk with the /R option and reboot the system.
Open the defrag utility and run the drive analysis.
Change the drive from basic to dynamic.
explanation: The only option that would help the situation would be to run the chkdsk command with the /R option. /R locates bad sectors and recovers readable information, which is the only option listed that might fix the file system corruption (keyword might). /R implies /F as well, which fixes basic errors on the drive. Though not listed in the A+ objectives, you might also use the dism tool to repair a slowly running Windows system.
whyWrong: Reloading the OS wipes the data, and FAT32 is a step back from NTFS, so it is not the next step.
A defrag analysis only reports fragmentation; it does not repair a corrupt file system.
Converting a basic drive to dynamic changes how volumes are managed; it does not repair file system errors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 42

stem: A technician must identify a solution to copy a large number of files, which may take several hours. In the past, they have experienced interrupted connections and network disruptions. If the network connection between the source and destination machines is unstable or experiences a temporary interruption, what will allow the file copying process to recover?
explanation: To handle the task of transferring a large number of files over an unreliable connection while allowing the ability to resume the process if the connection is interrupted, the recommended tool is Robocopy. Robocopy, short for “Robust File Copy,” is a command-line utility designed for efficient file copying and mirroring. It includes features such as the ability to restart file transfers from where they left off in case of connection disruptions, making it an ideal choice for scenarios involving unreliable connections.
whyWrong: sfc scans and repairs protected Windows system files; it does not copy files between computers.
chkdsk checks and repairs file system errors on a disk; it does not transfer files.
git clone copies a Git repository and is not built to resume large file copies after a dropped connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 15
note: 220-1102 1.2 (command-line tools); mapped to 220-1202 1.5 (File management: robocopy).

stem: A user at a branch office can open websites by typing their IP addresses, but not by typing their names. The technician believes the PC holds stale entries in its local DNS cache. Which command BEST clears those entries?
explanation: The /flushdns switch of ipconfig erases the local DNS resolver cache. The PC then asks the DNS server again for each name, so stale or wrong entries no longer block access to websites by name.
whyWrong: This switch gives up the PC's IP address from DHCP; it does not clear cached name lookups.
This lists active sessions in numeric form; it does not change or clear the DNS cache.
This traces the route without resolving names; it does not clear the stored name lookups.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 35: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part II

stem: After a power cut, a desktop PC shows a "Missing Operating System" message at startup. The technician has confirmed that the firmware boots from the correct drive and has opened the Command Prompt from Windows RE. Which command should the technician run NEXT?
explanation: A missing operating system message often comes from small errors on the drive. Running chkdsk with /R from Windows RE locates bad sectors and recovers readable data, and /F fixes file system errors. After a successful repair, the user's files should be backed up at once.
whyWrong: Formatting the system volume erases Windows and the user's data instead of repairing the drive.
Diskpart manages partitions and volumes; it does not check a file system for errors.
This only verifies protected system files without repairing anything, and it does not check the drive's sectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

stem: A technician changed a password rule in the Local Security Policy of a Windows 11 Pro PC. The user reports that the new rule is not applied yet, and the technician does not want the user to sign out. Which TWO commands should the technician use to apply the change and then confirm which policies are in effect? (Choose two.)
explanation: The gpupdate command applies every changed policy on the computer without a sign-out. The gpresult /r command then shows a summary of the Resultant Set of Policy for the user and computer, so the technician can confirm that the new rule is in effect.
whyWrong: System File Checker repairs protected system files; it does not apply or report policies.
Winver shows the Windows edition, version, and build; it does not apply or report policies.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 34: Microsoft Command-Line Tools, Part I

stem: Which of the following Windows utilities is slowly replacing the ancient Windows Control Panel?
explanation: Settings is slowly taking over many utilities from the Control Panel. Many Control Panel applets now open the matching page in the Settings app.
whyWrong: Device Manager is a tool for devices and drivers; it is not replacing the Control Panel.
Administrative Tools is a Control Panel folder of MMC tools, not its replacement.
Terminal is a command-line host app, not a replacement for the Control Panel.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 8
note: 220-1102 1.4/1.6; Settings as a whole is not one topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings: System).

stem: Which of the following Control Panel applets will display the amount of RAM in your PC?
explanation: You can use the System applet to see how much RAM is currently in your PC. In Windows 11 the System applet opens Settings, System, About, which also lists the installed RAM.
whyWrong: Devices and Printers shows attached devices such as printers, not the installed RAM.
Device Manager lists devices and drivers but does not show the total RAM installed.
Action Center showed security and maintenance messages, not the amount of RAM.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 4: RAM, Chapter Review question 7

stem: What does a black down arrow next to a device in Device Manager indicate?
options: A compatible driver has been installed that may not provide all of the functions for the device.
The device is missing, or Windows cannot recognize it.
The system resources have been assigned manually.
explanation: The device has been disabled. You can right-click the device and select Enable device to turn it back on.
whyWrong: A compatible but limited driver does not show a black down arrow in Device Manager.
A missing or unrecognized device shows a yellow warning icon, not a down arrow.
Manually assigned resources do not show a black down arrow next to the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 6: Motherboards, Chapter Review question 2
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Device Manager) and 1.4 (devmgmt.msc).

stem: If Windows recognizes a device, where will it appear?
explanation: Windows displays recognized devices in Device Manager. Device Manager lists each device by category and lets you update, roll back, or disable its driver.
whyWrong: There is no Devices folder under System32 that lists recognized hardware.
The desktop shows shortcuts and files, not the hardware that Windows recognized.
The Downloads folder holds downloaded files, not a list of devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 6: Motherboards, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1102 1.3; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Device Manager) and 1.4 (devmgmt.msc).

stem: Which of the following does Windows do if you enable Game Mode?
options: It disables some security protections that often interfere with modern games.
It increases mouse or trackpad sensitivity.
It prevents Windows Update from restarting Windows.
explanation: Game Mode prevents Windows Update from interrupting gameplay by restarting Windows to install updates. It also gives the game priority for system resources. You turn it on in Settings, Gaming.
whyWrong: Game Mode does not change the color quality of the display.
Game Mode does not disable security protections.
Game Mode does not change mouse or trackpad sensitivity.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 1

stem: What is Data Execution Prevention (DEP)?
options: A technology that prevents viruses from taking over programs loaded in system memory
A technology that enables you to set permissions for different users on your computer
A technology that prevents programs from being installed on your computer
A technology that prevents files from being written to your hard drive
explanation: Data Execution Prevention prevents viruses from taking control of programs loaded into memory. It stops code from running in memory areas that are marked for data only.
whyWrong: Setting permissions for users is done with NTFS permissions, not DEP.
DEP does not block the installation of programs.
DEP does not block files from being written to the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 1.4; DEP is not a listed 220-1202 topic, its settings are in System, Advanced system settings, Performance Options, mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (System).

stem: A user has plugged in two monitors (via a VGA cable and an HDMI cable) and wants to set up dual monitors. However, there does not seem to be an image on the second monitor. What should the user do FIRST to enable dual monitors?
options: Go to Settings, Home, Display, Multiple Displays, and then select Duplicate these displays
Go to Settings, Home, Projecting to this PC, and then select Extend these displays
Go to Settings, Home, Projecting to this PC, and then select Duplicate these displays
Go to Settings, Home, Display, Multiple Displays, and then select Extend these displays
explanation: When users have connected dual monitors and there is no image, they will need to adjust the display settings by going to Settings, Home, Display, Multiple Displays, and then selecting Extend these displays. This will enable dual monitors. If they choose the Duplicate these displays option, the image will be the same on both screens. They cannot create a dual-monitor setup using the Projecting to this PC option.
whyWrong: Duplicate these displays shows the same image on both monitors, so it does not create a dual-monitor desktop.
Projecting to this PC lets other devices project onto this computer; it does not set up a second monitor.
Projecting to this PC is for receiving a wireless projection, and duplicating would mirror the image anyway.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 12
note: 220-1101 1.2 (mobile device accessories); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings > System > Display).

stem: Which storage option in Windows 10 or 11 offers the BEST mix of resiliency and performance with two drives?
explanation: A two-way mirror space efficiently and effectively uses two drives for resilience and performance. A simple space offers no resiliency; the other options require three or more drives.
whyWrong: A simple space stripes data for speed but has no resiliency if a drive fails.
A three-way mirror space needs at least five drives, so it cannot be built from two.
A parity space needs at least three drives, so it cannot be built from two.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1101 3.4; Storage Spaces is not named in 220-1202; mapped to 1.6 (Windows Settings > System > Storage).

stem: What is the primary purpose of virtual RAM (or virtual memory) in a computer system?
options: To provide additional storage space for files and documents
To improve system performance by extending available memory
To create a backup of the system’s physical RAM
To facilitate faster data transfer between the CPU and GPU
explanation: The primary purpose of virtual RAM is to improve system performance by extending the available memory. It allows the computer to use a portion of the hard drive or SSD as additional RAM when the physical RAM becomes insufficient. Virtual RAM serves as an extension of the available memory, rather than a backup solution.
whyWrong: Virtual memory holds pages of running programs, not stored files and documents.
Virtual memory extends RAM; it is not a backup copy of physical memory.
Virtual memory has nothing to do with data transfer between the CPU and GPU.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 1
note: 220-1101 3.2 (virtual RAM); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel System, where the paging file is set).

stem: In addition to right-clicking the Desktop, how else can you access the Display Properties settings?
options: By clicking the Settings gear in the Start menu
By clicking the System icon under Control Panel
explanation: Clicking the Settings gear in the Start menu will open the Settings app. From there, the System category will allow you to change the Display Properties. Clicking the System icon under Control Panel allows you to change system settings. Pressing Ctrl+Alt+Esc launches the Task Manager. Pressing Ctrl+Alt+Tab launches the Task View in Windows 11.
whyWrong: The System icon in Control Panel shows system information and settings, not the display settings.
Ctrl+Alt+Esc is not the shortcut for display settings; Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager.
Ctrl+Alt+Tab switches between open windows; it does not open display settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which section in the Settings app lets you configure backups?
explanation: The Accounts settings screen allows you to access the Backup screen, where you can configure backups for the user under the Windows Backup menu item. The System section allows you to configure a multitude of options for Windows itself. The Devices section lets you configure devices, and the Apps section allows you to uninstall and configure applications.
whyWrong: The System section configures Windows itself, such as display and storage, but not Windows Backup.
The Devices section configures hardware such as printers and Bluetooth, not backups.
The Apps section manages installed applications, not backups.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 6

stem: Which Control Panel applet would you use to join the operating system to a domain?
explanation: The System Control Panel applet is used to change the operating system computer name and change its membership from a workgroup to a domain, or domain to workgroup. The User Accounts applet is used to make changes to your user account or others on the operating system. The Windows Tools option in Control Panel opens up a menu of tools, none of which join the operating system to a domain. The Programs And Features applet is used to uninstall and repair installed programs, as well as manage Windows features.
whyWrong: User Accounts changes user account settings; it does not change domain or workgroup membership.
Windows Tools opens a folder of administrative tools; it is not where you join a domain.
Programs and Features installs, changes, or removes programs; it does not join a domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 8

stem: You need to configure an iSCSI connection; where will you find iSCSI settings?
explanation: The iSCSI Initiator utility can be found in Control Panel, in Windows Tools. The Storage Spaces applet is used to configure storage spaces of already connected storage. The Disk Management snap-in is used to configure disks already connected to the operating system. Device Manager is used to configure hardware attached to the computer.
whyWrong: Storage Spaces groups storage that is already connected; it does not set up iSCSI connections.
Disk Management configures disks that are already attached; it does not create iSCSI connections.
Device Manager configures hardware devices and drivers, not iSCSI initiator connections.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 11

stem: You have a number of files with a .des extension and you want to be able to search each file's metadata; which applet should this be configured in?
explanation: The Indexing Options applet allows you to configure custom extensions so that metadata can be searched. The File Explorer Options applet is used to view and configure the File Explorer. The Windows Tools option in Control Panel is not really an applet; it opens up a menu of tools. The Ease of Access Center applet is used to configure options related to user disabilities to make the operating system easier to use.
whyWrong: File Explorer Options control how files and folders are shown, not which extensions are indexed.
Windows Tools opens a folder of administrative tools; it does not configure search indexing.
Ease of Access Center configures accessibility features, not file indexing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 14

stem: Which power mode will write the contents of the RAM to the disk?
explanation: The hibernate power mode will write the contents of the RAM to the disk so that the computer can enter a low power state. The standby power mode will turn off the monitor and lower power consumption by the computer. The sleep and suspend power mode will lower power consumption, but it will not write the contents of the RAM to the disk.
whyWrong: Standby turns off the monitor and lowers power use but keeps the session in RAM.
Sleep lowers power use and keeps the session in RAM rather than writing it to disk.
Suspend lowers power use and keeps the session in RAM rather than writing it to disk.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 2: Windows Configuration, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which restriction will be imposed on Windows users until they activate the operating system?
options: They won't be able to launch applications.
They won't be able to run Windows Updates.
They won't be able to change the wallpaper.
They won't be able to browse the Internet.
explanation: Users will not be able to change the wallpaper or personalize the operating system until it is active. Applications will still launch fine. Windows Updates will continue to function to keep Windows up-to-date. Browsing the Internet will not be affected.
whyWrong: Applications still launch normally on a Windows installation that is not activated.
Windows Update keeps working on a Windows installation that is not activated.
Web browsing is not affected on a Windows installation that is not activated.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 12

stem: Which power management mode stores data on a storage drive?
explanation: When a computer hibernates, all the information in RAM is written to a file called hiberfil.sys in the root of C: within the storage drive. The computer can then power off fully and restore the session from that file when it starts again.
whyWrong: Sleep keeps the session in RAM with low power, so the data is not written to the storage drive.
Standby is an older name for sleep, which keeps data in RAM, not on the storage drive.
Pillow.exe is not a Windows power management mode or a real Windows program.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: What tool can assist a user who needs to find results faster when searching for files on a storage drive?
explanation: Indexing helps you find results faster when you search your files for names or keywords. Indexing runs automatically on Windows and constantly tracks any changes to indexed areas. firewall.cpl, when issued in the Run prompt or at the command line, opens Microsoft Defender Firewall. The Internet Options dialog box (inetcpl.cpl) is primarily associated with the Internet Explorer web browser. But some settings within Internet Options, which are part of the Windows system, can still influence Microsoft Edge's behavior, particularly regarding security and privacy settings. appwiz.cpl opens the Programs and Features window, where you can uninstall or change programs and turn Windows features on and off.
whyWrong: firewall.cpl opens Windows Defender Firewall, which controls network traffic, not file search speed.
Internet Options sets web browser and connection settings; it does not speed up file searches.
appwiz.cpl opens Programs and Features to manage programs; it does not speed up file searches.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You are about to start troubleshooting a Windows system. You need to be able to view the bootmgr file in the C: root of the storage drive. Which of the following should you configure to make this file visible? (Select the two BEST answers.)
options: Encrypted or compressed NTFS files in color
explanation: In File Explorer Options > View, you can configure hidden files and folders and set it to Show hidden files, folders, and drives, and configure protected operating system files by deselecting the check mark for the setting Hide protected operating system files. Files such as bootmgr are hidden and protected by default; you need to unhide them in both ways to see them.
whyWrong: Showing extensions for known file types displays file name endings; it does not reveal hidden system files.
Showing encrypted or compressed NTFS files in color only changes their name color; it does not reveal hidden files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A customer wants you to set up the system to scale images at 200 percent. Which Control Panel icon should you access to configure this?
explanation: You can use the Ease of Access Center to turn on the magnifier and increase the view of the display to 200 percent. You can also operate the magnifier with keyboard shortcuts: Windows+Plus (+) to turn it on or to increase scaling; Windows+Minus (-) to reduce scaling; and Windows+Esc to turn off the program. Programs and Features is used to add and remove programs and add specific features to Windows. Mail and Sound are self-explanatory: They allow you to configure email and sound profiles, respectively. Devices and Printers is where you go to configure printers, keyboards, and multimedia devices.
whyWrong: Programs and Features adds and removes programs and Windows features; it does not magnify the display.
Mail sets up email profiles; it has no display magnification settings.
Sound configures audio devices and sound profiles; it does not scale images on the screen.
Devices and Printers manages printers and attached devices; it does not magnify the display.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following would you use to repair or uninstall a program or turn Windows features on or off?
explanation: Accessing Run and typing appwiz.cpl opens Programs and Features in Windows, where you can repair, uninstall programs, or turn Windows features on or off. You can access the Microsoft Defender Firewall by going to Run and entering firewall.cpl. Entering mmsys.cpl from Run opens the Sound dialog box. Entering lusrmgr.msc from Run opens Local Users and Groups.
whyWrong: firewall.cpl opens Windows Defender Firewall, which controls network traffic, not installed programs.
mmsys.cpl opens the Sound dialog box for audio devices; it does not repair or remove programs.
lusrmgr.msc opens Local Users and Groups to manage accounts; it does not manage programs or features.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following sections of Windows Settings allows a user to copy important information about a PC and possibly send it to a technician for troubleshooting purposes?
explanation: Navigate to Windows Settings > System > About. Here, you can copy device and Windows specifications and paste them into an email or to another location.
whyWrong: Network & Internet > Ethernet shows wired connection settings, not the device and Windows specifications.
Narrator is a screen reader in the accessibility settings; it does not copy PC information.
Diagnostics & Feedback controls what diagnostic data goes to Microsoft; it does not copy specifications to share.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Where would you go to see the current Wi-Fi settings?
options: Control Panel > Network and Sharing Center > Wi-Fi
explanation: Navigate to System > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi to see the settings for your Wi-Fi network. You can set up a connection in the Control Panel > Network and Sharing Center, but the option is called Set up a new connection or network and works very differently from the Settings area (and is much more difficult to manage).
whyWrong: System > About shows device and Windows specifications, not the current Wi-Fi settings.
There is no Hardware > Wi-Fi page under System; Wi-Fi settings are under Network & Internet.
Network and Sharing Center can set up a new connection, but it is not where Windows shows current Wi-Fi settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings, Cram Quiz question 2
note: In Windows 10/11 Settings, Network & Internet is a top-level category, not under System; the book's path in the correct option is kept.

stem: Where can a technician create rules for inbound and outbound network traffic? (Select the two BEST answers.)
options: Microsoft Defender Firewall with Advanced Security
explanation: The main difference between Microsoft Defender Firewall with Advanced Security and the basic Microsoft Defender Firewall is the ability to create rules for incoming and outgoing traffic.
