You can run Microsoft Defender Firewall with Advanced Security directly with Run > wf.msc. While the standard Microsoft Defender Firewall can allow apps through, it can’t make specific rules. The Apps category opens up the Apps & features section of Settings, where you can see a list of what applications are loaded on the system and how much space they take up and uninstall them if necessary.
whyWrong: The basic Windows Defender Firewall can allow apps through, but it cannot create specific inbound and outbound rules.
Apps & Features lists, sizes, and removes installed apps; it does not create firewall rules.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Why should you continue to run Windows Update?
options: Windows is unstable and updates make it more stable.
Windows updates provide patches to fix vulnerabilities.
Windows does not need to be updated.
explanation: Windows is a complex program (every operating system is really a type of program). As such, there are flaws. Windows Update patches the flaws that are found over time. In addition, Windows Update sometimes distributes new features to your system. Security is the main reason why you should run updates.
whyWrong: Some updates improve stability, but security patches for vulnerabilities are the main reason to update.
Windows Update installs patches and features for Windows itself; it does not install application programs.
Every operating system has flaws that are found over time, so Windows does need regular updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: On a Windows 11 computer, a technician opens Devices and Printers from the Control Panel. Where does Windows take the technician?
options: The Bluetooth & devices page in Settings
The Print Management console in Windows Tools
explanation: In Windows 11, the Devices and Printers applet redirects to the Bluetooth & devices page of the Settings app. There the technician can add, configure, and remove printers, scanners, and other external devices.
whyWrong: Device Manager lists hardware and drivers; the Devices and Printers applet does not open it.
Print Management is a separate administrative tool; Devices and Printers opens a Settings page instead.
The Network and Sharing Center shows network connections, not printers and attached devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A technician is working in the Network and Sharing Center and needs to turn on network discovery and file and printer sharing for the private network profile. Which link should the technician select?
options: Set up a new connection or network
explanation: The Change advanced sharing settings link controls network discovery and file and printer sharing for each network profile. On a public profile both options are off by default, which protects the computer on untrusted networks.
whyWrong: Change adapter settings opens the list of network adapters for manual configuration, not the sharing options.
Set up a new connection or network creates connections such as a VPN or a new router setup.
The troubleshooter diagnoses connection problems; it does not change discovery or sharing settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

stem: A new Windows 11 workstation has Windows Defender Firewall with its default settings. Which statement describes how the firewall treats network traffic?
options: It blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and allows outbound traffic
It blocks all outbound traffic until a rule allows it
It allows all traffic until the user turns the firewall on
It blocks inbound and outbound traffic on private networks only
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall is on by default and blocks incoming connections that no rule allows. Only inbound traffic is restricted by default, so programs can still start outbound connections. When an app tries to listen for traffic, Windows asks the user and can create an inbound rule.
whyWrong: Outbound traffic is allowed by default; outbound rules must be created to block it.
The firewall is turned on by default in Windows 11, so it does not wait for the user to enable it.
The firewall protects every network profile, and it does not restrict outbound traffic by default.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A technician wants to add a second email profile for a user and opens the Control Panel in icons view, but no Mail icon appears. What is the MOST LIKELY reason?
options: Microsoft Outlook is not installed on the computer
The user account is a standard account
Windows Defender Firewall is blocking the mail ports
The Control Panel must be switched to Category view
explanation: The Mail applet configures profiles, accounts, and data files for Microsoft Outlook. It appears in the Control Panel only when Outlook is installed, so its absence points to a computer without Outlook.
whyWrong: A standard account can still see the Mail icon; the icon depends on Outlook being installed.
Firewall rules affect network traffic; they do not hide Control Panel icons.
The Mail icon is listed in icons view, which shows all individual Control Panel items.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A presenter plugs a USB microphone into a Windows computer, but webinar software still records from the laptop's built-in microphone. What is the BEST way to make Windows use the USB microphone?
options: Open the Sound dialog box (mmsys.cpl), select the USB microphone on the Recording tab, and set it as the default device
Open the Sound dialog box (mmsys.cpl) and set the USB microphone as the default device on the Playback tab
Disable the built-in speakers in Device Manager
Change the sound scheme on the Sounds tab of the Sound dialog box
explanation: The Recording tab of the Sound dialog box lists microphones and other input devices. Setting the USB microphone as the default device makes Windows and most apps record from it.
whyWrong: The Playback tab chooses output devices such as speakers and headphones, not microphones.
Disabling speakers changes audio output and does nothing to select a recording device.
A sound scheme changes the sounds that Windows plays for events, not the recording device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

stem: A shared family computer has a local account that was set up as an administrator. The owner wants that account to keep its files but lose administrative rights. Where can a technician change the account type to Standard?
options: The User Accounts applet in Control Panel
The Indexing Options applet in Control Panel
The System applet in Control Panel
The Sound applet in Control Panel
explanation: The User Accounts applet lets you change an account's name and its type between Standard and Administrator. Changing the type keeps the account and its profile, so the user's files stay in place.
whyWrong: Indexing Options controls which locations Windows Search indexes, not account rights.
The System applet changes settings such as the computer name and domain membership, not account types.
The Sound applet sets audio devices and sound schemes and has no account settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

stem: A technician needs to change how often Windows prompts users before programs make changes to the computer. Which Control Panel item contains this User Account Control (UAC) setting?
explanation: The User Accounts applet includes the link to change User Account Control settings. The UAC slider sets how often Windows asks for approval before apps or users make changes that need administrative rights.
whyWrong: The firewall controls network traffic rules; it does not set UAC prompts.
Programs and Features repairs, removes, and adds programs and Windows features, not UAC levels.
Ease of Access Center configures accessibility options such as Narrator and Magnifier.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: Which TWO tasks can a user perform from the User Accounts applet in Control Panel? (Choose two.)
options: Manage saved credentials and file encryption certificates
Change the account name that appears on the sign-in screen
Join the computer to a domain
explanation: The User Accounts applet lets a user change the account name and type and manage other accounts. It also links to credential management, file encryption certificates, UAC settings, and advanced user profile settings.
whyWrong: The computer name is changed in the System settings, not in User Accounts.
Domain membership is set in the System settings, not in the User Accounts applet.
Firewall rules are created in Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

stem: A technician follows a Windows 10 guide that says to open Administrative Tools in the Control Panel to reach Task Scheduler and Disk Cleanup. On a Windows 11 computer, the technician cannot find Administrative Tools. Where are these tools now?
options: In the Settings app under Personalization
explanation: Windows 11 replaced the Administrative Tools folder with Windows Tools, which holds largely the same set of tools. It is a folder of shortcuts to tools such as Task Scheduler, Disk Cleanup, iSCSI Initiator, and Local Security Policy.
whyWrong: Personalization changes themes, colors, and the taskbar; it does not hold the administrative tools.
File Explorer Options control how files and folders are shown, not the administrative tools.
The Sound applet configures audio devices and has no administrative tool shortcuts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A user who moved from the United States to the United Kingdom wants Windows 11 to show dates as day/month/year and currency in pounds. Where should the technician change this?
explanation: The Language & region page under Time & language sets the country or region and the regional format. The regional format controls how Windows displays dates, times, and currency.
whyWrong: Themes change the background, colors, and sounds, not date or currency formats.
Text size makes text larger for readability and does not change regional formats.
Sign-in options set Windows Hello, PIN, and password methods, not regional settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A user rarely uses a chat app, but it opens every time the user signs in to Windows 11 and slows the sign-in. What is the BEST place to stop the app from starting automatically?
explanation: The Startup page under Apps lists the apps that start when the user signs in and lets you turn each one off. Turning off unused startup apps saves system resources and speeds up sign-in.
whyWrong: Default apps chooses which app opens each file type or link, not which apps start at sign-in.
Offline maps controls map downloads and their storage location.
Apps for websites links websites to apps; it does not control startup apps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings

stem: A user wants to pair new Bluetooth headphones with a Windows 11 laptop. Which Settings location should the user open?
explanation: The Bluetooth & devices page turns Bluetooth on and off and starts the pairing process with Add device. It is also where Windows lists the paired devices, printers, and cameras.
whyWrong: The volume mixer adjusts app volumes; it cannot pair a new Bluetooth device.
Wi-Fi settings manage wireless network connections, not Bluetooth pairing.
Accessibility audio options such as mono audio do not pair new devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings

stem: A user wants the mouse wheel to scroll a whole page at a time instead of a few lines. Where in the Windows 11 Settings app can the technician change this?
explanation: The Mouse section of Bluetooth & devices sets the primary button, cursor speed, and how far the scroll wheel moves. The wheel can scroll a set number of lines or a whole screen at a time.
whyWrong: Display settings change resolution, scale, and orientation, not mouse wheel behavior.
Taskbar settings control taskbar items and alignment, not the mouse.
Typing settings control autocorrect and the touch keyboard, not the scroll wheel.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings

stem: For security, a company does not want content on USB flash drives to run or open on its own when the drive is inserted. Which Windows 11 Settings page is the BEST place to configure this?
explanation: The AutoPlay section of Bluetooth & devices sets the default action for removable drives and memory cards. Turning AutoPlay off, or choosing to take no action, stops content from opening by itself when a drive is inserted.
whyWrong: Location settings control which apps can use the device location, not removable drives.
Storage settings show disk usage and Storage Sense; they do not set AutoPlay actions.
Advanced network settings manage adapters and sharing, not what happens when a drive is inserted.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 2: Windows Configuration

stem: A support technician is helping a user to solve a printing problem on their desktop computer. To test for a possible fix, it is necessary for the technician to disable the printer. Which of the following tools should the technician use to do this?
explanation: Device Manager must be used to disable a hardware device. Devices and Printers allows for the installation and management of printers but does not offer the option to disable them. Sync Center allows for the management of offline files. Power Options does not offer any options to control printers.
whyWrong: Devices and Printers adds and manages printers but has no option to disable the device.
Sync Center manages offline files and has no printer controls.
Power Options sets sleep and power plans and cannot disable a printer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem:
A user calls the service desk after discovering they are unable to open a JPEG file in their pictures folder. When the user double-clicks on the file, instead of being able to view the picture, a command prompt window flashes up for a few seconds and then disappears. A technician views the file and sees the following: Name: Sunshine.jpg; Date modified: 22/10/2020; Type: Application; Size: 78KB.

Which of the following Windows Control Panel utilities should the technician use to resolve this issue?
explanation: It is likely that the file type has been associated with the wrong application and this is what is causing an error. The default settings would open the JPEG in the Photos app. This can be corrected using the Control Panel | Default Programs option. Display settings, Device Manager, and Internet Options do not offer the option to change file associations.
whyWrong: Display settings change resolution and scaling, not which app opens a file type.
Device Manager manages hardware drivers and cannot change file associations.
Internet Options holds web browser settings only and does not set file associations.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.4; Default Programs is not listed in 220-1202 1.6, mapped to 1.6 Apps (default apps).

stem: Technicians must ensure that all users’ web browser traffic is forwarded to the new proxy server. Select the Control Panel utility that will allow the relevant settings to be configured.
options: Network and Sharing Centre | Change Adapter Settings
explanation: By configuring the Connections tab, we can ensure all web browser traffic is forwarded to the proxy server. Network and Sharing Centre | Change Adapter Settings does not allow for proxy configuration. Windows Defender Firewall cannot be used to configure proxy settings. Device Manager is used to troubleshoot problems with hardware.
whyWrong: Change Adapter Settings configures network adapters and IP settings, not the browser proxy.
Device Manager manages hardware drivers and has no proxy settings.
Windows Defender Firewall advanced settings control traffic rules and cannot set a proxy server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6, 1.7 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A support technician is resolving a support issue for a visually impaired user who is having issues with default colors and screen resolution. Which of the following utilities should the technician use?
explanation: Ease of Access Center allows the system to be optimized for a variety of different disabilities. For example, the system can be optimized for users who cannot use a mouse or keyboard, as well as for visually impaired users. Device Manager allows the configuration of extra hardware for users with disabilities, but not the optimization of the interface for the user. System and Programs and Features would each allow the installation of new software, not the optimization of default system features.
whyWrong: Device Manager installs and configures hardware drivers and does not adapt colors for users with low vision.
System shows computer information and settings, not visual accessibility options.
Programs and Features repairs or removes software and has no display accessibility options.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A support technician installs a new webcam and downloads the drivers from the manufacturer’s site, but the webcam fails to operate as expected. Which of the following options will BEST allow the technician to troubleshoot problems associated with the newly installed hardware?
explanation: If a device is not working after installing device drivers, the first place to look is Device Manager, which offers important information to aid in troubleshooting. The Services console and Event Viewer’s System logs (which will report a failed driver) would be useful to troubleshoot background services that may have failed, but Device Manager offers more information. Programs and Features is useful if a problematic application needs to be repaired.
whyWrong: The Services console manages background services, not the driver status of a new device.
Event Viewer can log a failed driver, but Device Manager gives more detail about the device itself.
Programs and Features repairs or removes applications, not drivers for new hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A project manager allowed a colleague to use their computer. Afterward, they notice that webpages are not being displayed as intended in the web browser. A technician troubleshoots the issue and discovers that many settings have been changed from their defaults. The technician must find a way to reset the web browser back to its default settings. Which Control Panel utility should the technician use?
explanation: Internet Options allows browser settings to be adjusted or reset to their defaults. System offers no browser-related settings. Programs and Features allows the browser to be uninstalled or repaired, but not for settings to be changed. Network and Sharing Center allows for troubleshooting network adapters and connections.
whyWrong: System shows computer details and has no web browser settings.
Programs and Features can repair or remove a browser but cannot reset its settings.
Network and Sharing Center troubleshoots network adapters and connections, not browser settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A technician needs to manually set a temporary IP address for five workstations in a branch office due to the DHCP server failing. Where will the technician find the controls to manage manual IP address assignment?
explanation: Network and Sharing Center allows an IP address to be manually set. Sync Center is used primarily to manage the synchronization of offline files. User Account Control is used to manage security prompts when configuration changes are attempted. Credential Manager is used to store accounts and passwords that allow the signed-in user to access third-party sites without being prompted for additional credentials.
whyWrong: Sync Center manages offline file synchronization and has no IP address settings.
User Account Control manages elevation prompts, not network adapter addressing.
Credential Manager stores saved sign-in details and does not configure IP addresses.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6, 1.7 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A service provider supports a small organization with less than ten users. The organization is informed by their Internet Service Provider (ISP) that the email server has been changed to a different DNS name. A technician needs to visit the small organization to update configurations for all the local users. What Control Panel utility will allow the technician to make the changes?
explanation: This setting can be accessed using the Mail option in the Control Panel. Internet Options configures browser settings, Windows Defender Firewall allows for the configuration of network access through ports and protocols, and User Accounts is where the local user account database can be managed.
whyWrong: Internet Options configures web browser settings, not mail server addresses.
Windows Defender Firewall controls network access by port and program, not email profiles.
User Accounts manages local accounts and passwords, not mail server settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A research scientist user wants to connect a Windows 10 laptop computer to an external desktop monitor, keyboard, and mouse. When the scientist shuts the lid, the system shuts down. How can the system be configured to remain powered up whenever the lid is closed?
explanation: When the lid is shut, the Do nothing option will ensure the system does not enable any power-saving settings preventing the function of external peripherals. Sleep, Hibernate, and Shut down each enable a power saving setting that will power the screen off.
whyWrong: Sleep puts the laptop in a low-power state when the lid closes, which turns off the external display.
Hibernate saves memory to disk and powers off, so the external peripherals stop working.
Shut down turns the laptop off when the lid closes, which is the current problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A user responsible for creating rich digital media has installed an additional sound card into their tower computer system. However, the audio output still uses the default built-in hardware. How can the user ensure the default playback device is configured for the new sound card?
options: Device Manager | Audio inputs and outputs
explanation: Control Panel | Sound allows the user to view settings to change their preference for the hardware used for audio output, as there will now be two choices (the original and new hardware). Device Manager | Audio inputs and outputs is where drivers are updated and devices disabled. Devices and Printers allows new devices to be detected or removed (but not the choice of preferred audio playback device). Speech Recognition is not a setting that allows for the default playback device to be selected.
whyWrong: Device Manager updates drivers and disables devices but does not pick the default playback device.
Devices and Printers adds or removes devices but does not set the preferred audio output.
Speech Recognition sets up voice control and cannot choose the default playback device.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.4 question 10
note: 220-1102 1.4; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Control Panel utilities in the old objectives).

stem: A legal firm has recently installed a new word-processing application on all user desktops. Some users have raised support tickets, complaining that they do not get what they expect when trying to input special characters. Where should the support technician go to remediate this problem?
explanation: Selecting Settings | Time & Language allows the current language keyboard to be selected. If this is not done, then a user in the United States, for example, would press Shift + 2 and expect to see the @ symbol. But if the keyboard language was set to U.K., the character displayed would be ".
whyWrong: Accessibility settings help users with disabilities and do not set the keyboard layout.
Personalization changes themes, colors, and the lock screen, not the input language.
Apps settings install, remove, and set defaults for applications, not the keyboard layout.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A support technician has been tasked with configuring a multiple-display setup for several members of the marketing team. After connecting all appropriate power and display cables, where should the technician go to configure the displays?
explanation: Settings | System allows the configuration of multiple monitors through the Display settings. The other choices do not give access to the multiple display configuration settings. In Display, the technician can arrange the monitors, choose extend or duplicate, and set the main display.
whyWrong: Time & language sets the clock, region, and keyboard language, not display layout.
Personalization changes backgrounds and themes but does not arrange multiple monitors.
Bluetooth & devices pairs peripherals and does not hold the multiple display settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A sales manager has returned from a company event and complains that their laptop computer is displaying warning messages about a lack of disk space. The manager saved a lot of new data on the local storage and was required to install some software during the event. A technician must now try to fix the problem. Where should they go NEXT to support the user?
explanation: It is possible to access Storage settings from Settings | System. The disk space used is displayed along with options to free up disk space. The other options here do not give access to Storage settings to review storage usage.
whyWrong: Time & language sets the clock, region, and language and has no storage tools.
Personalization changes the desktop look and has no storage usage settings.
File History backs up files to another drive and does not free space on the local disk.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A new company policy is being implemented and, prior to this policy being pushed out company-wide, the security settings must be configured and tested. One of the policy requirements is that when the screensaver locks the screen, a password must be used to unlock the screen. Where can this setting be accessed?
explanation: The screensaver settings can be configured from the Settings | Personalization | Lock screen options. All the other choices are either non-existent paths or do not offer the option to set a screen lock timeout.
whyWrong: There is no separate Screen Timeout page at the top of Settings; timeouts are under System or Personalization.
User Accounts manages accounts and UAC, not the screen saver password setting.
Privacy & security has no Lock screen page; the lock screen settings are under Personalization.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A company would like to use BitLocker to secure all Windows mobile devices, which will be centrally managed through group policy. In the pilot phase, a small number of laptops will be manually configured with this security feature. To do this, the Device Encryption settings will need to be accessed through which of the following paths?
explanation: In an organization where group policy is centrally managed, the BitLocker settings will be configured by the organization. To access the controls directly, you would need to enter Settings, then Privacy & security. Note that additional operating system and hardware support is required to successfully enable BitLocker (OS version needs to be a minimum of Windows Professional and TPM hardware support is needed). None of the other choices offer the option to enable BitLocker Drive Encryption.
whyWrong: Settings | System holds display, sound, power, and storage settings, not Device Encryption.
Settings | Apps manages installed applications and has no encryption settings.
Settings | Network & internet configures connections and has no drive encryption settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Settings: Privacy). The path is Windows 11; in Windows 10, Device encryption is under Update & Security.

stem: A small publishing company would like to configure all devices to connect through a newly purchased proxy server before accessing internet resources. Which Settings menu option will allow technicians to access the proxy server settings?
explanation: A proxy server enables an organization to protect client browser sessions by restricting access to unsafe sites based on URI/URLs and employing content filtering. None of the other choices offer the option to select a proxy server. In Windows, the Proxy page is found under Settings | Network & internet, where an address and port or a setup script can be entered.
whyWrong: Settings | System covers display, sound, and power, not proxy servers.
Settings | Apps manages installed applications and has no proxy settings.
Settings | Privacy & security controls permissions and security, not the proxy server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 6
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6, 1.7 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A research and design company has a Corporate Owned Personally Enabled (COPE) policy in place. The Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) allows users to access personal email accounts, as well as their business email. Where can these settings be accessed?
explanation: To access mailbox configuration options from the Settings menu, Accounts must be selected. Settings | Accounts allows a user to customize their preferences for a number of options (including email). None of the other choices give access to email options.
whyWrong: Internet Options configures browser settings and does not add email accounts.
Settings | Apps manages installed applications, not mailbox accounts.
Settings | Privacy & security controls app permissions and does not add email accounts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A company is testing a new gaming application and seeks to gauge customer feedback by recording the customer experience during gaming sessions. What Windows settings would allow them to record customer reactions and feedback during a game?
explanation: A company can use the same features to provide visual and audio feedback during a gaming session that a user would use to record and share their own gaming sessions. These are accessed through Settings | Gaming | Captures. This feature must be accessed through gaming controls. The other options will not provide access to the required settings.
whyWrong: AutoPlay chooses what happens when media is inserted and cannot record gameplay.
Video playback settings change how videos play back, not how game sessions are captured.
Sync Center manages offline files and has no recording features.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.5 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.5; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Windows Settings in the old objectives).

stem: A business unit has had a new network printer installed and directly connected to the Local Area Network (LAN) switch, and a technician must now configure several workstations to connect directly to the network printer. When adding a printer on the client workstations, which of the following options will allow the technician to connect the network printer?
options: Select a shared printer by name
Add a printer using an IP address or hostname
Add a Bluetooth or wireless discoverable printer
Connect directly with a USB cable
explanation: The configuration will need to include an IP address or hostname as the printer is connected directly to the network switch. Selecting a shared printer by name would only work if the printer was already installed and shared by an existing computer on the network. The other options would not give the desired result as the printer is not wireless or connected via USB.
whyWrong: Selecting a shared printer by name works only when another computer already shares the printer.
The printer is wired to the LAN switch, so it is not found as a Bluetooth or wireless device.
The printer is connected to the network switch, not to each workstation with a USB cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.6 and 1.7 (Devices and Printers, network connections)

stem: Which of the following Internet Options tabs should you access to enable TLS in Internet Explorer?
explanation: Use the Advanced tab to enable TLS 1.2/1.3 (and other security protocols) within Internet Explorer. The Advanced tab of Internet Options lists the protocol settings, including the versions of TLS that are allowed.
whyWrong: The Security tab sets the security level of each zone, not the specific protocols such as TLS.
The Privacy tab controls cookies and pop-ups, not the security protocols the browser uses.
The Connections tab sets up dial-up, VPN, and proxy connections, not the TLS settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 29

stem: A customer calls to report that when they walk away from their laptop for an extended period of time, they have to reconnect to wireless upon returning. Which of the following will MOST LIKELY correct this issue?
explanation: Try adjusting the power settings so that wireless connections will not time out as quickly. This can be done in Windows in Power Plans and the Power Options dialog box.
whyWrong: A faulty wireless card would fail all the time, not only after the laptop is left alone for a while.
The battery capacity does not decide when the wireless connection drops during idle time.
The screensaver does not control the wireless connection, so disabling it would not stop the drops.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 47

stem: Which Control Panel utility is BEST used to remove a Windows application?
explanation: Programs and Features is the place to go in the Control Panel (CP) to remove an application in Windows. You can also open this by entering appwiz.cpl in the Command Prompt. Or you could access Settings > Apps > Apps & features.
whyWrong: Disk Cleanup removes temporary and unneeded files; it does not uninstall applications.
Administrative Tools is a group of system tools such as Event Viewer, not the place to uninstall programs.
Folder Options changes how folders and files are displayed; it does not remove applications.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 70

stem: A call center technician receives a call from a home user seeking guidance on updating Windows. They would like to ensure that they are running the latest Windows edition when it is made available to customers. What is the appropriate course of action for the technician to take?
options: Suggest that the user consider using a different system if they are unable to complete updates
Instruct the user to send their password via text to the technician
Guide the user to click on the Search field, type “Check for Updates,” and then press the Enter key
Suggest the user waits for an upcoming, automatic patch
explanation: When assisting a user with updating Windows, the recommended approach for the call center technician is to guide the user through the process. In this case, the technician should instruct the user to click on the Search field, enter “Check for Updates,” and then press the Enter key. This action initiates the Windows update process and allows the user to check for available updates and install them manually.
whyWrong: Moving to a different system does not update Windows on the device the user already has.
A technician never asks for a password, and sending one by text breaks basic security rules.
Waiting for an automatic patch does not meet the user's wish to check for the latest updates now.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 7
note: 220-1102 1.5 (Windows Settings: Update and Security); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Update and Security).

stem: A user wants to exclude certain folders from the Windows search feature to improve search results. Which of the following steps should they follow?
options: Disable Windows Search Service in Services.msc
Add the folders to the “Excluded Folders” list in the Windows search settings
Delete the folders from the hard drive
explanation: To exclude specific folders from Windows search, the user should add those folders to the “Excluded Folders” list in the Windows search settings. This allows them to customize search preferences while keeping the search feature running.
whyWrong: Disabling the Windows Search service turns off search completely instead of excluding a few folders.
Deleting the folders destroys the data, while the user only wants them left out of search results.
Reinstalling Windows erases data and settings and is far too drastic to exclude folders from search.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 10
note: 220-1102 1.4 (Control Panel: Indexing Options) and 1.5 (Windows Settings); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Indexing Options).

stem: A payroll manager has created a file on a shared drive and wants to protect it from accidental deletion by other team members. Which of the following applications should the technician recommend to assist the manager in hiding the file?
explanation: To assist the manager in hiding the file and preventing accidental deletion by others, the technician should recommend using File Explorer. By modifying the file’s properties, the user can mark it as hidden, making it less visible to other users accessing the shared drive. This provides an additional layer of protection and helps maintain the file’s privacy and integrity.
whyWrong: Disk Cleanup frees space by removing unneeded files and has no option to hide a file.
Task Scheduler runs tasks on a schedule and cannot hide files.
Control Panel holds system settings and offers no direct way to hide one file on a share.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 29
note: 220-1102 1.4 (File Explorer Options: hidden files); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (File Explorer Options: view hidden files). The hidden attribute does not really stop deletion; NTFS permissions would. Book answer kept.

stem: A customer calls the service desk as they would like to activate speech recognition on their Windows 10 Home PC. Which Windows Settings tool should the user utilize to enable this feature?
explanation: To enable speech recognition on a PC, the user should navigate to the Accessibility settings. Within the Accessibility settings, there is an option to enable speech recognition, allowing the user to interact with their computer using voice commands.
whyWrong: Regional settings cover language, date, time, and location, not speech recognition.
Appearance settings personalize the display and themes, not speech recognition.
Privacy settings control the permissions of apps and features; they do not turn on speech recognition.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 34
note: 220-1102 1.5 (Windows Settings: Ease of Access); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Ease of Access).

stem: Following a failed update, an application is no longer launching and displays the error message “Application needs to be repaired.” To address this concern in Windows 10, which of the following utilities should a technician utilize?
explanation: To address the issue of an application failing to launch and displaying an error message indicating the need for repair, a technician should utilize the “Programs and Features” utility in Windows 10. This utility allows users to manage installed programs, including repairing or uninstalling problematic applications. By accessing “Programs and Features,” the technician can initiate the repair process for the application in question, resolving the launch issue.
whyWrong: Device Manager manages hardware devices and drivers, not the repair of applications.
Administrative Tools holds system management utilities, but none of them repairs an installed application.
Recovery offers System Restore and reset options, which do not repair one specific application.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 75
note: 220-1102 1.4 (Control Panel: Programs and Features); mapped to 220-1202 1.6 (Program and Features).

stem: A sales rep often closes the lid of a Windows laptop at the end of the day and leaves it in a bag for the weekend. On Monday the battery is flat and the open documents are gone. The rep wants the open work kept even if the battery runs out. Which lid action should the technician set as the BEST choice?
explanation: Hibernate writes the open session to hiberfil.sys on the drive and then powers the laptop off. Because the session is on the drive and not in RAM, it survives a flat battery. Sleep keeps the session in RAM, which is lost when power runs out.
whyWrong: Sleep keeps the session in RAM, so a flat battery still erases the open work.
Turning off the display leaves the laptop running and draining the battery in the bag.
Doing nothing keeps the laptop fully on, so the battery runs out even faster.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

stem: A technician at a clinic must remove an old scanner utility that is not listed in the modern installed apps list. The same visit also requires turning on the .NET Framework 3.5 feature for a billing program. Which Control Panel applet is the BEST place to do both tasks?
explanation: Programs and Features (appwiz.cpl) uninstalls, changes, and repairs desktop programs. Its Turn Windows features on or off link adds features such as the .NET Framework. Both tasks can be done in that one applet.
whyWrong: Devices and Printers manages attached hardware such as scanners, but it does not uninstall programs or add Windows features.
Administrative Tools is a folder of admin consoles; it has no list of installed programs or optional features.
The System applet shows device details and System Properties, not installed programs or Windows features.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 36: Windows Control Panel Utilities

stem: A consultant connects a Windows 11 laptop to the Wi-Fi in a hotel. Other guests must not be able to find the laptop, and the consultant pays for each gigabyte used on the hotel network. Which TWO Network and Internet settings BEST meet these needs? (Choose two.)
options: Set the network profile to Public
Set the network profile to Private
explanation: A public profile keeps the laptop from being discoverable, so other devices cannot see or connect to it. Marking the connection as metered, with a data limit if needed, holds back data use on a pay-per-use network. Both settings are on the Network and Internet page.
whyWrong: A private profile makes the laptop discoverable, which suits only a trusted network, not a hotel.
A mobile hotspot shares the laptop's connection with other devices, which adds data use and exposure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 37: Windows Settings

stem: You will need a dedicated server system in order to set up a Windows _______________ computer.
explanation: A Windows domain requires a lot of steps on behalf of the domain administrator and the computer needs to be joined to the domain. A user needs a domain account set up before anything else. The domain controller is the dedicated server that holds the domain accounts, unlike a workgroup.
whyWrong: Windows 10 Pro is a client edition that can join a domain; it does not itself require a server.
Windows 10 Enterprise is a client edition that can run without a dedicated server.
Windows 10 Home works in a workgroup and needs no server; it cannot join a domain at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 11: Installing and Upgrading Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 4
note: 220-1102 1.2; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (domain joined vs. workgroup).

stem: Which type of connection is configured in the Cellular screen in the Settings app?
explanation: The Wireless Wide Area Network (WWAN) connection is a cellular connection and is configured on the Cellular screen in the Settings app. A wired connection is configured on the Ethernet screen in the Settings app. A wireless connection is configured on the Wi-Fi screen in the Settings app. A virtual private network (VPN) connection is configured on the VPN screen in the Settings app.
whyWrong: Wired connections are configured on the Ethernet screen, not the Cellular screen.
Wireless connections are configured on the Wi-Fi screen, not the Cellular screen.
VPN connections are configured on the VPN screen, not the Cellular screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 3: Windows Administration, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which of the following are administrative share names? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: Every volume gets an administrative share by default, including the C: drive, which is assigned C$. ADMIN$ is another administrative share; it is the share name for C:\Windows. System32 is simply a folder name within C:\Windows. $print is not an administrative share, but it could be used as a share name. An actual administrative share is print$, with the $ at the end of the share name. By the way, the print$ share is used to deliver print drivers from the print server to the client computer.
whyWrong: C:\Windows is a folder path; its administrative share is named ADMIN$.
System32 is a folder inside C:\Windows, not a share name.
Administrative shares put the dollar sign at the end, as in print$; $print is not one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You need to design a local area network for 10 computers with very limited data sharing. Which of the following network types is the BEST option?
explanation: The best listed option is the Workgroup. In Microsoft environments, it works well for 20 or fewer computers. Client/server networks such as Microsoft Active Directory Domains are designed for more computers, often in an enterprise setting. A VPN is usually implemented for users who need secure connections to other networks or the Internet.
whyWrong: A client/server domain is meant for larger, centrally managed networks, which is more than ten computers need.
A VPN gives secure connections to other networks over the Internet; it is not a LAN type.
A domain needs a server and central administration, which is more than ten computers with little sharing need.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You want to connect to a share on \\server1\data-share. Which of the following should be used to accomplish this?
options: Right-click the folder and select Share with.
explanation: The net use command can connect to shares such as \\server1\data-share or any other share on the network. Of course, you could also do this by mapping a network drive in File Explorer. A proxy server is used to filter and cache client connectivity to the Internet. Right-clicking the folder and selecting Share with allows you to share the folder but doesn’t make a connection to the share. ipconfig is used in the command line to learn the IP configuration of the network adapter.
whyWrong: A proxy server filters and caches Internet traffic; it does not connect to a network share.
Share with makes a local folder available to others; it does not connect to a remote share.
ipconfig shows the network adapter's IP configuration; it does not connect to shares.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You have been tasked with setting up a client Windows computer. It needs to gain access to the Internet, but all web traffic is cached and filtered by a go-between server on the LAN. What should you configure to enable Internet access for the Windows client?
explanation: You can configure a proxy server by entering the IP address of the proxy server and the port to be used. A VPN allows secure connectivity to the Internet. A domain is a large network of computer systems that are centrally administered. A workgroup is a small group of networked systems.
whyWrong: A VPN makes a secure tunnel to another network; it is not the go-between that caches and filters web traffic.
A domain is a centrally managed group of computers; joining one does not set where web traffic goes.
A workgroup is a small peer-to-peer group of computers; it does not route web traffic through a server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: In Windows, which network location profile setting should you choose if you are not sure what computers will be on the network or if you can trust them?
explanation: A public network profile means that network discovery and file and print sharing are turned off; this connection is good when you need to connect to public networks that you don’t trust (like at a coffee shop) because you don’t know what computers will be on those networks. Private is reserved for networks where you trust the systems. While a VPN is private and secure (hopefully), it is not one of the “network location profiles” in Windows but rather a network connection type. A metered connection should be used for hotspots, VPNs, and other connection types that might have data caps.
whyWrong: Private is for trusted networks such as home, and it turns network discovery on.
A VPN is a connection type, not one of the Windows network location profiles.
A metered connection limits data use on capped links; it is not a profile for untrusted networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A network technician must add a new workstation to the Windows domain. What Windows settings would be used to switch from workgroup configuration to a domain-joined configuration?
options: Settings | System | About | Domain or Workgroup
Control Panel | Credential Manager | Domain or Workgroup
explanation: A domain-joined computer will allow the enterprise to centrally manage settings through tools such as Group Policy. There are a number of ways to add a computer to the domain, including the PowerShell Add-Computer command. To access the function through the settings menu, you must first select the System feature. While there are other ways to add a computer to a domain (for example, PowerShell), the other menu options presented do not allow this action.
whyWrong: Sign-in options set how a user signs in, such as a PIN or password; they do not join a domain.
Region settings control formats for dates, times, and currency, not domain membership.
Credential Manager stores saved passwords and has no option to join a domain or workgroup.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: A user contacts the service desk and reports that they cannot access any network resources. A support technician asks the user to open Command Prompt and type in IPCONFIG /ALL. The resulting output contains the 169.254.23.66 IP address. What is this address type and what is MOST LIKELY the problem on the network?
explanation: If a DHCP server cannot be located when a host computer requests an IP address, then an APIPA address will be locally assigned to the interface. The same behavior will occur if a lease expires on a previously assigned IP address. 169.254.23.66 is not a private IP address. IPv6 does not assign APIPA addresses. Active Directory and DNS services are not responsible for allocating IP addresses.
whyWrong: Private IPv4 ranges are 10.x, 172.16-31.x, and 192.168.x; 169.254.x is not one of them.
An IPv6 link-local address begins with FE80, while this is an IPv4 address.
Active Directory handles authentication and directory services; it does not hand out IP addresses.
DNS resolves names to addresses; a DNS failure does not cause a self-assigned 169.254 address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: A support ticket is raised by a user who is unable to share a newly installed departmental printer. The user has been assigned privileges to share folders and printers. The user is part of a workgroup NOT on the Windows domain. The user reports that email and internet browsing are working correctly. What setting is likely causing sharing error?
options: The user does not have permission to share the printer
The Network profile is set to public
The Network profile is set to private
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall does not allow Windows file and print traffic while the firewall profile is set to Public (this is intended to add security when not using a trusted network). The private network profile will allow file and print traffic. The user has been assigned the requisite privileges so this should not be a problem. Other network services are working so there cannot be a problem with the network card.
whyWrong: The user already has the privileges needed to share folders and printers.
Email and browsing work, so the network interface is enabled and connected.
The private profile allows file and printer sharing, so it would not block sharing.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: What Windows feature can be configured to prevent P2P file-sharing applications from being used by members of the sales department?
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall can be configured to block unwanted incoming and outgoing connections. This is the most effective way to prevent the use of a P2P file-sharing application. Windows Virus & threat protection will protect a Windows operating system from malware. Windows Secure Boot is designed to ensure a private key cannot be tampered with. Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption offers protection from unauthorized access to Windows hard disk drives.
whyWrong: Virus and threat protection scans for malware; it does not block a legitimate application's connections.
Secure Boot checks that boot software is signed; it does not control application network traffic.
BitLocker encrypts drives against offline access; it does not block network applications.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: A user raises a support ticket after being prevented from adding an exception to Windows Defender Firewall. The user has an application launcher that they are attempting to run from their Downloads folder. Which type of user account allows for the modification of firewall rules?
explanation: Only Administrator accounts can modify Windows Defender Firewall settings. Power Users is a group that is provided for backward compatibility and allows the same privileges as a Standard user. Guest Account has the least privileges of all accounts, and Standard users do not have privileges to change system configuration settings.
whyWrong: The Guest account has the fewest privileges and cannot change firewall rules.
Power Users exists for backward compatibility and has the same rights as a standard user.
Standard users cannot change system settings such as firewall rules.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: A company has recently switched to a remote workforce model. The company supports many users in remote locations with expensive cellular and satellite connections. In order to minimize the costs for these links, the company would like to restrict monthly data usage. Which TWO configuration options will BEST allow the organization to restrict data use?
options: Advanced Network Settings | Network Interface | Metered Connection – On
Advanced Network Settings | Network Interface | Flight Mode – On
explanation: In order to restrict data usage on a network interface, a limit must be set and the Metered Connection setting must be configured. System | Storage settings allows you to optimize the use of locally available storage devices, not network traffic. Advanced Network Settings | Advanced Sharing enables the configuration of network profiles used by Windows Defender Firewall. Network Interface | Flight Mode – On will disable Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
whyWrong: Storage settings manage local disk space, not the amount of network data used.
Advanced sharing settings configure network discovery and sharing per profile, not data limits.
Airplane mode turns off wireless radios entirely instead of limiting monthly data use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.6 question 7
note: 220-1102 1.6; mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Windows networking)

stem: A user is reporting that their web browser is not going to the site they are trying to access. Which of the following statements describes the BEST way to resolve this issue?
options: Ensure that the user is not using a proxy server.
explanation: Make sure the user is not using a proxy server within the browser before attempting anything else. A proxy address (whether added by malware or by the user) can redirect the browser to unwanted websites (often malicious in nature).
whyWrong: Unwanted Internet shortcuts may be worth checking later, but removing them does not fix a proxy that redirects every request.
Deleting cookies removes saved site data; it does not stop a proxy setting from sending the browser to the wrong site.
Clearing the cache removes stored page copies; it does not change a proxy setting that redirects the browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 25

stem: A customer wants to use FTP to push configurations to a couple of switches that they are updating. The customer can use the FTP program on a laptop and can place the configurations in the proper directories of the switches. But the switches cannot communicate to the PC with FTP. How can you resolve the problem?
options: Change the laptop’s IP address to dynamic.
Make sure that the laptop’s IP address is in the correct VLAN.
Generate a static DNS entry on the server for the laptop.
Create an exception in the local firewall of the laptop.
explanation: You most likely need to create an exception in the local firewall of the laptop. Outbound connections from the laptop are working fine, but that doesn’t necessarily mean that inbound connections will work; in fact, most host-based firewalls have an implicit deny on all incoming traffic, while outgoing traffic is allowed.
whyWrong: The laptop already reaches the switches, so its IP address works and does not need to change to dynamic.
Connectivity to the switches is already established, so the laptop is not in the wrong VLAN.
The connection uses IP addresses that already work, so a static DNS entry would not let the inbound traffic through.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 26

stem: Your organization’s network consists of 25 computers that are wired to a switch. Your boss is interested in employing a file server with network shares and a print server. Which of the following Windows network setups should you recommend?
explanation: You should recommend the Microsoft domain setup. This means installing a server that acts as an Active Directory domain controller, where all logon authentication is centralized. This way, all access to network shares and print servers is also centralized. A domain controller is a server that is running a version of the Windows Server operating system and has Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) running.
whyWrong: A workgroup suits about 20 or fewer computers and has no central logon, so it does not scale to 25 computers with shared servers.
An ad hoc network has no computer in control and suits only a few systems, not 25 computers with file and print servers.
Spoke-hub describes how the computers are wired to the switch, which is already in place; it is not a Windows sharing setup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 31

stem: You are working on a client computer and receive a message that says the trust relationship to the domain has been broken. Which of the following steps should be taken to resolve this problem from the client computer?
options: Update the BIOS/UEFI using the latest version.
Rejoin the computer to the domain.
Reboot the PC as the domain to automatically rebuild the relationship.
explanation: You must rejoin the computer to the domain. You can do this by navigating to the Computer Name tab of the System Properties dialog box, which is accessed from the Advanced settings link from the System window or by executing systempropertiescomputername.exe at the Run prompt. You might also use the netdom command in the Command Prompt if you have Remote Server Administration Tools (RSAT) enabled on the Windows client or are working directly on a Windows server.
whyWrong: A BIOS/UEFI update fixes firmware issues but has no effect on the computer's trust relationship with the domain.
chkdsk checks the storage drive for errors; it does not repair a broken domain trust.
A reboot does not rebuild the trust relationship; the computer must be rejoined to the domain manually.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 60

stem: You receive a tech support call from a user on your corporate network about an Internet connection that is not working. You analyze the system and find out that the user’s system has a valid IP address, can connect to network shares, and can view local intranet pages in the web browser. However, when you attempt to access a public website, the connection times out. Which of the following should you investigate NEXT?
explanation: Check the proxy server settings in the browser. A large network may use a proxy server to facilitate the caching of web pages—often for external, or public, websites only. It could be that the proxy server was not configured properly or wasn’t configured at all.
whyWrong: The system already has a valid IP address and reaches local resources, so the IPv6 settings are not the problem.
A tampered hosts file would usually break internal sites too, and it is rarely used on modern systems.
Intranet pages resolve and load, so name resolution through the DNS server is most likely working.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 71

stem: A network technician is deploying a new desktop computer into a SOHO environment. The computer must be configured so that the user can share folders with other Windows users on the network. Which of the following configurations should the technician implement to accomplish this objective?
options: Set the network configuration to private
Assign the user with network administrator privileges
Create a shortcut to the shared drive’s public documents
explanation: Setting the network configuration to private allows access to shared files on the Windows firewall. Public profiles do not allow file and print sharing.
whyWrong: A proxy server is used for Internet access through an intermediary, not for sharing folders on the local network.
Network administrator rights are not needed to share folders with other users on the network.
A shortcut to the public documents only opens one folder and does not let the user share folders.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 38
note: 220-1102 1.6 (Windows networking: public vs. private network); mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Public network vs. private network).

stem: Which protocol can a technician utilize to establish a secure tunnel that conceals IP addresses and ensures enhanced security for network traffic?
explanation: When it comes to creating a secure tunnel that hides IP addresses and provides enhanced security for network traffic, the protocol of choice is the virtual private network (VPN). VPNs establish an encrypted connection between the user’s device and a remote server, ensuring that all data transmitted between them remains confidential and secure. By routing network traffic through this encrypted tunnel, VPNs effectively protect the privacy and integrity of the data while concealing the user’s IP address.
whyWrong: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses and does not create an encrypted tunnel.
An IPS detects and blocks malicious activity, but it does not create tunnels or hide IP addresses.
SSH secures remote sessions and file transfers, but it does not tunnel and hide all network traffic as a VPN does.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 76
note: 220-1102 1.6 (Windows networking: VPN); mapped to 220-1202 1.7 (Establish network connections: VPN).

stem: A user at a law firm says her desktop cannot open any websites or the shared drive. The technician runs ipconfig and sees the address 169.254.37.12 with no default gateway. Other desktops on the same switch work. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: The desktop could not get an address from the DHCP server
The DNS server address is wrong
The Windows firewall is blocking web traffic
The network profile is set to Public
explanation: An address in the 169.254 range is an APIPA address, which Windows assigns itself when no DHCP server answers. The technician should check the cable, switch port, and DHCP server, then renew the lease.
whyWrong: A wrong DNS server breaks name lookups, but the PC would still have a normal leased address.
The firewall does not change the IP address, and it blocks inbound traffic rather than ordinary browsing.
The Public profile turns off discovery and sharing but does not stop the PC from getting an address.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 9: SOHO Network Configuration

stem: Marco connected his new Windows 11 laptop to his home Wi-Fi. He can browse the web, but the laptop does not see the family's other PCs under Network in File Explorer, and they cannot see his shared folder. Which action will BEST fix this?
options: Change the network profile of the home Wi-Fi to Private
Mark the home Wi-Fi as a metered connection
Join the laptop to an Active Directory domain
Enter a proxy server address in the network settings
explanation: When a network is marked Public, Windows turns off network discovery and file and printer sharing. The Private profile turns both on, which suits a trusted home network.
whyWrong: A metered connection limits data use; it does not turn on discovery or sharing.
A home network has no domain controller, and Windows Home editions cannot join a domain anyway.
A proxy server relays web traffic and has nothing to do with seeing local computers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

stem: A sales rep often works from a phone hotspot with a small monthly data cap. Last month large Windows updates used most of the cap. The rep still needs email and web access on the road. What is the BEST way to prevent this?
options: Set the hotspot connection as a metered connection
Turn off Microsoft Defender Firewall on the laptop
Set the hotspot connection to the Private profile
Map a network drive to the company file server
explanation: Windows tries to reduce data use on a metered connection, for example by holding back large background downloads. Mobile broadband and hotspots with a data cap should be marked as metered.
whyWrong: Turning off the firewall lowers security and does nothing to limit data use.
The Private profile turns on discovery and sharing, which is wrong for a hotspot and does not limit data.
A mapped drive gives a share a drive letter; it does not control background downloads.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 38: Windows Networking

stem: What macOS feature is essentially multiple Desktops?
explanation: Spaces is the term Apple uses for multiple Desktops in macOS. Mission Control gives the overview from which users add and switch between Spaces.
whyWrong: Charms was a Windows 8 sidebar menu, not a macOS feature.
The Desktop is a single workspace; it does not by itself give you several of them.
Mission Control shows an overview of open windows and Spaces, but the extra desktops themselves are Spaces.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which macOS feature is functionally equivalent to Windows File Explorer?
explanation: Finder is the equivalent of File Explorer. Finder lets users browse, copy, move, and delete files and folders on a Mac.
whyWrong: The Dock launches and switches apps; it does not browse files and folders.
Quartz is the macOS graphics layer, not a file browser.
File Manager is not the name of the macOS file browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 7

stem: What feature of macOS is the equivalent of the command-line interface in Windows?
explanation: Terminal is the equivalent of the Windows command-line interface. Terminal opens a shell (zsh by default) where users type UNIX commands.
whyWrong: The Dock launches and switches apps; it does not give a command line.
Spaces gives multiple desktops, not a command-line interface.
Unity was a Linux desktop environment, not a macOS feature.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Which macOS tool, feature, or preference pane performs a function similar to the Certificate Manager MMC snap-in?
explanation: On macOS, Keychain (more specifically, the Keychain Access app) enables users to browse and manage certificates. Keychain also stores saved passwords and keys.
whyWrong: Apple ID is the account for Apple services, not a certificate manager.
FileVault encrypts the startup disk; it does not manage certificates.
The Network pane configures network connections, not certificates.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 12: Working with Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 6

stem: Which of the following is not a file extension you’d expect to see in the process of downloading and installing an app on macOS?
explanation: The .msc extension is associated with Windows MMC snap-ins. The .dmg, .pkg, and .app types are the macOS installation file types.
whyWrong: An .app file is a macOS application bundle that you copy to /Applications.
A .dmg file is a macOS disk image that often holds an app to install.
A .pkg file is a macOS installer package.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 6

stem: What tool is used in macOS to perform full system backups?
explanation: macOS uses Time Machine to perform full system backups. Time Machine backs up to an external drive or a network location and keeps hourly, daily, and weekly copies.
whyWrong: Backup and Restore is a Windows backup tool, not a macOS tool.
File History is a Windows tool for backing up files and folders.
iCloud syncs files and some data to the cloud but is not the macOS full system backup tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Which of the following commands will delete all the files in a directory in macOS?
explanation: Type rm * and press enter to delete all files in a directory in macOS. The asterisk is a wildcard that matches every filename in the current directory.
whyWrong: del is a Windows command; it does not exist in the macOS Terminal.
del is a Windows command, and all is not a wildcard.
rm all removes only a file named all, not every file in the directory.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 3

stem: What do you type before a macOS command to access help for that command?
explanation: Access the help for a macOS command by typing man [command name]. The manual page describes the command and its options.
whyWrong: Get-Help is the PowerShell help command, not the macOS Terminal help command.
A question mark alone does not open help in the macOS Terminal.
The /? switch opens help for Windows commands, not macOS commands.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 6

stem: Which of the following allows you to see all running programs in macOS?
explanation: Mission Control is a quick way on macOS to view what is currently running. Keychain or keychain access is a tool that saves credentials so that the user does not need to be prompted. The Finder is the macOS equivalent to the Windows File Explorer. Force Quit is a function of the macOS for killing a process.
whyWrong: Keychain stores credentials so the user is not prompted; it does not show running programs.
Finder browses files like Windows File Explorer; it does not show all running programs.
Force Quit ends a program that is not responding; it is not used to view running programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 2

stem: As part of your training program, you're trying to convince users to make backups on a regular basis. Which Apple app can be used to make backups of various types on a regular basis?
explanation: Time Machine is the Apple application that can be used to create backups on a regular basis. The Finder is the macOS equivalent to Windows File Explorer. VSS is a Windows technology that is used to create snapshots of a volume. Keychain is a tool that saves credentials so that the user does not need to be prompted.
whyWrong: Finder browses and manages files; it does not make regular backups.
VSS is a Windows technology for volume snapshots, not an Apple backup app.
Keychain stores passwords and credentials; it does not make backups.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of the following is a macOS feature for password management in the latest version macOS 15.2 (Sequoia)?
explanation: The Passwords feature has replaced the Keychain tool in the latest version of macOS 15.2 (Sequoia). The Passwords feature saves credentials so that the user does not need to be prompted.
