Spotlight is a utility in macOS that allows a search of the operating system and Internet for search terms. The Dock is the macOS application menu that is located on the bottom of the screen.
whyWrong: Keychain was the earlier password tool that the Passwords app replaced in macOS Sequoia.
The Dock launches and switches applications; it does not manage passwords.
Spotlight searches the computer and the Internet; it does not manage passwords.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 6

stem: What type of backup is kept on-site at the computer center for immediate recovery purposes?
explanation: Working copies are backups that are kept on-site at the computer center for immediate recovery purposes. An on-path attack is an attack where an eavesdropper listens between two people or devices. Cloud copies are backups that are sent to cloud storage and cannot be immediately recovered. Journal copies is a wrong answer.
whyWrong: An on-path attack is an eavesdropping attack, not a type of backup.
Cloud copies are stored off-site and cannot be restored as quickly as copies kept on-site.
Journal copies is not a backup type kept for immediate recovery.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 8
note: Backup copy types are also tested under 220-1202 4.3 (onsite vs. offsite); the chapter covers them as a macOS best practice, so mapped to 1.8.

stem: What is the name of the area at the bottom of a macOS screen where, by default, a bar of crucial icons appears?
explanation: The Dock is the area at the bottom of the macOS screen that is used to launch applications. The footer is not a valid answer. Mission Control is a macOS feature that allows you to see all the applications running. The Taskbar is a Windows Desktop element that is used to track running applications and quickly launch them.
whyWrong: Footer is not the name of any macOS screen element.
Mission Control shows all open windows and desktops; it is not the icon bar at the bottom.
The Taskbar is the Windows element at the bottom of the screen, not the macOS one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 14

stem: Which key combination can you use to bring up Spotlight from within an app?
explanation: The Command+spacebar key combination will bring up the Spotlight utility. Control+Shift, Option+Tab, and Alt+Home are wrong answers. Spotlight searches files, applications, and the Internet from any app.
whyWrong: Control+Shift is not the shortcut that opens Spotlight.
Option+Tab is not the shortcut that opens Spotlight.
Alt+Home is not a macOS shortcut for Spotlight.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 15

stem: Which of the following is the built-in web browser for macOS?
explanation: Safari is Apple’s web browser. It is used in macOS and iOS. Chrome is developed by Google and can be added to macOS. Firefox (Mozilla) can also be added to macOS. Microsoft Edge is the built-in browser that Windows uses.
whyWrong: Chrome is made by Google; it can be added to macOS but is not built in.
Firefox is made by Mozilla; it can be added to macOS but is not built in.
Edge is the browser built into Windows, not the built-in macOS browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which program should you use to access Utilities in macOS? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: Finder is the application to use when looking for applications and files. Utilities is located in Finder > Applications. Spotlight can be used to locate just about anything on a Mac, including Utilities. Mission Control allows you to modify the desktop (and run multiple desktops). Apple provides the Keychain Access utility, a password management system that can contain not only passwords but private keys and certificates.
whyWrong: Mission Control shows open windows and multiple desktops; it does not open the Utilities folder.
Keychain Access stores passwords, keys, and certificates; it does not open the Utilities folder.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following should be enabled when you want a user at another Mac to take control of your computer?
explanation: Use Screen Sharing in macOS to allow another user to view and take control of your Mac. (The remote user could also use VNC.) Remote Desktop and Remote Assistance are similar programs used in Windows. Screen mirroring is a technology (common in mobile devices) that allows the display to be mirrored to a TV or to another computer.
whyWrong: Remote Desktop is a Windows remote control feature, not the macOS feature for this.
Remote Assistance is a Windows feature for inviting help, not a macOS feature.
Screen mirroring copies the display to a TV or another screen; it does not let a user take control.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What root level folder contains core operating system files?
explanation: /System contains core operating system files. Usually, this is not an area to modify! /Applications stores user-installed applications. /Users contains the home directories for users, and /Library holds systemwide settings.
whyWrong: /Applications holds installed applications, not the core operating system files.
/Users holds the home folders of the user accounts, not core operating system files.
/Library holds systemwide settings and support files, not the core operating system files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You want to save the state of a Mac running macOS. Which tool should be used?
explanation: Use the Time Machine to save the state of the computer or to restore to that computer’s earlier state. This is similar to the Windows System Restore utility. Force Quit is a utility in macOS that closes a nonresponsive application. Disk Utility is used to verify and repair macOS drives.
whyWrong: System Restore is a Windows tool; it is not available on a Mac.
Force Quit closes an application that does not respond; it does not save the state of the Mac.
Disk Utility verifies, repairs, and formats drives; it does not save the state of the computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Due to recent corporate espionage attempts, a technician needs to secure the contents of the main storage drive on the CEO’s Mac. Which macOS utility will allow the tech to encrypt the drive? (Select the BEST answer.)
explanation: The tech can encrypt the contents of the main storage drive on a Mac with FileVault. Terminal allows you to enter commands, manipulate data, and make configuration changes and is similar to the PowerShell or Command Prompt in Windows. A typical way to get macOS apps (with a valid Apple ID) is to simply go to the App Store. Although FileVault implements AES 128-bit encryption to encrypt the entire contents of a drive, 128-bit encryption by itself is not a macOS utility.
whyWrong: Terminal is the macOS command-line app; it is not the utility that encrypts the drive.
The App Store is where macOS apps are downloaded; it does not encrypt the storage drive.
128-bit encryption is the strength FileVault uses, not a macOS utility in itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which program handles installing a printer’s driver automatically in macOS? (Select the BEST answer.)
explanation: AirPrint is the technology used to install a printer automatically in macOS (as long as the printer is compatible with macOS). Bonjour is a networking technology used by macOS to locate networked computers and devices. The Magic Mouse is an Apple mouse that allows for special clicking and gesturing, making it easier to navigate through macOS. iCloud is Apple’s cloud infrastructure, where a Mac user can store and back up data. While AirPrint might locate the printer driver on iCloud, iCloud is not the best answer.
whyWrong: Bonjour finds computers and devices on the network; it does not install the printer driver.
The Magic Mouse is an Apple mouse with gestures, not software that installs printers.
iCloud is Apple's cloud storage and backup service; it is not the tool that installs printer drivers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: You need to download an application that is not available on the App Store. It needs to be mounted as an image. Which of the following extensions should you use?
explanation: Download the .dmg file format. This provides a mountable image that is opened by the Disk Image Mounter utility when double-clicked. It then mounts a virtual disk in Finder, but Finder is a program, not an extension. The .pkg and .app file types do not mount an image the way that a .dmg does. However, an .app might exist inside a .dmg!
whyWrong: A .pkg file is an installer package that runs an installer; it is not mounted as a disk image.
An .app file is the application bundle itself; it is not a mountable image, though it may sit inside one.
Finder is the macOS file manager program, not a file extension.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 8

stem: A customer reports that a spinning wheel appears on the screen when trying to run a specific application. What does this spinning wheel represent? (Select the BEST answer.)
options: An Apple macOS proprietary crash screen
A Microsoft Windows proprietary crash screen
explanation: A pinwheel, also known as a spinning pinwheel of death (SPOD), is an Apple macOS proprietary crash screen. An example of a Microsoft Windows proprietary crash screen is the blue screen of death (BSOD). Linux is an open-source operating system. Although there are crash screens in Linux, they are not considered proprietary. A spinning wheel could possibly be caused by a failing CPU, but it is more likely caused by a stalled or frozen application.
whyWrong: A failing CPU could cause it, but a spinning wheel in one app most often means that app has stalled.
The Microsoft Windows crash screen is the blue screen of death, not a spinning wheel.
Linux is open source, so its crash screens are not proprietary, and this symptom is from macOS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS, Cram Quiz question 9
note: The spinning pinwheel means the app is not responding (fix with Force Quit); calling it a crash screen is the book's wording. Book answer kept.

stem: An employee signs in to a company Mac with a Managed Apple ID and tries to buy an app from the App Store, but the purchase is not allowed. What is the MOST LIKELY reason?
options: Managed Apple IDs cannot make purchases
The Mac needs a FileVault recovery key first
The user's personal Apple ID has expired
The App Store works only from an administrator account in Terminal
explanation: A Managed Apple ID is created and owned by the organization, and Apple restricts it to protect company data. These accounts cannot make purchases, and some features are disabled, so the employee must contact the company administrator for the app.
whyWrong: FileVault encrypts the drive; its recovery key has no effect on App Store purchases.
The employee is signed in with the Managed Apple ID, so the personal account does not affect this purchase.
The App Store is a graphical app, and purchases do not depend on Terminal or an administrator account.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS

stem: Which TWO statements about Managed Apple IDs are true? (Choose two.)
options: They are created and assigned to users by the organization's administrator
They are separate from the user's personal Apple ID
They replace the user's personal Apple ID on all of the user's devices
They let users install any app because the company pays for it
They can be created only with a phone number that is not used by any other Apple ID
explanation: A Managed Apple ID is an account that a company creates and assigns to an employee for business use, and the company effectively owns it. It is separate from the employee's personal Apple ID, although both can use the same email address and phone number.
whyWrong: A Managed Apple ID exists alongside the personal Apple ID; it does not replace it.
Managed Apple IDs have restrictions, and companies often allow only approved apps.
A user can have the same email address and phone number on a personal and a Managed Apple ID.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 39: macOS

stem: A company wants employees to install only approved apps on company-owned Macs and iPhones. Which method is the BEST way to apply this corporate restriction?
options: Use mobile device management (MDM) to allow only approved apps for the users' Apple IDs
Turn on FileVault on every device
Ask employees to sign out of iCloud
Enable two-factor authentication on each personal Apple ID
explanation: Corporate restrictions are usually applied through MDM software that is tied to the employees' Apple IDs. The administrator can allow a list of approved apps and block other installations, and can also use the App Store to distribute the required apps.
whyWrong: FileVault encrypts the startup disk; it does not control which apps can be installed.
Signing out of iCloud stops syncing but does not limit app installations.
Two-factor authentication protects the sign-in; it does not restrict which apps employees install.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux

stem: Several users in the publishing department would like to have access to Skype, as this is the standard tool within the organization for conducting meetings and making calls with colleagues. The users in the publishing department all use macOS and cannot find the Skype application in the Apple App Store, but it is available as a download from the official Microsoft site. What file format should the users select to ensure the Skype application can be installed on their macOS computers?
explanation: The standard file extensions for a Mac installation file is DMG (from D isk i M a G e) and replaces the much older IMG file format. MSI and EXE file formats are used by Windows computers. APK files are Android Package files and are used to deploy applications on devices running the Android operating system.
whyWrong: MSI is a Windows Installer package and does not install on macOS.
EXE is a Windows executable and does not run on macOS.
APK is an Android application package, not a macOS installer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 1

stem: A support technician is helping a user to restore deleted files from a recent backup. The user’s workstation runs on macOS, and the user needs to take a look through the files on the backup before restoring some of the files. Which macOS utility will be MOST useful for this task?
explanation: The Mac Finder application allows the user to view files on all supported media. Keychain is used to support single sign-on (SSO) and allows transparent authentication across multiple sites. Mission Control is used to switch between different workspaces on a Mac. Explorer is a Windows feature.
whyWrong: Keychain stores passwords and certificates; it does not browse files.
Mission Control switches between open windows and desktops, not files.
Explorer is the Windows file manager and is not on macOS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 2

stem: A user raises a support ticket as they are unsure how to create automated backups onto an external hard disk that they have purchased. The client workstation is running the latest version of macOS. What tool or application would be the BEST choice for scheduling automatic backups onto the drive?
explanation: The Mac feature used to back up and restore data files is Time Machine. File History and Windows Backup are features supported only on Windows operating systems. Mission Control is not used to back up or restore files.
whyWrong: File History is a Windows backup feature and is not on macOS.
Windows Backup runs only on Windows, not on macOS.
Mission Control manages windows and desktops; it does not back up files.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 3

stem: A technician is providing support to the user of a macOS computer on which the e-mail application is unresponsive. What feature will allow the technician to view a list of currently active applications and shut down the unresponsive application?
explanation: The Force Quit menu allows unresponsive applications to be terminated. Task Manager, Task List, and Control Panel are all features available only on Windows computers.
whyWrong: Task Manager is a Windows tool and is not on macOS.
Tasklist is a Windows command and is not on macOS.
Control Panel is a Windows settings tool and is not on macOS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 4

stem: A research department recently purchased MacBook computers for departmental users. Due to highly sensitive data being stored on these computers, management is asking for additional security for locally stored content. What feature would be a good choice to secure the local data drive?
explanation: FileVault allows a Mac hard drive to be encrypted using 128-bit or 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). Once the feature has been enabled, the user must supply their password before the system can boot up. If no password is provided, then the disk will remain encrypted. iCloud is used to synchronize data from Apple devices to cloud-based storage. BitLocker is a disk encryption technology used on Windows operating systems.
whyWrong: iCloud syncs data to cloud storage; it does not encrypt the local drive.
Keychain stores passwords and keys; it does not encrypt the whole drive.
BitLocker is the Windows drive encryption feature and is not on macOS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 5

stem: A user visits several different internet sites where a user account and password must be entered to access the site. The user would like to automate this process so that, when they sign in to their macOS computer, they will not need to enter additional passwords to access these sites. What macOS feature will allow the use and management of multiple credentials?
explanation: The Keychain feature allows a user to store passwords and account information that can then be used to reduce the number of passwords that a user would otherwise need to remember. Mission Control is used to switch between applications and desktops. Spotlight is used for system-wide searches (such as searching for an application, email, or files) on a macOS machine. Dock is used to quickly navigate to applications and features.
whyWrong: Mission Control switches between windows and desktops; it does not store passwords.
Spotlight searches the system for files and apps; it does not store passwords.
The Dock launches apps and opens folders; it does not store passwords.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 7

stem: A technician has been asked to uninstall a large application that is no longer used on a manager’s MacBook Pro. How can they uninstall the application?
options: Use Finder to locate the application and delete the application folder
Use Mission Control to locate the application and delete the application window
Use the App Store to remove the unwanted application
Use Finder to locate the application and move it to Trash
explanation: On macOS, an application without its own uninstaller is removed by dragging it from the Applications folder in Finder to the Trash and then emptying the Trash. Apps from the App Store can also be removed from Launchpad. Mission Control only arranges open windows and desktops.
whyWrong: A Mac application is a single app bundle that you move to the Trash; you do not search for and delete an application folder.
Mission Control shows open windows and desktops; it cannot uninstall applications.
The App Store itself does not remove apps on macOS; apps are removed from the Applications folder or Launchpad.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 8
note: 220-1102 1.10; mapped to 220-1202 1.8 (macOS). Book answer A (delete the application folder) corrected: Exam Cram 2e Chapter 39 says to run the app's uninstaller or drag the app from Applications to the Trash, which is option D.

stem:
A marketing manager raises a support request when their macOS laptop fails to boot, displaying the following error message: No bootable device – insert boot disk and press any key

What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Access the Recovery menu by holding Command + R during boot and choose the Disk Utility
Access the Recovery menu by holding Command + R during boot and choose Reinstall macOS
Access the Recovery menu by booting from DVD installation media and choose the Disk Utility
Boot into safe mode using Command + R during the boot and choose Restore from the Time Machine Backup
explanation: In the event that a Mac computer fails to boot, it is likely that one or more critical files on the hard disk are missing or damaged. To access the Recovery menu, Command + R must be pressed during the boot process. The recovery options can then be accessed to attempt to fix the error. Do not attempt to reinstall the operating system until all other options have been attempted. The Recovery menu cannot be accessed by booting the computer from a DVD, not to mention that most modern Macs do not include a DVD drive.
whyWrong: Reinstalling macOS can lose data, so try Disk Utility before it.
Recovery is reached with a key combination at boot, not from DVD media.
Safe mode is not started with Command + R, and a restore is not the first step.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.10; mapped to 220-1202 1.8 (macOS). Command + R applies to Intel Macs; on Apple silicon Macs, Recovery opens by holding the power button at startup.

stem: After installing a number of applications on a user’s MacBook Pro, the technician deletes a number of DMG and PKG files from the downloads folder. Upon running Activity Monitor, there does not appear to be much free disk space. What can the technician do to free up disk space?
options: Use the Trash application to permanently delete the files
Use the Recycle Bin application to permanently delete the files
Use the Disk Cleaner application to identify unwanted files
Use Disk Utility to split the hard drive into separate partitions
explanation: To permanently delete the files and free up disk space, the Trash application should be emptied. Recycle Bin and Disk Cleaner are Windows features. Separating a disk into separate partitions with Disk Utility will not increase the available disk space.
whyWrong: Recycle Bin is the Windows name; macOS uses the Trash.
Disk Cleaner is not a macOS tool, and Disk Cleanup is a Windows tool.
Splitting a drive into partitions does not add any free space.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 10

stem: A user would like to customize the list of available utilities and applications that they see after successfully logging on to their MacBook Pro. What feature should they customize?
explanation: The Dock is normally displayed at the bottom of the screen and is a convenient place through which to access features, applications, folders, and files. The Dock will display recently used applications by default but can be customized by dragging an item onto the Dock to create a persistent link. Mission Control allows users to switch between different workspaces. The Start menu is a Microsoft Windows feature. Toolbars are used to access features within an application.
whyWrong: Mission Control switches between workspaces; it does not hold app shortcuts.
The Start menu is a Windows feature and is not on macOS.
Toolbars give access to features inside one application, not to all apps.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 11

stem: A technician must perform a number of tasks to configure a macOS workstation before assigning it to a user. They need to configure network settings, set up a printer, and configure backups. Which folder will host these configuration utilities?
explanation: System Preferences allows the configuration and customization of all common configuration preferences. Mission Control allows users to switch between different workspaces. Dock offers easy access to applications and files. Disk Utility is a system tool that handles disk-specific tasks on Mac computers.
whyWrong: Mission Control switches between workspaces and does not hold settings.
The Dock gives quick access to apps and files, not to system settings.
Disk Utility handles disks and volumes, not network, printer, or backup settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 12

stem: A user wants to use multiple desktops on their macOS workstation. Which of the following methods will allow the user to switch between desktops? (Choose two.)
options: Control + right or left arrow keys
Select the desktop from the Dock using the mouse or trackpad
Enter Mission Control and choose the desired desktop using the mouse or trackpad
explanation: To avoid an overly cluttered desktop due to a large number of running applications, it is possible for a Mac user to create additional desktops. These desktops are known as spaces. The user can switch between them either by using Control + right or left arrow keys or by adding and/or selecting another desktop in Mission Control. Desktops (or spaces) cannot be accessed directly from the Dock. Command + spacebar is used to call up the Spotlight search function.
whyWrong: Desktops (spaces) are not opened from the Dock.
Command + spacebar opens Spotlight search, not another desktop.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.10 question 13

stem: What macOS root level folder holds systemwide settings, resources, and support files used by the applications and the operating system itself?
explanation: /Library holds systemwide settings. It stores the resources and support files that applications and macOS itself use for all users on the Mac.
whyWrong: /Applications stores the installed applications, not the systemwide settings and support files.
/Users holds the home folders of each user account, not the systemwide settings.
/System contains the core operating system files, which are not meant to be modified.
/Users/Library holds the settings and support files of a single user, not of the whole system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 1

stem: When installing new software on a macOS computer, which of the following file extensions is most commonly used by technicians?
explanation: When working with macOS, the “.dmg” file extension is commonly used for software installation. A DMG (disk image) file contains the necessary files and folders required for installing applications on macOS systems. The DMG file acts as a virtual disk that can be mounted, allowing access to the installer package contained within. Once mounted, the technician can initiate the installation process to install the software onto the macOS computer.
whyWrong: A .pkg file is a macOS installer package, but software is most often delivered inside a .dmg disk image.
A .bat file is a Windows batch script, not a macOS installation file.
An .msi file is a Windows Installer package and is not used to install software on macOS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 18
note: 220-1102 1.10 (macOS: installation of applications); mapped to 220-1202 1.8 (Installation and uninstallation of applications).

stem: In order to resize a partition on the internal storage drive of a computer running macOS, which tool should a technician utilize for this task?
explanation: To resize a partition on the internal storage drive of a computer running macOS, the technician should employ the Disk Utility tool. Disk Utility is a built-in utility in macOS that allows users to manage, format, and resize storage drives and partitions.
whyWrong: Activity Monitor shows processes and resource use; it does not resize partitions.
Time Machine is the macOS backup tool and cannot resize partitions.
Terminal is a command-line tool, and Disk Utility is the macOS tool meant for resizing partitions.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 39
note: 220-1102 1.10 (macOS: Disk Utility); mapped to 220-1202 1.8 (Disk Utility).

stem: A marketing team leader is helping a new starter get acquainted with their iMac desktop computer. Which graphical user interface (GUI) and file manager is typically set as the default in macOS for managing files and folders?
explanation: In macOS, the default GUI and file manager for organizing, searching, and accessing files and folders is Finder. It provides a user-friendly interface and various features to navigate through the filesystem, perform file operations, and manage the overall file hierarchy.
whyWrong: Disk Utility formats, partitions, and repairs disks; it is not the file manager.
The Dock gives quick access to applications and files, but it is not the file manager.
FileVault encrypts the startup disk; it is not a file manager.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 59
note: 220-1102 1.10 (macOS: Finder); mapped to 220-1202 1.8 (Features: Finder).

stem: In order to manually set an IP address on a computer running macOS, which of the following commands should a technician use?
explanation: To manually set an IP address on a computer running macOS, the technician should use the “ifconfig” command. The “ifconfig” command allows the configuration and management of network interfaces, including the assignment of IP addresses.
whyWrong: ipconfig is the Windows command for IP configuration and does not exist on macOS.
ARPA is a DNS domain used for reverse lookups, not a command that sets an IP address.
ping tests connectivity to another host and cannot configure an IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 80
note: 220-1102 1.10 (macOS: Terminal) and 1.11 (Linux: ifconfig); mapped to 220-1202 1.8 (Terminal). The 220-1202 objectives list ip for Linux, not ifconfig.

stem: Which of the following enables you to schedule maintenance tasks on macOS and Linux?
explanation: While systemd, launchd, and Task Scheduler can all schedule maintenance tasks, only cron is available on both macOS and Linux. A cron job runs a command at the times listed in a crontab file.
whyWrong: systemd can schedule tasks on Linux, but macOS does not use it.
launchd schedules tasks on macOS, but Linux does not use it.
Task Scheduler is the Windows scheduler, not a macOS or Linux tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 7
note: 220-1102 1.10/1.11; cron is not a listed 220-1202 topic, mapped to 220-1202 1.9 (OS components: systemd).

stem: Which of the following is an illegal character in a Linux filename?
explanation: Any of these characters are acceptable in a Linux filename except the forward slash (/), which is used exclusively as a path separator. Linux filenames are case-sensitive, and nearly any character except the slash is allowed.
whyWrong: The asterisk is allowed in a Linux filename, though it is awkward to use at the shell.
The dot is allowed in a Linux filename and starts hidden files.
The underscore is allowed in a Linux filename.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 1

stem: Which command do you use to determine what directory your prompt is focusing on in Linux?
explanation: The pwd command enables you to determine the current folder location in Linux. The name pwd stands for print working directory.
whyWrong: dir is the Windows command that lists directory contents; it does not show the current directory in Linux.
path shows or sets the search path in Windows, not the current directory.
prompt changes the Windows command prompt text; it is not a Linux command.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which of the following UNIX commands will show detailed information about the contents of a folder?
explanation: Type ls -l and press enter to see detailed information about a folder in UNIX systems. The long listing shows permissions, owner, group, size, and date for each item.
whyWrong: The -e option does not give the detailed long listing.
The -h option shows sizes in human-readable form only together with -l; it does not give the long listing.
The -k option does not give the detailed long listing.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Which UNIX command enables you to see a continually updating list of active processes?
explanation: top is the UNIX command that shows a continually updating list of active processes. Use ps for a snapshot of the processes at one moment.
whyWrong: ps shows a one-time snapshot of the processes; it does not keep updating the list.
zsh is a shell, not a command that lists processes.
kill ends a process; it does not list processes.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 15: Working with the Command-Line Interface, Chapter Review question 8
note: 220-1102 1.11; mapped to 220-1202 1.9 (informational: top, ps). Book answer A (ps) corrected: ps shows a one-time snapshot of the processes, and top is the command that shows a continually updating list.

stem: Within a Linux terminal, you want to see all the files on your system in long format (using the -l option), including any hidden files (which requires the -a option). Which command should you use?
explanation: The command ls -la will list all the files in a long format. The command ls -a | ls-l will not work. ls -s; ls -a will show two listings: one with the size and the other with all the files. The ls -a\ls -l command will show two listings—one with all the files and the other in a long format—but it will not show all the files in a long format.
whyWrong: Piping one ls command into another does not combine the options into one listing.
This runs two separate listings, one by size and one in long format, without hidden files in long format.
This produces two separate listings instead of one long listing with hidden files.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 1
note: Option labels (pipe, backslash) added so the options differ after punctuation is ignored.

stem: Which of the following Linux commands/utilities can be used to edit a file?
explanation: The nano command is used to edit files. The ps command lists processes running. The rm command removes files or directories. The ls command lists files and folders in the filesystem.
whyWrong: The ps command lists running processes; it cannot edit a file.
The rm command deletes files or directories; it cannot edit them.
The ls command lists files and folders; it cannot edit a file.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 4

stem: Which of the following Linux commands/utilities can be used to edit an Ethernet connection's configuration settings?
explanation: The ip command can be used to edit an Ethernet connection's configuration settings. The dd command is used to duplicate disks. The apt command is used with the APT package management system for downloading packages. The pwd command will show the current working directory.
whyWrong: The dd command copies disks and data blocks; it does not configure network interfaces.
The apt command manages software packages, not network settings.
The pwd command shows the current working directory; it does not configure networking.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 5

stem: The interpreter in Linux between the operating system and the user is known as the _______.
explanation: The shell is the interpreter in Linux between the operating system and the user. The translator is a wrong answer. Login is something you perform to access the shell. The graphical user interface (GUI) does not interpret commands and therefore is not considered an interpreter.
whyWrong: Translator is not the Linux name for the command interpreter.
Login is the step that gives access to the shell; it is not the interpreter.
A graphical user interface does not interpret typed commands, so it is not the shell.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which of the following utilities can be used in Linux to download patches for installation on a workstation?
explanation: The apt utility can be used to download and apply patches to a Linux installation. The update command is not a utility. Shell/terminal is an interface for interacting with the operating system with the command line. The patch command is not a utility.
whyWrong: Linux has no standard update utility for downloading patches; apt does this job.
The shell or terminal is the interface where commands run, not a patch download utility.
The book treats patch as not a utility for downloading updates; apt downloads and installs patches.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 9

stem: Which of the following commands can be used to change the owner of a file to a new owner in Linux?
explanation: The chown command is used to change ownership of a file. The cd command changes the working directory. The chmod command changes permissions on files. The pwd command displays the current working directory.
whyWrong: The cd command changes the working directory; it does not change file ownership.
The chmod command changes file permissions, not the owner.
The pwd command shows the current working directory; it does not change ownership.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which Linux utility can be used to check and repair disks?
explanation: The fsck Linux utility is used to check and repair disks. The chkdsk utility is a Windows utility used to check and repair disks. The du utility is used to show the current disk usage. dumgr is not a utility and is a wrong answer.
whyWrong: The chkdsk utility checks disks on Windows, not on Linux.
The du utility shows disk usage; it does not check or repair a disk.
There is no dumgr utility in Linux.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 11

stem: Which of the following is the most common shell used with Linux?
explanation: Bash is the most common command-line shell used with Linux. Tcl/Tk is a shell used with Linux, but it is very uncommon. Terminal is a utility used to access the command-line shell. SSH, or Secure Shell, is a secure protocol used to access the shell over a network.
whyWrong: Tcl/Tk can act as a shell on Linux, but it is rarely used for that.
Terminal is the program that gives access to a shell, not a shell itself.
SSH is a secure protocol for reaching a shell over a network, not a shell.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 13

stem: Which Linux command can be used to let you run a single command as another user?
explanation: The sudo command can be used to run a single command as another user. The su command allows you to change user logins at the command line. The passwd command changes the user's password. The ifconfig command allows you to view and modify the wired network interface.
whyWrong: The su command switches to another user's login for the session, not just one command.
The passwd command changes a user's password; it does not run commands as another user.
The ifconfig command views and changes network interfaces, not the user that runs a command.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 16

stem: Which of the following Linux commands will show you a list of running processes?
explanation: The ps command will display a snapshot of the current running processes on a Linux operating system. The ls command will display a listing of files from the working directory. The cat command will display the contents of a file. The su command allows you to change user logins at the command line.
whyWrong: The ls command lists files in a directory, not running processes.
The cat command shows the contents of a file, not running processes.
The su command switches users; it does not list processes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 17

stem: You are currently in a Linux terminal session and in the /home/testuser/documents/mail directory. Which command will take you to /home/testuser/documents?
explanation: The command cd .. will take you one level back from the current working directory. The command cd . will do nothing, because the period signifies the current working directory. The command cd . . . is not a valid command. The command cd ~ will change directories to the home directory of the user.
whyWrong: The single period means the current directory, so this command does not move you.
Three periods is not a valid directory reference, so this command does not work.
The tilde moves you to your home directory, not one level up.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 18
note: Option labels in parentheses added so the options differ after punctuation is ignored.

stem: If the permissions for a file are rwxrw-r--, what permissions apply for a user who is a member of the group to which the owner belongs?
explanation: The effective permissions are read and write. From left to right, the permissions are rwx for the user, rw- for the group, and r-- for everyone else. Since the user is only a member of the group applied to the file, they will have read and write permissions.
whyWrong: Read, write, and execute is the owner's set, rwx, not the group's set.
Read only is the set for everyone else, r--, not the group's set.
The group has read and write access, so no access is wrong.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 19

stem: What does the -p option with mkdir do?
options: Prompts the user before creating files
Prompts the user before creating subfolders
Creates subfolders as well as folders
explanation: The -p option on the mkdir command allows subfolders to be created as well as the target folder. All other answers are incorrect.
whyWrong: The -p option does not prompt the user; it creates folders without asking.
The -p option does not prompt before creating subfolders; it creates the whole path.
One of the listed options is correct, so None of the above is wrong.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux, Review Questions question 20

stem: Which command in Linux shows the contents of a directory?
explanation: ls will list the directory contents in Linux and macOS. It is similar to the dir command in Windows (which can also be used in Linux). pwd is used to display the full path of the working directory (for example, /home/root). cd is used to change directories; it is similar to the Windows command of the same name. mv is used to move files.
whyWrong: pwd prints the full path of the working directory; it does not list the directory contents.
cd changes the working directory; it does not list what the directory contains.
mv moves or renames files; it does not list the contents of a directory.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which command should be used to change the permissions of a file?
explanation: Use the chmod command to change permissions in Linux and macOS. ps displays information about a given process. chown changes ownership of a file. NTFS is the file system used by Windows that allows for file-level security assigned by a user or group.
whyWrong: ps shows information about running processes; it does not change file permissions.
chown changes who owns a file, not the read, write, and execute permissions on it.
NTFS is a Windows file system with its own permissions; it is not a Linux command.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You are working as a junior administrator at a midsized company. You are tasked with updating Linux system software. Which command should be used to gain the necessary permissions to update the software?
explanation: Use the sudo command before other commands that require administrative permissions. For example, you might type sudo apt upgrade to update the installed software.
whyWrong: grep searches text for a pattern; it does not give administrative permissions.
chmod changes the permissions on files; it does not run a command with administrative rights.
pwd prints the working directory path; it does not raise the user's permissions.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You are troubleshooting a network connectivity problem on a Linux computer. Which of the following commands will display information about the network interface?
explanation: Use the ip a command (short for ip address) to find information about the network interface. grep is a search and filtering tool. If used with the -i option, it ignores case distinctions (meaning uppercase and lowercase). sudo needs to be issued before any administrative commands. netsh (short for network shell) is actually a Windows command that you would run in PowerShell or the Command Prompt—tricky!
whyWrong: grep -i searches text for a pattern while ignoring case; it does not show network interfaces.
sudo runs a command with administrative rights; on its own it shows no network information.
netsh is a Windows command-line tool; it does not run on a Linux computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 5

stem:
One of your customers tells you that an application in Linux will not open and gives this error:

Only one instance of the program can be run at any time.

You log in to the system as root and open Terminal. Which of the following commands should you run to ensure that no other instances of the program are open?
explanation: Use the ps command to see what processes are running and the kill command to terminate the processes as necessary. cp is used to copy files, and rm is used to remove them. ls lists the contents of a directory, and chown changes ownership of files and directories. pwd shows the current path, and chmod changes permissions on files and directories. sudo is used before administrative commands, and nano opens the built-in text editor.
whyWrong: cp copies files and rm removes them; neither shows or stops running program instances.
ls lists directory contents and chown changes file ownership; neither finds running processes.
pwd shows the current path and chmod changes permissions; neither stops a running program.
sudo runs administrative commands and nano edits text; neither finds or ends the open instance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 6

stem:
An administrator logs in to a Linux computer and runs the following command:

ps -aux | grep firefox

Of the following, which BEST describes the functionality of this command?
options: It locates and lists the processes used to run the Firefox web browser.
It kills any running programs that start with the word firefox.
It opens directories that start with the word firefox.
It creates a new tab for filtering in Firefox.
explanation: The command will list the processes used by the Firefox web browser. To show this, you would need to have Firefox running when you type the command. The ps command reports a snapshot of the current running processes, and with -aux, it will see every single process. The pipe symbol (|) passes the output of ps to the grep command. The grep command filters the results of the ps command, asking the system to display only results that include the word firefox.
whyWrong: Ending programs needs the kill command; ps with grep only lists processes.
Opening a directory is done with cd; ps with grep lists processes, not directories.
New browser tabs are made inside the browser; this command only lists running processes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: Which command can be used to download updates and patches on a Linux workstation?
explanation: The apt command can be used to download and apply updates and patches to a Linux system. nano and vi are text editors that can be run from Terminal in Linux. fsck scans and repairs inconsistencies within a file system.
whyWrong: nano is a text editor run from the terminal; it does not download updates.
vi is a text editor run from the terminal; it does not download or apply patches.
fsck scans and repairs a file system; it does not download updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 8

stem: Which special user account wields absolute power over the entire system and is automatically created when you install Linux?
explanation: The root account in Linux is a special user account that wields absolute power over the entire system. It’s a superuser account that grants unrestricted access to all files, directories, and commands. A root account is automatically created when you install Linux. It is similar to a Windows Administrator account. However, unlike Windows, which defaults the primary user to an Administrator account, Linux also has you set up a standard user when installing.
whyWrong: Superuser describes what root is, but the account that Linux creates is named root.
Administrator is the Windows name for the built-in admin account, not the Linux account.
A standard user has limited rights and needs sudo for administrative tasks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 9

stem: Which Linux configuration file has restricted permissions and stores the actual encrypted user passwords?
explanation: /etc/shadow stores the actual encrypted user passwords (usually it’s actually password hashes). It has restricted permissions to protect sensitive data. Previously, /etc/passwd stored passwords, but now it usually only holds a placeholder designated as an x. Know the common Linux configuration files for the exam!
whyWrong: /etc/passwd holds basic account information such as user names and home folders; it now has only an x for the password.
/etc/hosts maps host names to IP addresses for local name resolution; it holds no passwords.
/etc/resolv.conf lists the DNS servers the system uses; it holds no user passwords.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 10

stem: Which of the following does the Linux kernel load that is considered a system and service manager for Linux operating systems and runs all the other initialization processes?
explanation: After kernel initialization completes, the kernel loads systemd, which is a system and service manager for Linux operating systems. systemd then runs all the other initialization processes. The bootloader in Linux is often called GRUB (or Grand Unified Bootloader) and is the first software that loads after the BIOS/UEFI boots and clears POST.
whyWrong: The bootloader, often GRUB, loads the kernel itself; it is not started by the kernel.
man opens the manual page for a command; it does not run the startup processes.
top shows running processes and their CPU and RAM use; it is not the service manager.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux, Cram Quiz question 11

stem: A technician has edited a configuration file in the nano editor and wants to save the changes and leave the editor. Which key sequence does this?
options: Press Ctrl+X, then press y to save the changes
explanation: In nano, Ctrl+X exits the editor, and nano then asks whether to save the modified file. Pressing y saves the changes to the file. The shortcut keys are listed at the bottom of the nano screen.
whyWrong: Esc followed by :wq saves and quits in vi or Vim, not in nano.
Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Q are common shortcuts in graphical editors, but nano exits with Ctrl+X.
Alt+F4 closes a graphical window and does not save a file in a terminal editor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux

stem: A Linux administrator uses the mount command to attach a new data partition at /data. After a reboot, the partition is no longer mounted. Which file should the administrator edit so the partition mounts at every boot?
explanation: The /etc/fstab file lists the file systems to mount at boot, with the device, mount point, file system type, and options for each. A partition mounted only with the mount command is not mounted again after a reboot unless it has an entry in this file.
whyWrong: /etc/resolv.conf lists the DNS servers that the system uses for name resolution.
/etc/hosts maps hostnames to IP addresses for local name resolution.
/etc/passwd stores basic user account information such as usernames, UIDs, and home directories.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 40: Linux

stem: A new Linux administrator signs in as root every day to do routine work, including web browsing and editing documents. What is the BEST recommendation?
options: Use a standard user account for daily work and run administrative commands with sudo
Keep using root but change its password every week
Give every user the root password so they can fix their own problems
Rename the root account so attackers cannot find it
explanation: The root account has unrestricted access to every file and command, so a mistake or compromise while signed in as root can damage the whole system. Following least privilege, daily work belongs in a standard account, and sudo runs individual administrative commands when needed.
whyWrong: Changing the password often does not reduce the risk of running everyday work with full system rights.
Sharing the root password gives everyone unrestricted access and breaks the principle of least privilege.
Renaming root does not reduce its privileges, so daily work would still run with full system rights.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 4: Working with macOS and Linux

stem: A technician is assisting the HR manager in protecting a number of sensitive files that had been saved in the HR documents folder. The technician is able to see the following output: -rw-r----- 1 mark HumanResources 0 Jan 9 14:37 Employee-Conduct -rw-r----- 1 mark HumanResources 0 Jan 9 14:37 Employee-Details -rw-r----- 1 mark HumanResources 0 Jan 9 14:36 Employee-Health -rw-r----- 1 mark Sales 0 Jan 9 14:37 Employee-Reports Which command did the technician use to view the output, and which command would BEST secure sensitive file(s)? (Choose two.)
explanation: To list files in a directory, the ls (list) command with the -l switch (for long listing) would be used to show all permissions for the contents of the directory. sudo + chown would allow the ownership of the Employee-Reports file to be changed from sales group ownership to the HumanResources group. Looking at the other permissions that have been allocated, it seems likely that the sales group has incorrectly been given group ownership of the file. sudo + chmod would reset permissions on a file or directory. pwd (present working directory) will show the directory where commands are currently being processed.
whyWrong: dir is a Windows command and does not produce this Linux long listing.
chmod 664 would give everyone read access and leave the Sales group as owner.
pwd shows the current directory; it does not list files or secure them.
Moving the file to a Sales folder does not change its group ownership or protect it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 1

stem: A technician must log into the Linux print server and restart the print service. What command-line syntax will they use if they want to make use of root privileges during the session?
explanation: Using the sudo command, a user can access the privileges of the superuser account. They will be prompted to type their own user password. It is also possible to switch user to an account that’s alive with the su command. pwd displays the present working directory. grep is used to search for text strings.
whyWrong: pwd shows the present working directory and does not grant root privileges.
grep searches text for patterns and does not grant root privileges.
Samba shares files with Windows computers and is not a privilege command.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 2

stem: A technician is investigating user complaints of latency when accessing applications on the Ubuntu Linux server. The technician reviews command output that refreshes in real time and lists each process with the columns PID, USER, PR, NI, VIRT, RES, %CPU, and %MEM. What command did the technician use to view this performance data?
explanation: The Linux top command shows real-time active processes. PID is the Process ID number, USER is the owner of the task, PR and NI show the priority of the task, and VIRT and RES show memory usage. Other important values are %CPU, which shows CPU usage, and %MEM, which shows the memory being used per process. nano is a text editor on Linux systems. ps is used to list running processes on a Linux system but does not display the details of resources being used to the same extent as the top command.
whyWrong: nano is a text editor and does not show process performance.
dig sends DNS queries and does not show process performance.
ps lists processes once and does not show live CPU and memory use like this.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 3

stem: What command can be used to delete a file or folder on a Linux operating system?
explanation: The rm command (also known as the remove command) is used to delete files and directories from a Linux system. The command supports additional switches, such as -r (recursive), that allow for directories to be deleted along with files. chmod allows for permissions on files and directories to be changed. man is used to display the manual for a command (for example man rm will display verbose information for the remove command). df is the disk-free command and displays filesystem information.
whyWrong: chmod changes the permissions of a file; it does not delete it.
man shows the manual page for a command; it does not delete files.
df shows free disk space on file systems; it does not delete files.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 4

stem:
A developer is worried that they may be running short of available disk space on their local system. They run a command at the prompt that results in the following output: Filesystem 1K-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted on /dev/sda1 263174212 230887666 32286546 87% /

What Linux command have they used?
explanation: The output from df shows the developer how much unused space remains on the storage location (hard disk). ps and top display the running processes. ip is used to configure settings for network interfaces. The Use% column shows that 87 percent of the root file system is already in use.
whyWrong: ps lists running processes, not disk space.
top shows live process activity, not disk space.
ip configures network interfaces, not disk space.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 5

stem: What is the purpose of the man command when it precedes a command-line interface (CLI) command in Linux?
options: It elevates the users’ privileges so they can perform administrative tasks
It automatically assigns the manager privilege to the command
It displays help in the form of a manual
It enters maintenance mode for the command
explanation: The man command displays help in the form of a manual, usually offering much more detail than the corresponding --help command when typed after the CLI command. The other explanations are false.
whyWrong: sudo, not man, runs a command with elevated privileges.
There is no manager privilege in Linux that man assigns.
man has no maintenance mode; it only displays documentation.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 7

stem: Which command allows an administrator to download and install new application packages on a Red Hat Linux workstation?
explanation: A package management system allows for the installation, update, and removal of software packages. There are two common package management systems supported on Linux operating systems. Red Hat Linux supports yum. Ubuntu Linux uses a packager named apt. The remaining CLI tools are not used to install applications.
whyWrong: grep searches text for patterns and does not install packages.
ps lists running processes and does not install packages.
dig queries DNS servers and does not install packages.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 9
note: 220-1102 1.11; mapped to 220-1202 1.9 (package management). 220-1202 names dnf, the successor of yum on Red Hat systems.

stem: The Human Resources manager is searching the HR folder for a file called Employee-Details. Once found, they need to search the file for information regarding Joe Smith. What TWO commands were used to generate the following output? -rw-r--r-- 1 mark HumanResources 263 Jan 9 18:24 Employee-Details Joe Smith 6 Beacon Drive, Edinburgh EH1 4DL 0131 789765
explanation: The first command, ls -l, will display the “long” listing for the Employee-Details file. The grep command searches for patterns in any line of text. Therefore, the second command will display any lines that have the pattern Joe Smith within the Employee-Details file. dir /L is a Windows command (although many Linux distributions do support a number of native Windows commands). The Linux cat (concatenate) command cannot be used to search for a pattern of characters but could be used to display the contents of the Employee-Details file.
whyWrong: dir /L is a Windows command and is not supported on a Linux command line.
cat displays a file's contents but cannot search it for a pattern.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 10

stem:
A technician is troubleshooting a networking issue on an Ubuntu Linux workstation. The technician issues commands in the terminal window, resulting in the following output: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP group default qlen 1000 link/ether 00:15:5d:30:49:57 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff inet 172.22.64.215/20 brd 172.22.79.255 scope global eth0 inet6 fe80::215:5dff:fe30:4957/64 scope link ANSWER SECTION: www.google.com. 0 IN A 142.250.114.104 www.google.com. 0 IN A 142.250.114.106 www.google.com. 0 IN A 142.250.114.99 www.google.com. 0 IN A 142.250.114.147 www.google.com. 0 IN A 142.250.114.103 www.google.com. 0 IN A 142.250.114.105 ;; Query time: 130 msec

What TWO Linux network commands were used to generate the output?
explanation: The Linux ip (Internet Protocol) command queries a network object. ip route will show the computer’s default gateway, and in this case, ip address will show the configuration settings for all network interfaces. The second command, dig (Domain Internet Groper), is used to retrieve records from DNS servers. dig www.google.com was used to display the records for IP addresses registered against the domain name www.google.com. ipconfig, nslookup, and tracert are networking commands supported only on Windows operating systems (not Linux).
whyWrong: ipconfig is a Windows command; Linux uses ip to show interface settings.
nslookup output does not have the ANSWER SECTION and query time shown here, which come from dig.
tracert is a Windows command that lists the hops to a host.
ping tests reachability and shows replies, not interface settings or DNS records.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 11

stem: A developer raises a support ticket as they cannot access a file shared from a colleague’s Red Hat Linux workstation. What command would be BEST to assign permissions for the file?
explanation: The chmod (change and modify) command allows the permissions to be reset. grep is used to search for patterns in lines of text. ip address displays the network configuration. pwd displays the current directory where commands are being run. For example, chmod 644 gives the owner read and write access and gives everyone else read access.
whyWrong: grep searches text for patterns and does not change permissions.
ip address shows network settings and does not change file permissions.
pwd shows the current directory and does not change permissions.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.11 question 12

stem: Which of the following commands should be used to search for a specific string in a filename?
explanation: grep is the Linux command used to search for matching information in a file, files, or filename. It prints the lines or names that match the string or pattern you give it.
whyWrong: sudo runs a command as another user, such as root; it does not search for a string.
chmod changes the permissions of a file or folder; it does not search for text.
wget downloads content from web servers; it does not search files for a string.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 49

stem: Which of the following tools is used to type recovery commands into a Linux box?
explanation: The most common Linux shell program is the Terminal utility, which uses the Bash shell by default on most Linux distros. (This is also available in macOS.) This utility allows the user to enter commands of all types—including recovery commands—to be executed by Linux.
whyWrong: Backup programs such as Time Machine do not accept typed recovery commands; they need no text interface.
Restore and snapshot tools return a system to a saved state, but you cannot type commands into them.
CMD is the Windows Command Prompt, not the command-line tool of a Linux system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 66

stem: When the “cat ssh_config” command is executed on a Linux terminal, which of the following outcomes should be anticipated?
options: The original “ssh_config” file will be replaced with a new blank document
The contents of the “ssh_config” file will be displayed
The lines of text in the “ssh_config” file will be sorted in alphabetical order
The contents of the “ssh_config” file will be copied to another file named “ ssh_config”
explanation: When the “cat” command is used in a Linux terminal with a filename such as “ssh_config,” it displays the content of that file on the terminal. It does not modify the file or create a new file.
whyWrong: cat only reads the file, so it does not replace it with a blank document.
cat prints the lines in their stored order; sorting text is the job of the sort command.
cat on its own prints to the screen and does not copy the file to another file.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 11
note: 220-1102 1.11 (Linux commands); mapped to 220-1202 1.9 (Informational: cat). The book's explanation named the file comptia.txt; changed to ssh_config to match the stem.

stem: Which of the following is the utility used to download apps in Windows?
explanation: Microsoft Store is used to download apps in Windows. The Store is one of the distribution methods for applications, next to downloadable packages and physical media.
whyWrong: Play Store is the app store for Android devices, not for Windows.
Spaces is a macOS feature for multiple desktops; there is no Apple Spaces app store for Windows.
Windows Store was the older name; the current Windows utility is called Microsoft Store.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 2
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (distribution methods).

stem: 32-bit programs are installed into which folder by default in a 64-bit edition of Windows?
explanation: By default, 32-bit applications install into the C:\Program Files (x86) folder. Keeping 32-bit and 64-bit programs in separate folders lets Windows load the correct libraries for each.
whyWrong: C:\Program Files is the default folder for 64-bit programs on a 64-bit edition of Windows.
Windows does not use a Program Files (x32) folder.
Windows does not use a Program Files\Wins\Old folder for 32-bit programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 2: The Visible Computer, Chapter Review question 6
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (32-bit vs. 64-bit dependent application requirements).

stem: Jack downloaded a video shared by a friend, ourfamilyholiday.avi. When he opens it in his media player software, he hears sound but gets no picture. What’s the MOST LIKELY problem and solution?
options: His media player software doesn’t support AVI files. He needs to install a new media player.
His computer is a Mac; he needs to play the file on a Windows system.
His computer lacks the proper video codec. He needs to update the codecs installed on his computer.
The video is corrupt. His friend needs to share it with him again.
explanation: Most likely, Jack’s system lacks the video codec needed for the video portion of the file. He needs to update the codecs on his machine.
whyWrong: The sound plays, so the player opens the AVI file; a new player is not needed.
Macs can play AVI files with the right codec, so changing to Windows is not the fix.
A corrupt file would usually fail to open or show errors, while sound playing points to a missing codec.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 10
note: 220-1101 (multimedia, codecs); codecs are not named in 220-1202; mapped to 1.10 (system requirements for applications).

stem: Which of the following installation methods would you use if you wanted to install a program on a virtual machine? (Choose the BEST method.)
explanation: If you wanted to install a program on a virtual machine, the preferred method would be to mount an ISO image of the application. USB and optical discs are not common installation methods for virtual machines. Although ZIP files could be used, a ZIP file is only a compression method and not a delivery method.
whyWrong: A virtual machine has no physical USB drive by default, so a USB installer is an awkward choice.
Optical discs are rarely used with virtual machines because an ISO image does the same job without media.
A ZIP file only compresses files; it is not a delivery method that a virtual machine can mount.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 4

stem: Which of the following are important considerations when planning the installation of a new application? (Select the three BEST answers.)
explanation: When installing a new application, you should consider the CPU speed (and other minimum/recommended hardware requirements), the Program Files location (64-bit or 32-bit), and user permissions. The Windows location isn’t really important; by default, it will be C:\Windows, but its location doesn’t really impact the installation of the application. The warranty (if there is one) can be important if there is a failure, but it doesn’t play into the installation of the software.
whyWrong: The Windows folder location is usually C:\Windows and does not affect how a new application installs.
A warranty matters if something fails later, but it plays no part in installing the software.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 41: Application Installation and Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: What is the name of the folder where Windows stores 64-bit system files?
explanation: System32 is the folder that Windows uses to store 64-bit system files. SysWOW64 is actually the location of 32-bit system files. Program Files (x86) is the place where 32-bit versions of programs are stored.
whyWrong: Systemroot is a variable for the main Windows folder, usually C:\Windows, not the 64-bit system file folder.
SysWOW64 holds the 32-bit system files on 64-bit Windows, not the 64-bit files.
Program Files (x86) holds 32-bit programs, not Windows 64-bit system files.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 41: Application Installation and Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 2

stem:
One of the users at your company attempts to install an application and receives the following error:

Not enough disk space to install...

Which of the following was overlooked by the user?
explanation: The user did not pay attention to the minimum system requirements. Perhaps the application needed 10 GB of storage drive space, and only 8 GB were left on the partition. (Close is not good enough!) It appears that the installation started well enough, so the OS should be compatible, and the installation method is most likely correct. As long as the user has rights to run executable files, which is likely, there shouldn’t be any file permissions issues.
whyWrong: The installer started and ran, so the operating system is compatible with the application.
The installer ran normally, so the installation method was not the problem.
The user could run the installer, so file permissions did not block it; free space did.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 41: Application Installation and Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 3

stem:
A customer submits a request for a technician to install a new application on a computer. The computer has the following specifications: quad-core x86-64 processor, 64-bit operating system, 16 GB of RAM, a 1 TB drive with 900 GB used, and a 1000 Mbps network connection.

The new application has the following minimum requirements: quad-core processor, 64-bit operating system, 8 GB of RAM, 120 GB of free space, and 1 Gbps network connection.

Which of the following will result when the technician installs the software?
explanation: The system has insufficient storage space. If the system has a 1 TB drive that has 900 GB used, that leaves 100 GB free, which is not enough for an application that requires 120 GB. The technician would first have to free up space by going to Settings > Apps > Apps & features and removing some unused applications. There is plenty of RAM on the system, and the network connection is fine (1000 Mbps is the same as 1 Gbps). The system architecture should be adequate: The software requires a 64-bit system, and the x86-64 CPU is 64-bit.
whyWrong: The computer has 16 GB of RAM, which is more than the 8 GB the application needs.
The 1000 Mbps network connection is the same as the 1 Gbps the application needs.
A quad-core x86-64 CPU from Intel or AMD is common and meets the processor requirement.
The x86-64 processor and OS are 64-bit, which matches the 64-bit requirement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 41: Application Installation and Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 4
note: The book's specification table was missing from the text; the computer's specifications were rebuilt from the book's answer explanation (the RAM amount, 16 GB, is assumed: the book says only that there is plenty).

stem: A technician is supporting a customer who has a Windows 10 x86 computer with 4GB of RAM. The customer needs to increase the available memory to 16GB RAM in order to install an engineering application. What should the technician recommend to the customer in order to meet this requirement?
explanation: The x86 architecture describes a processor that has 32 registers. This architecture means that a maximum of 4GB of RAM can be accessed by the system.
