To access any additional RAM purchased would require the system to be upgraded to an x64-bit architecture. Installing Ubuntu Linux will not affect the amount of memory that can be accessed. Installing a larger hard drive will not help, and the addition of more RAM on the existing x86 architecture will not be effective.
whyWrong: Changing to Ubuntu does not remove the 4GB limit of a 32-bit system.
A larger SSD adds storage space, not addressable memory.
A 32-bit system cannot address more than 4GB, so added RAM would go unused.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.7 question 1
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (application installation)

stem:
Several members of the engineering design team have raised service tickets due to latency issues and poor performance when using a Computer-Aided Design (CAD) application. A hardware scan of the workstations reveals the following: - 64GB DDR4 Memory - 2GB Integrated Graphics - 1TB SSD HDD - Intel XEON 3.4GHZ 16-Core CPU

What change can the engineers make that would be most beneficial when using the CAD application?
explanation: While the exact requirements of the CAD application are unknown and the base hardware seems reasonably sufficient, the exception to this is the graphics card. CAD applications place heavy demands on the graphics hardware and will benefit from dedicated hardware comprising a multi-core Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) and dedicated video RAM. As the existing hardware is of a high standard, there is no obvious requirement to upgrade anything but the integrated graphics.
whyWrong: The workstations already have 64GB of RAM, which is plenty for CAD work.
A 16-core 3.4GHz Xeon is already a strong CPU for this workload.
A 1TB SSD is already fast storage, so faster drives would add little.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.7 question 2
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (application installation)

stem: A marketing team is using a Customer Relationship Manager (CRM) system on their 32-bit Windows 8.1 workstations. After upgrading the workstations to Windows 11 64-bit edition, the team wants to use the same CRM application. Which of the following restrictions will they encounter when using a 32-bit application on a 64-bit OS?
options: 32-bit applications will be restricted to 32GB of RAM
32-bit applications will be restricted to 4GB of RAM
explanation: 32-bit applications are able to run on 64-bit Windows using a compatibility setting provided by the Windows on Windows (WOW) architecture. They will run in a similar fashion as they would on a native 32-bit host, with the same memory restrictions (4 GB RAM at most). Apart from the memory restrictions, all other functionalities will still be supported, including multi-tasking and multi-threading.
whyWrong: A 32-bit application is limited to 4GB of RAM, not 32GB.
32-bit applications can still use multiple threads on a 64-bit OS.
32-bit applications run alongside other programs, so multitasking still works.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.7 question 3
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (application installation)

stem: Following the upgrade of a customer’s Windows 8 operating system to Windows 10, an application now fails to launch. An error message is displayed, stating that the application was written for Windows 8 and is incompatible with the current operating system. What can a support technician offer as a quick fix for this problem?
options: Contact the application vendor to investigate whether an updated version can be purchased
Set the application compatibility setting to Windows 8
Boot Windows into safe mode to run the application
Set the application compatibility setting to Windows 7
explanation: In some cases, an application makes a call to the operating system to get the current version and checks to see if that matches its requirements. Often, the application fails simply because the value is not the same as its requirements when the application is told that the OS is Windows 10, but it expected Windows 8. A quick fix is to try and trick the application into believing it is running on Windows 8 by selecting that as the compatibility setting. Updating the application to the latest version may be a long-term option, but it doesn’t offer a quick fix. Safe mode is used to troubleshoot faulting drivers and services but is unlikely to offer a solution to the technician’s current problem.
whyWrong: Buying an updated version may solve it later, but it is not a quick fix.
Safe mode is for troubleshooting drivers and services, not for running incompatible applications.
The application expects Windows 8, so a Windows 7 compatibility setting is the wrong match.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.7 question 4
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (application to OS compatibility)

stem: A software development company has designed a Computer-Aided Design (CAD) application at great expense. They need a control to ensure that each copy of the application will only run from a licensed workstation. What would be the MOST effective way to protect the application from theft?
options: Make each customer agree to strict licensing requirements during installation
Deploy an external hardware token for each copy of the application
Make each customer sign an Acceptable Use Policy (AUP)
Only sell the application to trustworthy customers
explanation: A hardware token can store a unique key that is used to authorize the launch of the CAD software. Where the value of a single license may run into several thousand dollars, this is an effective way to ensure the software is not fraudulently used. None of the other options fully protect the developers from unscrupulous users.
whyWrong: A license agreement is only a promise and does not technically stop copying.
An acceptable use policy sets rules for users but does not stop the software from running elsewhere.
Choosing trustworthy customers is not a technical control and cannot be enforced.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 7: Operating Systems, Objective 1.7 question 5
note: 220-1102 1.7; mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (application installation)

stem: You attempt to install a legacy application on a computer running Windows. You receive an error that says the application cannot be installed because the OS is not supported. Which of the following describes the FIRST step you should take to continue installing the application?
options: Purchase the latest version of the application.
Install the application in Safe Mode.
Install the application in compatibility mode.
explanation: Attempt to install legacy (older) applications in compatibility mode. Select the older OS that the application was originally written for.
whyWrong: Buying a new version is not needed as a first step, because compatibility mode can let the old version install.
Safe Mode is for troubleshooting the system; it does not make an unsupported OS acceptable to the installer.
Security updates do not change which OS versions the legacy installer accepts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 44

stem: You are installing an older 32-bit program on a 64-bit version of Windows. Where does the program get installed to?
explanation: The program would be installed to C:\Program Files (x86). This is the default folder for 32-bit programs when installed to a 64-bit version of Windows.
whyWrong: C:\ is the root of the drive, and programs are installed to folders under it, not to the root itself.
C:\Program Files is the default folder for 64-bit programs on a 64-bit version of Windows.
C:\Windows holds the operating system files, not installed 32-bit programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 57

stem: An engineering firm is considering implementing the latest version of its computer-aided design (CAD) software, which includes a feature requiring backups of all CAD files to be stored externally in the software vendor’s data center. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY to raise concerns for the IT manager?
options: Comprehensive compatibility testing with all system types and accessories must be conducted for the updated software
Adequate budget allocation for additional staff hours during the installation of updates needs to be ensured
Network utilization is expected to significantly increase due to the larger size of CAD files being backed up
The local hard drives may become overloaded due to the size of the update and installation files
explanation: The IT manager is likely to have concerns about the significant increase in network utilization caused by the larger size of CAD files being backed up to the software’s cloud server. This increase in data transfer can put a strain on the network bandwidth and potentially affect the overall network performance.
whyWrong: Compatibility testing matters for any update, but it is not tied to storing the backups in the vendor's data center.
Staff hours for installing updates are a normal cost and are not the main concern raised by off-site backups.
The off-site backup feature moves data off the local drives, so local storage is not the main concern.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 26
note: 220-1102 1.7 (application installation: impact considerations); mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (Impact considerations: network).

stem: A research scientist needs access to a specialist application that is only supported on a Linux OS. The scientist currently only has access to a Windows OS. The scientist needs to work in a remote laboratory with no access to external networks during the day. What offers the BEST solution for the scientist to access the specialist application?
options: Pay for a remote desktop utilizing a Linux OS
Install the Linux application within the supported Windows Linux subsystem
Install Linux as the primary OS and purchase a second computer to handle the Windows application
Enable the Windows Hyper-V client and install the Linux OS and the Linux application
explanation: The most efficient solution in this scenario would be setting up a virtual machine within the Windows OS to run Linux and the required application. This allows Windows and Linux applications to be run at the same time. Hyper-V runs the virtual machine locally, so it needs no connection to external networks.
whyWrong: A remote Linux desktop needs a network connection, which the laboratory does not have during the day.
The Windows Subsystem for Linux may not support every Linux application, especially graphical ones, as well as a full Linux install.
Running two computers works but adds needless cost when one computer can run Linux in a virtual machine.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 32
note: 220-1102 1.7 (application to OS compatibility) and Core 1 4.1 (virtualization); mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (System requirements: application to OS compatibility).

stem: A departmental manager is proposing to upgrade the design team’s workstations with 32 GB of RAM. The plan is also to upgrade the OS from 32-bit to 64-bit. What will be the major benefit of the move to a 64-bit OS?
options: A 64-bit OS can utilize more RAM efficiently, allowing applications to access larger amounts of memory
A 64-bit OS provides faster processing speeds than a 32-bit OS
A 64-bit OS improves graphics performance and rendering capabilities
A 64-bit OS enhances network connectivity and data transfer rates
explanation: This is the correct answer because one of the major benefits of moving to a 64-bit OS is the ability to access and utilize larger amounts of random access memory (RAM) than a 32-bit OS. This is particularly important for tasks such as video editing, 3D rendering, and other memory-intensive applications.
whyWrong: A 64-bit OS can speed up some tasks, but its major benefit is addressing more RAM, not faster processing.
Graphics may benefit indirectly, but the main gain of a 64-bit OS is access to more memory.
A 64-bit OS does not change network connectivity or transfer rates, which depend on the network hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 36
note: 220-1102 1.7 (32-bit vs. 64-bit requirements); mapped to 220-1202 1.10 (System requirements: 32-bit vs. 64-bit).

stem: A graphic designer's PC has integrated graphics that share system RAM. A new 3D rendering program lists a minimum of 4 GB of VRAM and hardware acceleration. The CPU, RAM, and storage meet the requirements. What should the technician do BEST to meet the requirement?
options: Install a dedicated PCIe graphics card with at least 4 GB of VRAM
Add more system RAM so the integrated graphics can borrow it
Install the 32-bit version of the rendering program
Mount the program's ISO image instead of using the download
explanation: VRAM is memory on the graphics card itself, and a dedicated card in a PCIe slot provides it. Integrated graphics share slower system RAM and usually cannot meet a VRAM requirement or give strong hardware acceleration.
whyWrong: Integrated graphics still share system memory, so more RAM does not give the dedicated VRAM the program needs.
A 32-bit build does not change graphics needs and would run worse on a 64-bit system.
The installation method does not change the hardware requirements of the program.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 41: Application Installation and Configuration Concepts

stem: A school must set up 60 new computers for a lab. Every computer needs the same Windows build, the same office suite, and the same settings, and the computers hold no user data yet. Which method is the BEST choice?
options: Deploy one prepared system image to all the computers
Install the suite on each computer from the vendor's DVD
Have each student download the suite on first sign-in
Mount the suite's ISO file on each computer one by one
explanation: When many computers need the same OS and software, a prepared image is the fastest and most consistent method. The reference computer is generalized with sysprep and the image is then deployed to every computer.
whyWrong: Installing from optical media one PC at a time is slow and does not scale to 60 computers.
Student downloads would be slow, inconsistent, and need rights that students should not have.
Mounting an ISO on each PC still means 60 separate installs and does not copy the settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

stem: A company plans to install a new multiuser customer database app on all 200 office PCs. Nobody in the company has used it before, and the vendor offers an evaluation version. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Test the evaluation version on an isolated test network or virtual machines
Push the app to all 200 PCs over the weekend
Turn off the firewall on every PC so the app can connect
Remove all other apps from the PCs to avoid conflicts
explanation: Every new app increases the attack surface and may open ports or conflict with other software. Testing it first on an isolated testbed shows these problems before they affect live PCs and the business.
whyWrong: Pushing an untested app to every PC risks outages and security problems across the whole company.
Turning off the firewall weakens security for every PC and is never a first step.
Removing other apps would disrupt work; testing shows whether there is a conflict at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 41: Application Installation and Configuration Concepts

stem: Which of the following are true about Google Workspace? (Select all that apply)
options: It is a subscription service with a 14-day free trial
There is at least 30 GB of storage per user
You need a live.com email to access it
explanation: Following a 14-day free trial, a Google Workspace subscription starts at $5.75 per user and allows access to many applications, at least 30 GB of storage, and video meetings with up to 100 users. Google Drive is the storage service included in the subscription. You cannot create virtual machines, and a live.com email address is for Microsoft products.
whyWrong: Google Workspace is a productivity suite; virtual machines are created in a cloud platform such as Google Cloud.
A live.com address is a Microsoft account; Google Workspace uses Google accounts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.4 question 21
note: 220-1101 1.4 (mobile device application support); mapped to 220-1202 1.11 (cloud-based productivity tools).

stem: Which application will sync your files to the cloud?
explanation: OneDrive is a cloud-based file synchronization application; it is similar to Google Drive. Excel is a spreadsheet application that is part of the Microsoft 365 suite of products. Microsoft Exchange is an on-premises email server; its cloud-based counterpart is Microsoft Exchange Online, and it is similar to Google Gmail. Outlook is the email client used with Microsoft Exchange.
whyWrong: Excel is a spreadsheet application; it does not synchronize files to cloud storage.
Exchange is an email server product, not a file synchronization client.
Outlook is an email and calendar client; it does not sync your files to the cloud.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 1: Operating System Basics, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of these represent reasons to move to an online email system? (Select all that apply.)
options: Online email is faster than local email.
Configuration is done for you, which reduces errors.
Local email is always deleted immediately from the Internet.
Email is available anytime, anywhere you have Internet access.
explanation: Configuration is done for the end user, which eliminates errors with entry of specific server addresses. Email is available to users wherever and whenever they have Internet access. It is not necessarily any faster; they view their email in a web browser. While local email could be deleted upon downloading, this is no longer a common occurrence.
whyWrong: Online email is not necessarily faster; users often just read it in a web browser.
Local email is not always deleted from the server; deleting it on download is no longer common.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Storing data online gives which of the following advantages? (Select all that apply.)
options: Storing online will protect your email
explanation: You have access to your files anywhere, at any time. Your cloud provider will back up the files automatically within its system, so if a disaster were to hit, your files should be protected. You can share your files with whomever you choose, and if you have a provider who allows this, you can also collaborate on editing these documents. Spell check is available without going online, and online storage and email, while both online, are unrelated.
whyWrong: Spell check works without going online, so it is not an advantage of online storage.
Online storage and online email are separate services; storing files online does not protect email.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Documents shared online through SaaS such as Microsoft 365 or Google Docs have which of the following characteristics? (Select all that apply.)
options: Collaboration with other users in real time is practical.
Files are stored locally on individual machines.
Files cannot be backed up easily.
explanation: Files created with SaaS tools such as Microsoft 365 and Google Docs are, by default, stored online, which means that users can collaborate easily with one another, sharing the documents and even working on the documents together in real time. The files can be accessed anywhere you have Internet access, at any time of day or night. They are not generally stored on individual machines (that can be done, but it takes additional steps), and backups are automatic because the files are already online.
whyWrong: SaaS documents are stored online by default; keeping them on individual machines takes extra steps.
SaaS files are already online, so backups are automatic and easy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Instant messaging tools can be used to communicate in which of the following ways? (Select all that apply.)
options: Create short messages sent as text messages
Create short messages that need no reply
Create short messages for more informal communication
Create short messages for more conversational communication
explanation: Instant messaging tools are used for more informal communication and can work in a more conversational manner than the more formal email format (hard to believe we’re referring to email as formal!). While some can be configured to send the messages to mobile phones as text messages, this approach is uncommon.
whyWrong: Some tools can send messages to phones as texts, but that is an uncommon way to use instant messaging.
Instant messages are conversational and usually expect a reply, so needing no reply is not the point.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Videoconferencing tools allow for what type of team? (Select all that apply.)
options: Specialized hardware is required for the team
explanation: Although the teams can be fully remote, even in different countries from one another, the key component is the remoteness from one another, either geographically or physically. With the advent of cheap videoconferencing, teams can keep in touch while not being in the same physical location. This capability allows for better collaboration and better work-life balance.
whyWrong: Teams in different countries can use it too, but the book's key is remote and multi-office teams.
Cheap videoconferencing works on ordinary computers and phones, so specialized hardware is not needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools, Cram Quiz question 5
note: The book's explanation says teams can be in different countries, yet its key leaves out option C; the key is kept.

stem: A company with an on-premises Active Directory domain is moving to Microsoft 365. Administrators want every user created in Active Directory to get a matching cloud identity automatically, so users sign in to Microsoft 365 with the same credentials. What is the BEST solution?
options: Synchronize Active Directory to Entra ID with Entra Connect Sync or Entra Cloud Sync
Create a second account for each user manually in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Assign each user a Microsoft 365 E3 license
Join every workstation to a workgroup
explanation: Identity synchronization copies users and groups from on-premises Active Directory to Entra ID, which creates a hybrid identity. Entra Connect Sync and Entra Cloud Sync both do this, and both support password writeback. Users then use one set of credentials, and administrators enter account information in only one system.
whyWrong: Creating accounts by hand doubles the work and gives users separate credentials to remember.
A license grants access to Microsoft 365 services but does not create or synchronize identities.
A workgroup removes central management and has nothing to do with cloud identities.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

stem: An organization hires many seasonal staff, and administrators want each new user to receive a Microsoft 365 license as soon as the account is added to the Sales group. What is the BEST way to set this up?
options: Use group-based licensing to assign the license to the Sales group
Assign the license to each new user by hand in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Buy a node-locked license for each workstation
Install a USB hardware license token on each computer
explanation: With group-based licensing, an administrator assigns a license to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center or through Entra ID. Any user added to that group receives the license automatically, and removing the user from the group frees the license for someone else.
whyWrong: Assigning licenses by hand works, but it is slow and easy to forget when many users join.
Node-locked licenses tie software to one machine, but Microsoft 365 licenses are assigned to users.
A hardware token licenses software on one computer, which does not fit per-user cloud licensing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

stem: You are configuring a friend’s iPad. This friend needs to access their work email. To provide this access, you require information from the IT department. Which information should you ask for?
explanation: To enable the iPad access to this email account, you’ll need the type of server that handles email (be it SMTP, POP3, IMAP, or an Exchange server) and the domain name that the server resides on. Often, this will be the same domain name as the email address, but not always. An example of an SMTP mail server might be mail.example.com.
whyWrong: The gateway is needed to reach the Internet, not to set up an email account, so it is not what IT must supply.
The email app resolves the server name to an IP address itself, so an IP address is not needed.
The email app resolves the server name itself, and DNS is a network setting, not email account information.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 61

stem: You are setting up a new email account for a user in Microsoft Outlook. Which protocol should you use if you want the email to be accessible from multiple devices and keep emails synchronized across them?
explanation: IMAP is designed for accessing emails from multiple devices while keeping them synchronized. It’s the preferred choice for this scenario.
whyWrong: POP3 downloads messages to one device and does not keep them synchronized across devices.
SMTP is used to send email, not to receive and synchronize it.
HTTP is used for web browsing, not for email access in an email client such as Outlook.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 87
note: 220-1102 Core 1 2.1 (email ports and protocols); mapped to 220-1202 1.11 (Email systems).

stem: A consultant's laptop has a 128 GB drive, but her OneDrive library holds 300 GB of project files. She wants every file to show in File Explorer but opens only a few each day. Which setting BEST meets this need?
options: A mapped network drive to the office file server
Syncing every OneDrive folder to the local drive
explanation: Files On-Demand shows cloud files as placeholders and downloads a file only when it is opened. Every file still appears in File Explorer, but the small drive does not fill up.
whyWrong: Cached Exchange Mode keeps a local copy of a mailbox, not of OneDrive files.
A mapped drive reaches a file server share, not the user's cloud library.
Syncing every folder would need 300 GB of local space, more than the drive holds.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 1: Operating System Basics

stem: A company with an on-premises Active Directory domain is moving to Microsoft 365. The administrators want users to sign in to the cloud apps with their existing domain user names and passwords and to create each account only once. What is the BEST solution?
options: Synchronize the Active Directory accounts to Entra ID
Create a new cloud account for each user by hand
Assign each user a Microsoft 365 license
Map a network drive for each user to OneDrive
explanation: Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync copies users and groups from Active Directory to Entra ID. This gives each user a hybrid identity with the same sign-in, and accounts are created only once.
whyWrong: Separate cloud accounts would mean a second user name and password and twice the account work.
A license gives an account the right to use the apps, but it does not link the account to the domain.
A mapped drive gives a share a drive letter and does nothing for sign-in.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools

stem: A small business uses every one of its 25 Microsoft 365 licenses. A new employee starts on Monday, and an employee who left last month still has a licensed account. The owner does not want to buy more licenses. What should the administrator do BEST?
options: Remove the license from the former employee and assign it to the new employee
Let the new employee sign in with the former employee's account
Give the new employee the web apps without a license
Synchronize the new employee's account to Entra ID
explanation: Licenses are assigned to user accounts in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Removing the license from an account that is no longer used frees it for the new employee without buying more.
whyWrong: Sharing a former employee's account breaks accountability and is a security risk.
The Microsoft 365 apps, including the web apps, need a license assigned to the account.
Synchronization creates or links the account, but it does not give the account a license.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 42: Cloud-Based Productivity Tools
